rustamid-imamate.t: An Ibadi imamate ruled from Tahert in Algeria, known for learning, trade and religious tolerance in the early Islamic Maghreb.
rustamid-imamate.o: [[e:abd-al-rahman-ibn-rustam|Abd al-Rahman ibn Rustam]], of Persian descent, had governed [[e:kairouan|Kairouan]] for the [[s:ibadi-imamate-of-tripolitania|Ibadi Imamate of Tripolitania]]. After its defeat in 761 he fled west and founded the city of [[e:tiaret|Tahert]] (near modern Tiaret), where around 777 the Ibadi community elected him [[e:imam|imam]].
rustamid-imamate.r: In theory the [[e:imamate|imamate]] was elective, but in practice the Rustamids ruled hereditarily, advised by religious scholars. [[e:tiaret|Tahert]] attracted merchants from [[e:kairouan|Kairouan]], [[e:basra|Basra]] and [[e:persia|Persia]], and its scholars debated theology freely. The state relied on [[e:berbers|Berber]] tribes and Ibadi communities as far as the [[e:nafusa-mountains|Jebel Nafusa]] and [[s:sultanate-of-ouargla|Ouargla]], and profited from caravan trade to the [[e:sahara|Sahara]]. [[e:aflah-ibn-abd-al-wahhab|Aflah ibn Abd al-Wahhab]] ruled for about fifty years.
rustamid-imamate.e: In 909 [[e:abu-abdallah-al-shii|Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i]], leading the [[e:kutama-berbers|Kutama]] armies of the Fatimid movement, captured [[e:tiaret|Tahert]]. The surviving [[e:ibadism|Ibadis]] fled to [[s:sultanate-of-ouargla|Ouargla]] and [[e:sedrata|Sedrata]], and later to the Mzab, where the [[s:mzab-confederation|Mzab confederation]] preserved their tradition.

republic-of-colombia.t: The centralised Colombian republic founded by the constitution of 1886, which lost Panama, endured decades of internal conflict and made peace with the FARC in 2016.
republic-of-colombia.o: After the Liberal federation of the [[s:united-states-of-colombia|United States of Colombia]] failed, [[e:rafael-nunez|Rafael Núñez]] and the Conservatives imposed the constitution of 1886, which created a centralised [[s:gran-colombia|Republic of Colombia]], gave the president strong powers and restored the Catholic Church's role in education.
republic-of-colombia.r: The [[e:thousand-days-war|Thousand Days' War]] of 1899 to 1902 devastated the country, and in 1903 [[s:republic-of-panama|Panama]] seceded with [[s:united-states|United States]] support. [[e:coffee-economy|Coffee]] became the main export. The assassination of [[e:jorge-eliecer-gaitan|Jorge Eliécer Gaitán]] in 1948 unleashed [[e:la-violencia|La Violencia]], a civil conflict ended by the power-sharing [[e:national-front-colombia|National Front]] from 1958 to 1974. [[e:guerrilla-warfare|Guerrilla]] groups such as the [[e:revolutionary-armed-forces-of-colombia|FARC]], founded in 1964, and drug cartels such as [[e:pablo-escobar|Pablo Escobar's]] in [[e:medellin|Medellín]] fuelled violence for decades.
republic-of-colombia.e: A new constitution in 1991 replaced that of 1886. President [[e:juan-manuel-santos|Juan Manuel Santos]] signed a peace agreement with the [[e:revolutionary-armed-forces-of-colombia|FARC]] in 2016, winning the [[e:nobel-peace-prize|Nobel Peace Prize]]. [[e:gustavo-petro|Gustavo Petro]] became the first left-wing president in 2022.

ramadanids.t: A Turkmen dynasty that ruled Adana and the Cilician plain for over 250 years, first under the Mamluks and then under the Ottomans.
ramadanids.o: After the [[e:mamluk-sultanate|Mamluks]] broke the [[s:armenian-kingdom-of-cilicia|Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia]], [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] of the Uc Ok group settled the Cilician plain. Around 1352 their leader [[e:ramadan-bey|Ramadan Bey]] was recognised by the [[e:mamluk|Mamluks]] as emir of the region, with [[e:adana|Adana]] as his seat.
ramadanids.r: The Ramadanids ruled as hereditary [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] [[e:vassal|vassals]] over [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] tribes and the [[e:cotton|cotton]] and grain lands of the Cilician plain, guarding the frontier with the [[s:karamanids|Karamanids]] and the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]]. In 1516-1517 they went over to [[e:selim-i|Selim I]] and were kept as hereditary governors of the Ottoman sanjak of [[e:adana|Adana]]. [[e:piri-mehmed-pasha-ramadanid|Piri Mehmed Pasha]], a 16th-century ruler, built the Great Mosque complex of Adana.
ramadanids.e: The family lost its hereditary governorship in 1608, when [[e:adana|Adana]] became an ordinary Ottoman province. The Ramazanoglu mansion and mosque in Adana survive.

republic-of-venice.t: The 'Most Serene Republic', a merchant state on the lagoon that ruled a maritime empire across the Adriatic and Aegean for a thousand years until Napoleon ended it in 1797.
republic-of-venice.o: Refugees from mainland cities settled the lagoon islands during the barbarian invasions. Venetian tradition places the election of the first doge, [[e:paolo-lucio-anafesto|Paolo Lucio Anafesto]], in 697, under Byzantine overlordship. After resisting [[e:pepin-of-italy|Pepin of Italy]] in 810 the government moved to the [[e:rialto|Rialto]] islands, and in 828 merchants brought the relics of [[e:mark-the-evangelist|Saint Mark]], the city's patron.
republic-of-venice.r: [[e:venice|Venice]] was an aristocratic republic headed by an elected doge for life, whose power was increasingly checked by councils. The 1297 '[[e:serrata-del-maggior-consiglio|Serrata]]' closed the Great Council to a hereditary nobility, and the Council of Ten guarded security. Trade privileges in [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] from 1082 and the Fourth Crusade of 1204, led by Doge [[e:enrico-dandolo|Enrico Dandolo]], built a [[e:stato-da-mar|Stato da Mar]] of [[e:dalmatia|Dalmatia]], [[e:crete|Crete]], [[s:corcyra|Corfu]] and later [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]]. The Arsenal, glass-making and [[e:printing-press|printing]] made it an industrial and cultural centre.
republic-of-venice.e: Wars with the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] cost [[e:venice|Venice]] [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]] (1571), [[e:crete|Crete]] (1669) and the [[e:peloponnese|Morea]] (1718). In 1797 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] forced the last doge, [[e:ludovico-manin|Ludovico Manin]], to abdicate, and the [[e:treaty-of-campo-formio|Treaty of Campo Formio]] handed Venice to [[e:austria|Austria]]. It joined the [[s:kingdom-of-italy|Kingdom of Italy]] in 1866.

republic-of-the-seven-tenths.t: Alpine peasant republic of the upper Rhône valley, an ally of the Swiss Confederacy that ruled itself through seven communal districts.
republic-of-the-seven-tenths.o: The communities ([[e:zenden|Zenden]]) of the [[e:upper-valais|Upper Valais]] had long contested power with the prince-[[e:bishop|bishop]] of [[e:sion-switzerland|Sion]]. After decades of struggle, the Zenden forced Bishop [[e:hildebrand-jost|Hildebrand Jost]] to abandon most of his temporal rights in 1628 and finally in 1634, and the [[e:valais|Valais]] became a republic of seven tenths: [[e:goms|Goms]], [[e:brig-switzerland|Brig]], [[e:visp|Visp]], [[e:raron|Raron]], [[e:leuk|Leuk]], [[e:sierre|Sierre]] and Sion.
republic-of-the-seven-tenths.r: [[e:sovereignty|Sovereignty]] lay with the Diet (Landrat), in which each tenth sent delegates, while the [[e:bishop|bishop]] kept a largely honorary role. The republic was a [[e:zugewandter-ort|Zugewandter Ort]], an associate of the [[s:old-swiss-confederacy|Old Swiss Confederacy]], and governed the French-speaking [[e:lower-valais|Lower Valais]] as a subject territory. Its economy rested on Alpine farming and trade over the [[e:simplon-pass|Simplon]] pass, dominated by families such as the Stockalper of [[e:brig-switzerland|Brig]].
republic-of-the-seven-tenths.e: The [[e:lower-valais|Lower Valais]] rebelled in 1798 and French troops entered the country. [[e:valais|Valais]] was incorporated into the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]] in 1798, later becoming the [[s:rhodanic-republic|Rhodanic Republic]], a French [[e:departement|department]], and in 1815 a Swiss canton.

republic-of-pirates.t: The pirate stronghold at Nassau that, for a decade after the War of the Spanish Succession, sheltered Blackbeard and the leading pirates of the golden age.
republic-of-pirates.o: French and Spanish raids in 1703 and 1706 wrecked [[s:county-of-nassau|Nassau]] on [[e:new-providence|New Providence]] and drove off the governor, leaving the [[s:bahamas|Bahamas]] without effective authority. Privateers left idle by the end of the [[e:war-of-the-spanish-succession|War of the Spanish Succession]], and sailors who had plundered the wrecks of the 1715 Spanish treasure fleet, gathered in its harbour.
republic-of-pirates.r: It was not a formal state but a loose community of pirate crews, often called the [[e:flying-gang|Flying Gang]], who elected captains and shared plunder under ship articles. [[e:benjamin-hornigold|Benjamin Hornigold]] and [[e:henry-jennings|Henry Jennings]] were leading figures, alongside [[e:blackbeard|Edward Teach]], [[e:charles-vane|Charles Vane]], [[e:sam-bellamy|Sam Bellamy]] and [[e:calico-jack|Calico Jack Rackham]]. Merchants from [[e:new-england|New England]] and the islands traded supplies for loot, and the shallow harbour protected pirate sloops from warships.
republic-of-pirates.e: In 1718 [[e:woodes-rogers|Woodes Rogers]] arrived as royal governor with a royal pardon. Many [[e:piracy|pirates]] accepted it, and [[e:benjamin-hornigold|Hornigold]] even hunted former comrades; [[e:charles-vane|Vane]] escaped and fought on, while Teach was killed off North [[s:province-of-carolina|Carolina]] that year. Eight pirates were hanged at [[s:county-of-nassau|Nassau]] in December 1718, and the base was closed.

russian-sfsr.t: Soviet Russia, the first socialist state, created by the October Revolution and later the largest republic of the Soviet Union.
russian-sfsr.o: In the [[e:october-revolution|October Revolution]] of 1917 the Bolsheviks under [[e:vladimir-lenin|Vladimir Lenin]] overthrew the [[s:russian-republic|Russian Republic]]'s Provisional Government in [[e:petrograd|Petrograd]] and proclaimed Soviet power. In January 1918 the state was declared a Soviet republic, the capital moved to [[e:moscow|Moscow]] in March, and the first constitution of July 1918 named it the Russian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic.
russian-sfsr.r: Power lay with the [[e:communist-party-of-the-soviet-union|Communist Party]], which ruled through soviets and the secret police, the [[e:cheka|Cheka]]. The Bolsheviks nationalised land and industry, made peace with [[e:germany|Germany]] at [[e:treaty-of-brest-litovsk|Brest-Litovsk]] and won the Civil War against the [[e:white-movement|Whites]]. In 1922 the republic co-founded the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]], after which it was governed largely through Union institutions, without its own Communist Party until 1990.
russian-sfsr.e: In 1990 the republic declared [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]], and [[e:boris-yeltsin|Boris Yeltsin]] was elected its president in 1991. After the failed August coup, the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] was dissolved in December 1991, and the republic became the Russian Federation, continuing as the [[e:soviet-union|Soviet Union's]] successor state.

republic-of-el-salvador.t: The smallest and most densely populated country of Central America, independent since 1841, shaped by coffee oligarchy, military rule and civil war.
republic-of-el-salvador.o: After the [[s:federal-republic-of-central-america|Federal Republic of Central America]] broke apart, El [[e:salvador|Salvador]] adopted a constitution in February 1841 declaring itself a sovereign and independent state. For decades it remained entangled in the wars of its neighbours, often allied or opposed to [[e:guatemala|Guatemala's]] [[e:rafael-carrera|Rafael Carrera]], while some leaders still hoped to restore the union.
republic-of-el-salvador.r: From the 1860s [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] replaced [[e:indigo|indigo]], and laws of 1881 to 1882 abolished communal lands, concentrating property among a small elite. In 1932 the regime of [[e:maximiliano-hernandez-martinez|Maximiliano Hernández Martínez]] crushed a peasant uprising in [[e:la-matanza|La Matanza]], killing thousands, many of them indigenous. Military governments ruled for half a century. The [[e:football-war|Football War]] with [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]] came in 1969, and from 1980 to 1992 civil war between the army and the [[e:farabundo-marti-national-liberation-front|FMLN]] [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrillas]] killed about 75,000 people.
republic-of-el-salvador.e: The [[e:chapultepec-peace-accords|Chapultepec Peace Accords]] of 1992 ended the war. El [[e:salvador|Salvador]] adopted the US dollar in 2001. President [[e:nayib-bukele|Nayib Bukele]], elected in 2019, adopted bitcoin as legal tender and imposed a long state of exception against gangs, reshaping the country's politics.

republic-of-mahabad.t: The short-lived Kurdish republic of 1946, the first modern Kurdish state, whose leaders' fate shaped Kurdish nationalism for generations.
republic-of-mahabad.o: During the Soviet occupation of northern [[e:iran|Iran]], Kurdish nationalists in [[e:mahabad|Mahabad]] formed the [[e:society-for-the-revival-of-kurdistan|Komala]] society and then the [[e:kurdistan|Kurdistan]] [[e:democratic-party-uganda|Democratic Party]] under [[e:qazi-muhammad|Qazi Muhammad]], a respected judge and religious leader. With Soviet backing, the Kurdish Republic was proclaimed in Mahabad on 22 January 1946.
republic-of-mahabad.r: The republic controlled a small area around [[e:mahabad|Mahabad]]. It made Kurdish the language of schools and government, published newspapers and journals, and created a small army whose most important commander was [[e:mustafa-barzani|Mustafa Barzani]], leader of Iraqi Kurdish fighters who had taken refuge in [[e:iran|Iran]]. It cooperated with the [[s:azerbaijan-peoples-government|Azerbaijan People's Government]] in [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]] while disputing border districts with it.
republic-of-mahabad.e: After the Soviet withdrawal, Iranian troops entered [[e:mahabad|Mahabad]] in December 1946. [[e:qazi-muhammad|Qazi Muhammad]] was hanged in March 1947; [[e:mustafa-barzani|Barzani]] led his men on a march to the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]], later returning to lead the Kurdish movement in the [[s:republic-of-iraq|Republic of Iraq]].

rajahnate-of-cebu.t: The Visayan port kingdom of Sugbu, where Magellan baptised Rajah Humabon in 1521 and Spain founded its first Philippine settlement in 1565.
rajahnate-of-cebu.o: [[e:cebu|Cebu]] grew as a trading port on the east coast of Cebu Island, linked to Chinese, Siamese and other Asian traders by the 15th century; Chinese ceramics are common in its burials. A later tradition, the Aginid, attributes its founding to a prince called Sri Lumay, but this is not supported by contemporary sources.
rajahnate-of-cebu.r: [[e:cebu|Cebu]] was ruled by a rajah over datus, freemen and dependants, and taxed visiting ships. [[e:antonio-pigafetta|Antonio Pigafetta]], who arrived with [[e:ferdinand-magellan|Ferdinand Magellan]] in April 1521, described its trade and court. [[e:rajah-humabon|Rajah Humabon]] and hundreds of his people were baptised, but the alliance broke down after [[e:lapulapu|Lapulapu]] of Mactan killed Magellan in battle on 27 April 1521.
rajahnate-of-cebu.e: [[e:miguel-lopez-de-legazpi|Miguel Lopez de Legazpi]] arrived in 1565 and [[e:rajah-humabon|Humabon]]'s successor Rajah Tupas submitted to [[e:spain|Spain]]. [[e:cebu|Cebu]] became the first Spanish city in the islands and the seat of the [[s:captaincy-general-of-the-philippines|Captaincy General of the Philippines]] until 1571. [[e:magellans-cross|Magellan's Cross]] and the [[e:santo-nino-de-cebu|Santo Nino]] image recall the first encounter.
rajahnate-of-cebu.re: Indigenous Philippine religion, later Roman Catholicism

republic-of-south-africa.t: South Africa as a republic since 1961, from the height of apartheid to the democratic transition led by Nelson Mandela in 1994.
republic-of-south-africa.o: After a whites-only referendum in 1960, the [[s:union-of-south-africa|Union of South Africa]] became a republic on 31 May 1961 and left the [[e:commonwealth-of-nations|Commonwealth]]. Prime Minister [[e:hendrik-verwoerd|Hendrik Verwoerd]] was the leading architect of grand apartheid, while the [[e:african-national-congress|African National Congress]], banned after [[e:sharpeville-massacre|Sharpeville]] in 1960, turned to armed struggle.
republic-of-south-africa.r: The apartheid state classified people by race, created [[e:bantustan|Bantustans]] such as [[e:transkei|Transkei]] and [[e:bophuthatswana|Bophuthatswana]], and imprisoned leaders including [[e:nelson-mandela|Nelson Mandela]] after the [[e:rivonia-trial|Rivonia Trial]] of 1964. The [[e:soweto-uprising|Soweto uprising]] of 1976, township revolts and international [[e:sanctions|sanctions]] weakened the regime. Mining, especially of gold, and manufacturing made it [[e:africa|Africa's]] largest economy. [[e:pretoria|Pretoria]], [[e:cape-town|Cape Town]] and [[e:bloemfontein|Bloemfontein]] shared capital functions.
republic-of-south-africa.e: [[e:f-w-de-klerk|F. W. de Klerk]] unbanned the [[e:african-national-congress|ANC]] and released [[e:nelson-mandela|Mandela]] in 1990. The first democratic elections, on 27 April 1994, made Mandela president, and the 1996 constitution set up a multiracial democracy with eleven official languages.
republic-of-south-africa.la: isiZulu, isiXhosa, Afrikaans, English, Sesotho, Setswana

republic-of-yucatan.t: Breakaway republic on the Yucatán Peninsula that twice left Mexico in the 1840s and returned in 1848 as the Caste War threatened its existence.
republic-of-yucatan.o: Yucatán's elites resented the [[s:centralist-republic-of-mexico|Centralist Republic of Mexico]] and its taxes and levies. A federalist revolt led by [[e:santiago-iman|Santiago Imán]] in 1839 to 1840 restored local autonomy, and in 1841 the peninsula declared itself independent, with [[e:merida-yucatan|Mérida]] as capital. A brief reunion in 1843 broke down, and Yucatán separated again in 1845 to 1846.
republic-of-yucatan.r: Its 1841 constitution, drafted largely by [[e:manuel-crescencio-rejon|Manuel Crescencio Rejón]], introduced the amparo, a citizen's legal protection against unconstitutional acts that later entered Mexican law. Politics was dominated by the rivalry of [[e:santiago-mendez|Santiago Méndez]] of [[e:campeche|Campeche]] and [[e:miguel-barbachano|Miguel Barbachano]] of [[e:merida-yucatan|Mérida]]. The economy relied on henequen, [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] and [[e:maize|maize]], and Maya peasants bore heavy taxes, debt and loss of land, while being armed for the factions' wars.
republic-of-yucatan.e: In 1847 Maya communities rose in the [[e:caste-war-of-yucatan|Caste War]] and nearly drove the whites from the peninsula. Desperate, the government offered [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] to the [[s:united-states|United States]], [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and [[e:spain|Spain]]. [[s:mexico|Mexico]] sent troops and money, and Yucatán formally rejoined [[e:mexico|Mexico]] in August 1848. Rebel Maya later founded [[s:chan-santa-cruz|Chan Santa Cruz]].

rambrai-state.t: A small Khasi chiefdom of the West Khasi Hills, one of the 25 Khasi states that acceded to India in 1948.
rambrai-state.o: Hima Rambrai was one of the Khasi chiefdoms of the [[e:meghalaya|Meghalaya]] plateau; its origins are known only from oral tradition, and the register's start date is approximate.
rambrai-state.r: Rambrai was headed by a [[e:syiem|Syiem]] chosen from a royal clan, with succession through the female line and decisions taken with clan elders in a dorbar. Little written record of its history exists.
rambrai-state.e: Rambrai came under British supervision in the 19th century and acceded to [[e:india|India]] in 1948, joining [[e:assam|Assam]]. It is now part of West Khasi Hills district, [[e:meghalaya|Meghalaya]].

ryuzoji-clan-domain.t: The domain of the Ryuzoji of Hizen, whose ruthless lord Ryuzoji Takanobu briefly dominated northwestern Kyushu.
ryuzoji-clan-domain.o: The [[e:ryuzoji-clan|Ryuzoji]] were [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the Shoni family in [[e:hizen-province|Hizen]] province. [[e:ryuzoji-takanobu|Ryuzoji Takanobu]], once a monk, succeeded to the headship and around 1550 secured control of Saga; he then broke the power of his former masters, the Shoni, and subdued rival local lords.
ryuzoji-clan-domain.r: After the [[e:otomo-clan|Otomo]] were crushed by the [[e:shimazu-clan|Shimazu]] at [[e:battle-of-mimikawa|Mimikawa]] in 1578, [[e:ryuzoji-takanobu|Takanobu]] expanded quickly across [[e:hizen-province|Hizen]], [[e:chikugo-province|Chikugo]] and parts of [[e:chikuzen-province|Chikuzen]], becoming one of three great powers of [[e:kyushu|Kyushu]] alongside the Otomo and Shimazu. He was known as the bear of Hizen and governed through force, with his retainer [[e:nabeshima-naoshige|Nabeshima Naoshige]] as his chief commander and adviser.
ryuzoji-clan-domain.e: In 1584 [[e:ryuzoji-takanobu|Takanobu]] attacked the Arima family, who were supported by the [[e:shimazu-clan|Shimazu]], and was killed at the battle of [[e:battle-of-okitanawate|Okitanawate]]. Power passed in practice to [[e:nabeshima-naoshige|Nabeshima Naoshige]], whose family founded the [[s:saga-domain|Saga Domain]].

ruperts-land.t: The vast Hudson Bay watershed granted to the Hudson's Bay Company in 1670 and run as a fur-trading empire for 200 years before passing to Canada.
ruperts-land.o: In 1670 [[e:charles-ii-of-england|Charles II]] chartered the [[e:hudsons-bay-company|Hudson's Bay Company]], giving it trading rights and ownership of all lands draining into [[e:hudson-bay|Hudson Bay]], named Rupert's Land after its first governor, [[e:prince-rupert-of-the-rhine|Prince Rupert]]. The grant covered much of what is now northern [[s:province-of-quebec|Quebec]] and [[e:ontario|Ontario]], [[e:manitoba|Manitoba]], [[e:saskatchewan|Saskatchewan]], [[e:alberta|Alberta]] and parts of the northern [[s:united-states|United States]], though the company knew little of the interior.
ruperts-land.r: For a century the company kept to coastal forts such as [[e:york-factory|York Factory]], where [[e:cree|Cree]] and [[e:assiniboine|Assiniboine]] traders brought beaver pelts in exchange for guns, kettles and cloth. French raids under [[e:pierre-le-moyne-diberville|Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville]] captured several posts until the [[e:treaty-of-utrecht|Treaty of Utrecht]] in 1713. Competition from the [[e:north-west-company|North West Company]] pushed the company inland after 1774, ending in merger in 1821. Under governor [[e:george-simpson|George Simpson]] it ruled the West, and the [[s:red-river-colony|Red River Colony]] and [[e:metis|Métis]] society grew.
ruperts-land.e: Under the [[e:deed-of-surrender|Deed of Surrender]] of 1869 the company sold Rupert's Land to the new [[s:canada|Dominion of Canada]] for 300,000 pounds, and the transfer in 1870 followed the [[e:red-river-resistance|Red River Resistance]] led by [[e:louis-riel|Louis Riel]].

remi.t: Belgic people of Champagne who sided with Caesar from the start, making Reims the chief Roman city of northern Gaul.
remi.o: The Remi held the chalk plains of [[s:county-of-champagne|Champagne]] around [[e:reims|Durocortorum]] (Reims). In 57 BCE, while the other [[s:belgae-britain|Belgae]] formed a league against [[e:rome|Rome]], they sent the envoys Iccius and Andecomborius to offer Caesar their submission and support.
remi.r: They shared laws and magistrates with their kinsmen the [[s:suessiones|Suessiones]] and controlled a network of oppida. Their loyalty brought them supremacy over neighbouring peoples, and Caesar used their land as a base throughout his campaigns.
remi.e: Under [[e:rome|Rome]] [[e:reims|Durocortorum]] became capital of the province of [[e:gallia-belgica|Gallia Belgica]], with monuments such as the [[e:porte-de-mars|Porte de Mars]]. As Reims it became an archbishopric, where [[e:bishop|Bishop]] [[e:saint-remigius|Remigius]] baptised [[e:clovis-i|Clovis]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-franks|Kingdom of the Franks]] and French kings were later crowned.

republic-of-geneva.t: The Calvinist city-republic on Lake Geneva, the 'Protestant Rome', which threw off its bishop and Savoy in 1535.
republic-of-geneva.o: [[e:geneva|Geneva]] was ruled by the [[s:prince-bishopric-of-geneva|Prince-Bishopric of Geneva]], with the [[s:duchy-of-savoy|Duchy of Savoy]] exerting growing influence. The townspeople allied with the [[s:canton-of-fribourg|Canton of Fribourg]] and the [[s:canton-of-bern|Canton of Bern]] in 1526, and in 1535, with Bernese support, they drove out the [[e:bishop|bishop]] and adopted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]], making the city an independent republic.
republic-of-geneva.r: [[e:john-calvin|John Calvin]], who settled there in 1536 and again from 1541, shaped its church ordinances; the Consistory enforced strict morals, and the [[e:academy-of-geneva|Academy]], founded in 1559, trained Reformed pastors for [[e:france|France]], [[e:scotland|Scotland]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]]. Councils dominated by leading families governed, and the city prospered from [[e:printing-press|printing]], banking and watchmaking, much of it brought by [[e:huguenots|Huguenot]] refugees. In 1602 Genevans repelled Savoy's night attack, the [[e:l-escalade|Escalade]].
republic-of-geneva.e: [[e:france|France]] annexed [[e:geneva|Geneva]] in 1798, making it the capital of the [[e:departement|department]] of [[e:leman-department|Léman]]. Freed in 1813, it joined the [[s:swiss-confederation|Swiss Confederation]] as a canton in 1815.

ramnad-kingdom.t: The kingdom of the Sethupathi chiefs of Ramanathapuram, guardians of the pilgrimage route to Rameswaram.
ramnad-kingdom.o: The [[e:maravar|Maravar]] chief [[e:sadaikka-thevar|Sadaikka Thevar]] was recognised as Sethupathi, protector of the causeway to [[e:rameswaram|Rameswaram]], by the [[s:madurai-nayak-dynasty|Madurai Nayak dynasty]] around 1605. His successors ruled the dry coastal region of Ramnad as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of [[e:madurai|Madurai]] until [[e:kizhavan-sethupathi|Kizhavan Sethupathi]] asserted independence in the late 17th century.
ramnad-kingdom.r: The Sethupathis led a warrior society of [[e:maravar|Maravar]] clans and controlled the pilgrim route and pearl fisheries of the [[e:palk-strait|Palk Strait]]. They endowed the [[e:ramanathaswamy-temple|Ramanathaswamy]] temple at [[e:rameswaram|Rameswaram]], building its long corridors. [[e:kizhavan-sethupathi|Kizhavan Sethupathi]] persecuted [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] converts and executed the missionary [[e:john-de-britto|John de Britto]] in 1693.
ramnad-kingdom.e: Ramnad lost territory to [[e:thanjavur|Thanjavur]] and the Sivaganga chiefdom in the 18th century. After the [[s:carnatic-sultanate|Nawabs of Arcot]] and then the British took control, the [[e:east-india-company|British East India Company]] deposed the Sethupathi in the 1790s and turned Ramnad into a zamindari estate in 1803.

republic-of-spanish-haiti.t: The first, nine-week independence of the Dominican east of Hispaniola, declared in 1821 and ended by Haitian occupation in 1822.
republic-of-spanish-haiti.o: Frustrated by [[e:spain|Spain's]] neglect during [[s:espana-boba|España Boba]], the lawyer and official [[e:jose-nunez-de-caceres|José Núñez de Cáceres]] led a bloodless coup in [[e:santo-domingo|Santo Domingo]] on 1 December 1821. He proclaimed the Independent State of Spanish [[s:first-empire-of-haiti|Haiti]] and sought union with [[e:simon-bolivar|Simón Bolívar's]] [[s:gran-colombia|Gran Colombia]].
republic-of-spanish-haiti.r: [[e:jose-nunez-de-caceres|Núñez de Cáceres]] headed a provisional government and issued a constitutive act modelled on the Spanish American republics. The new state kept [[e:slavery|slavery]] and the existing social hierarchy, which alienated many black and mulatto Dominicans, and some frontier towns declared for [[s:first-empire-of-haiti|Haiti]] instead. [[e:simon-bolivar|Bolívar]]'s government never replied to the request for union.
republic-of-spanish-haiti.e: [[e:jean-pierre-boyer|Jean-Pierre Boyer]], president of the [[s:republic-of-haiti-1806-1849|Republic of Haiti]], marched east with an army, and [[e:santo-domingo|Santo Domingo]] surrendered without resistance on 9 February 1822. The whole island was united under [[s:first-empire-of-haiti|Haiti]] until 1844, and the period is remembered in the [[s:first-dominican-republic|Dominican Republic]] as the 'Ephemeral Independence'.

ruteni.t: Gallic people of the Rouergue whose land later produced the red samian pottery of La Graufesenque, sold across the Roman world.
ruteni.o: The Ruteni lived in the modern [[e:aveyron|Aveyron]], around [[e:rodez|Segodunum]] (Rodez). After 121 BCE part of their territory was annexed to the Roman Province, so that Caesar distinguishes the Ruteni provinciales from the independent Ruteni.
ruteni.r: They were clients of the [[s:arverni|Arverni]]. Their land held [[e:silver|silver]] mines, and they struck their own coins.
ruteni.e: The independent Ruteni joined [[e:vercingetorix|Vercingetorix]] in 52 BCE. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] [[e:rodez|Segodunum]] became Rodez, and the workshops of [[e:la-graufesenque|La Graufesenque]] near [[e:millau|Millau]] made millions of red-gloss pots exported across the Roman world. The medieval [[s:county-of-rodez|Rouergue]] kept their name.

republic-of-counani.t: A self-proclaimed republic in the jungle territory disputed by France and Brazil, created by French adventurers and never recognised.
republic-of-counani.o: The land between the [[e:oyapock-river|Oyapock]] and Araguari rivers, now the Brazilian state of [[e:amapa|Amapá]], was claimed by both [[e:france|France]] and [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]]. In 1886 a group of settlers at Counani, encouraged by French adventurers, proclaimed an independent republic, and the geographer [[e:jules-gros|Jules Gros]], who never visited it, was named president for life in [[e:paris|Paris]].
republic-of-counani.r: The republic existed mainly in [[e:paris|Paris]], where [[e:jules-gros|Gros]] issued decrees, created an order of chivalry and sold titles and stamps. On the ground Counani was a small settlement of a few hundred people, mostly of African and indigenous descent, living from gathering and gold prospecting. Neither [[e:france|France]] nor [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] recognised it, and the French government disavowed it in 1887.
republic-of-counani.e: The republic faded by 1891. A gold rush in the territory in the 1890s raised tensions, and in 1900 Swiss arbitration awarded the disputed region to [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]]. Later attempts to revive the republic came to nothing.

rueda-de-jalon-hudid.t: The last refuge of the Hudid kings of Zaragoza, a castle state on the Jalón kept alive through alliance with the Christian kings.
rueda-de-jalon-hudid.o: When the [[e:almoravid-empire|Almoravids]] took [[e:zaragoza|Zaragoza]] in 1110, the [[e:banu-hud|Hudid]] heir [[e:abd-al-malik-imad-al-dawla|Abd al-Malik Imad al-Dawla]] withdrew to the strong castle of [[e:rueda-de-jalon|Rueda de Jalón]], west of the city, and continued to rule a small territory from there, relying on [[e:alfonso-i-of-aragon|Alfonso I of Aragon]] against the Almoravids.
rueda-de-jalon-hudid.r: The [[e:banu-hud|Hudid]] remnant was a client principality, surviving between Almoravid [[e:zaragoza|Zaragoza]] and the advancing [[s:kingdom-of-aragon|Kingdom of Aragon]]. After Abd al-Malik's death in 1130 his son [[e:zafadola|Ahmad Sayf al-Dawla]], known to Christians as Zafadola, negotiated with [[e:alfonso-vii-of-leon-and-castile|Alfonso VII of Castile]].
rueda-de-jalon-hudid.e: [[e:zafadola|Zafadola]] handed [[e:rueda-de-jalon|Rueda]] to [[e:alfonso-vii-of-leon-and-castile|Alfonso VII]] in exchange for lands near [[e:toledo|Toledo]] and became a Castilian [[e:vassal|vassal]]. He later led Andalusi revolts against the [[e:almoravid-empire|Almoravids]] and was killed in 1146. The castle passed to Aragon.

radimichs.t: An East Slavic tribe on the Sozh river, tributaries first of the Khazars and then of Kiev, best known from a chronicle taunt.
radimichs.o: The [[e:primary-chronicle|Primary Chronicle]] says the [[e:radimichians|Radimichs]] descended from Radim, who came with his brother Vyatko from the west and settled on the [[e:sozh-river|Sozh]], a tributary of the [[e:dnieper|Dnieper]] in modern [[e:belarus|Belarus]] and western [[e:russia|Russia]]. Archaeology dates their settlement to the 8th century.
radimichs.r: They lived from farming and forest crafts in small fortified settlements, and their women wore distinctive seven-rayed temple rings. Like their neighbours they paid tribute to the [[e:khazar-khaganate|Khazars]], reportedly a [[e:silver|silver]] coin per plough. In 885 [[e:oleg-of-novgorod|Prince Oleg]] ordered them to pay that tribute to him instead.
radimichs.e: In 984 the general of Vladimir I, nicknamed Wolf's Tail, routed them on the river Pishchana, and the chronicle mocks them with the saying that [[e:radimichians|Radimichs]] run from a wolf's tail. They disappear as a separate tribe in the 12th century, their lands divided between the principalities of [[e:chernigov|Chernigov]] and [[e:smolensk|Smolensk]].

republic-of-maryland.t: A colony of free Black Americans at Cape Palmas, founded by Maryland colonisationists, which became an independent republic before joining Liberia in 1857.
republic-of-maryland.o: The [[e:maryland-state-colonization-society|Maryland State Colonization Society]], founded to remove free Black people from Maryland, sent settlers in 1834 under its agent [[e:james-hall-colonial-agent|James Hall]]. They bought land at [[e:cape-palmas|Cape Palmas]] from [[e:grebo-people|Grebo]] rulers and founded the town of [[e:harper-liberia|Harper]]. The colony, known as Maryland in [[e:africa|Africa]], stayed separate from the [[s:colony-of-liberia|Colony of Liberia]].
republic-of-maryland.r: In 1836 [[e:john-brown-russwurm|John Brown Russwurm]], a Jamaican-born graduate of [[e:bowdoin-college|Bowdoin College]] and co-founder of the first African American newspaper, became governor, the first Black governor of the colony, serving until 1851. The economy rested on farming and coastal trade. Relations with the numerous [[e:grebo-people|Grebo]] communities were tense over land and trade.
republic-of-maryland.e: Maryland declared independence in 1854 with [[e:william-prout-maryland|William Prout]] as governor. War with the [[e:grebo-people|Grebo]] in 1856-1857 nearly destroyed it, and after Liberian troops came to its aid it was annexed to [[s:liberia|Liberia]] in 1857 as [[e:maryland-county|Maryland County]].

regency-of-algiers.t: The Ottoman corsair state of Algiers, governed by pashas, aghas and finally deys, a major Mediterranean naval power for three centuries.
regency-of-algiers.o: In 1516 the corsair [[e:oruc-reis|Oruç Barbarossa]] seized [[e:algiers|Algiers]]. After his death, his brother [[e:hayreddin-barbarossa|Hayreddin]] placed the city under the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]] in 1519, receiving troops and the title of beylerbey. In 1529 he took the Spanish fortress on the [[e:penon-of-algiers|Peñon]], giving Algiers a secure harbour.
regency-of-algiers.r: Power passed from [[e:beylerbey|beylerbeys]] to pashas, then to aghas of the [[e:janissaries|Janissary]] corps and, from 1671, to elected deys. Beys ruled the provinces of Constantine, [[s:beylik-of-titteri|Titteri]] and the West. The state lived from corsairing, ransoming captives such as [[e:miguel-de-cervantes|Cervantes]], tribute paid by European states, and grain exports. [[e:uluj-ali|Uluj Ali]] was among its famous commanders.
regency-of-algiers.e: Attacks by the [[s:united-states|United States]] in 1815 and an Anglo-[[e:dutch|Dutch]] bombardment in 1816 weakened [[e:algiers|Algiers]]. After [[e:hussein-dey|Hussein Dey]] struck the French consul with a fly-whisk in 1827, [[e:france|France]] invaded in 1830, and the Dey capitulated, beginning [[s:french-algeria|French Algeria]].

republic-of-lithuania.t: The modern Lithuanian state, proclaimed in 1918, annexed by the Soviet Union in 1940 and the first Soviet republic to restore its independence, in 1990.
republic-of-lithuania.o: The [[e:council-of-lithuania|Council of Lithuania]], the Taryba, declared independence in [[e:vilnius|Vilnius]] on 16 February 1918 during the German occupation run by [[s:ober-ost|Ober Ost]]. After [[e:germany|Germany's]] defeat, [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] fought the Bolsheviks, the [[e:west-russian-volunteer-army|Bermontians]] and [[e:poland|Poland]]. Poland seized Vilnius in 1920, so [[e:kaunas|Kaunas]] became the temporary capital, and in 1923 [[e:lithuania|Lithuania]] took the [[s:klaipeda-region|Klaipėda Region]].
republic-of-lithuania.r: [[s:republic-of-lithuania-1918-1940|Interwar Lithuania]] carried out land reform and built national institutions; [[e:antanas-smetona|Antanas Smetona]], its first president, returned to power in a 1926 coup and ruled as an authoritarian leader. The [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] occupied and annexed the country in 1940, creating the [[s:lithuanian-soviet-socialist-republic|Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic]], followed by Nazi occupation and the [[e:holocaust|Holocaust]], which destroyed [[e:lithuanian-jews|Lithuanian Jewry]].
republic-of-lithuania.e: The [[e:sajudis|Sąjūdis]] movement led to the declaration of restored independence on 11 March 1990 under [[e:vytautas-landsbergis|Vytautas Landsbergis]]. Soviet troops killed fourteen civilians in [[e:vilnius|Vilnius]] on 13 January 1991, but independence was recognised later that year. [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] joined the EU and [[e:nato|NATO]] in 2004 and the eurozone in 2015.

republic-of-bolivia.t: The landlocked Andean republic named after Simón Bolívar, born from Upper Peru in 1825 and refounded as a plurinational state in 2009.
republic-of-bolivia.o: After [[e:antonio-jose-de-sucre|Antonio José de Sucre's]] victory at [[e:battle-of-ayacucho|Ayacucho]] in 1824, an assembly in [[e:sucre|Chuquisaca]] declared the independence of [[s:royal-audiencia-of-charcas|Upper Peru]], the former Royal [[e:audiencia|Audiencia]] of [[e:upper-peru|Charcas]], on 6 August 1825. The new state was named after [[e:simon-bolivar|Bolívar]], and Sucre became its first elected president.
republic-of-bolivia.r: [[e:andres-de-santa-cruz|Andrés de Santa Cruz]] formed the [[s:peru-bolivian-confederation|Peru-Bolivian Confederation]] from 1836 to 1839. [[e:bolivia|Bolivia]] lost its coastline to [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]] in the War of the Pacific, [[e:acre|Acre]] to [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] in 1903, and much of the [[e:gran-chaco|Chaco]] to [[s:republic-of-paraguay|Paraguay]] in the Chaco War. [[e:silver|Silver]] and then [[e:tin|tin]] mining dominated the economy. The 1952 revolution under [[e:victor-paz-estenssoro|Víctor Paz Estenssoro]] brought universal suffrage, land reform and nationalisation of the mines, followed by military regimes from 1964 to 1982.
republic-of-bolivia.e: Democracy returned in 1982. In 2006 [[e:evo-morales|Evo Morales]] became the first indigenous president, and a 2009 constitution renamed the country the Plurinational State of [[e:bolivia|Bolivia]]. [[e:sucre|Sucre]] remains the constitutional capital, while [[e:la-paz|La Paz]] is the seat of government.

republic-of-mainz.t: The first democratic republic on German soil, a short experiment under French protection in revolutionary Mainz.
republic-of-mainz.o: French troops under General [[e:adam-philippe-comte-de-custine|Custine]] took [[e:mainz|Mainz]] in October 1792, and the elector fled. A Jacobin club formed, and in early 1793 elections were held under French supervision. On 18 March 1793 the [[e:rhenish-german-national-convention|Rhenish-German National Convention]] proclaimed a free state covering the left bank of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] from [[e:landau|Landau]] to [[e:bingen-am-rhein|Bingen]].
republic-of-mainz.r: The convention, led by the professor [[e:andreas-joseph-hofmann|Andreas Joseph Hofmann]] and the naturalist [[e:georg-forster|Georg Forster]], abolished feudal rule. Many inhabitants refused to vote or swear oaths, and the republic had no real authority beyond the French army's reach. On 21 March the convention asked to be annexed to [[e:france|France]], and Forster went to [[e:paris|Paris]] to present the request.
republic-of-mainz.e: Prussian and Austrian forces besieged [[e:mainz|Mainz]], which surrendered in July 1793, and the [[e:jacobin-club|Jacobins]] were persecuted. [[e:georg-forster|Forster]] died in exile in [[e:paris|Paris]] in 1794. The left bank later passed to [[e:france|France]], and the republic is remembered as an early German democracy.

reformed-government-of-the-republic-of-c.t: A Japanese-sponsored puppet government for occupied central China, set up at Nanjing in 1938 in the aftermath of the Nanjing Massacre.
reformed-government-of-the-republic-of-c.o: After capturing [[e:shanghai|Shanghai]] and [[e:nanjing|Nanjing]] in late 1937, the Japanese Central [[e:china|China]] Area Army sought Chinese collaborators to administer the lower [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]]. On 28 March 1938 it inaugurated the Reformed Government of the [[s:republic-of-china|Republic of China]] at Nanjing, under [[e:liang-hongzhi|Liang Hongzhi]], a former official of the [[s:beiyang-government|Beiyang government]].
reformed-government-of-the-republic-of-c.r: The regime nominally governed occupied parts of [[e:jiangsu|Jiangsu]], [[e:zhejiang|Zhejiang]] and Anhui and the Chinese districts of [[e:shanghai|Shanghai]], but its ministers had little authority and its revenues depended on Japanese approval. Its members were mostly older politicians from the warlord era, and it had little public support in a region devastated by war.
reformed-government-of-the-republic-of-c.e: In March 1940 it was dissolved into the [[s:wang-jingwei-regime|Wang Jingwei regime]], which took over its offices at [[e:nanjing|Nanjing]]. [[e:liang-hongzhi|Liang Hongzhi]] held posts in the new government and was executed for treason in 1946.
