raumarike.t: Petty kingdom of the Romerike plain north-east of Oslo, site of the Eidsivating assembly and an early conquest of Halfdan the Black.
raumarike.o: Raumarike covered the broad farming lowland of Romerike, north-east of the [[e:oslofjord|Oslofjord]]. It is known only from the sagas, which describe it as a small kingdom taken by [[e:halfdan-the-black|Halfdan the Black of Vestfold]] in the 9th century.
raumarike.r: The district was among the most fertile in eastern [[e:norway|Norway]], with dense settlement along the [[e:glomma|Glomma]] and [[e:vorma|Vorma]] rivers. The [[e:eidsivating|Eidsivating]], the law assembly of the [[e:upplands-norway|Upplands]], met at [[e:eidsvoll|Eidsvoll]] in the region, giving it a role in the legal life of inland Norway.
raumarike.e: [[e:halfdan-the-black|Halfdan the Black]] and his son [[e:harald-fairhair|Harald Fairhair]] incorporated Raumarike into their growing realm, and it became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-norway|Kingdom of Norway]]. [[e:eidsvoll|Eidsvoll]] later gained national fame as the place where [[e:norway|Norway's]] constitution was adopted in 1814.

republic-of-texas.t: The Lone Star Republic, which broke away from Mexico in 1836 and stayed independent for nearly ten years before joining the United States.
republic-of-texas.o: From the 1820s [[s:mexico|Mexico]] invited American settlers, led by empresarios such as [[e:stephen-f-austin|Stephen F. Austin]], into [[e:coahuila|Coahuila]] y [[s:hasinai-confederacy|Tejas]]. Tension over centralist rule and [[e:slavery|slavery]] led to revolt in 1835. Independence was declared at [[e:washington-on-the-brazos|Washington-on-the-Brazos]] on 2 March 1836; after the fall of the [[e:alamo-mission|Alamo]], [[e:sam-houston|Sam Houston]] defeated [[e:antonio-lopez-de-santa-anna|Santa Anna]] at [[e:battle-of-san-jacinto|San Jacinto]] in April.
republic-of-texas.r: The republic had a president, congress and constitution modelled on the [[s:united-states|United States]], and it protected [[e:slavery|slavery]]. [[e:cotton|Cotton]] farming expanded and settlers poured in with offers of free land. [[s:mexico|Mexico]] never recognised independence and raided [[e:san-antonio|San Antonio]] in 1842. Debts mounted, [[e:mirabeau-b-lamar|Mirabeau Lamar]]'s ill-fated [[e:texan-santa-fe-expedition|Santa Fe Expedition]] failed, and policy towards the [[e:comanche|Comanche]] swung between war and [[e:sam-houston|Houston]]'s attempts at peace. [[e:austin-texas|Austin]] became the capital in 1839.
republic-of-texas.e: Most Texans wanted annexation, delayed in Washington by the [[e:slavery|slavery]] question. Congress approved it in 1845, and [[e:texas|Texas]] became the 28th state in December. The annexation was a cause of the [[e:mexican-american-war|Mexican-American War]] of 1846 to 1848.

rhegion.t: Greek city on the toe of Italy guarding the Strait of Messina, which under the tyrant Anaxilas controlled both shores of the strait.
rhegion.o: Chalcidians from [[e:euboea|Euboea]], joined by exiles from [[s:messene|Messenia]], founded Rhegion around 720 BCE at the southern tip of [[e:calabria|Calabria]], on the Delphic oracle's advice according to tradition. Facing [[s:zancle|Zancle]] across the Strait, it controlled shipping between the Tyrrhenian and [[e:ionian-sea|Ionian Seas]].
rhegion.r: Rhegion adopted the laws of [[e:charondas|Charondas]] and was ruled by an aristocracy of Messenian descent until [[e:anaxilas|Anaxilas]] made himself tyrant around 494 BCE. He seized [[s:zancle|Zancle]], renamed it [[s:mamertine-messana|Messana]], and allied with [[e:carthage|Carthage]]. The city was later a democracy and an ally of [[s:athens|Athens]]. The lyric poet [[e:ibycus|Ibycus]] and the sculptor [[e:pythagoras|Pythagoras]] came from Rhegion. Its coins showing a lion's head and a hare are well known.
rhegion.e: [[e:dionysius-i-of-syracuse|Dionysius I]] captured and destroyed Rhegion in 387 BCE, but it revived. In 280 BCE, during the war with [[e:pyrrhus-of-epirus|Pyrrhus]], a Roman garrison of Campanian troops seized the city; [[e:rome|Rome]] retook it in 270 BCE and executed the mutineers. It remained a Greek-speaking ally, later [[e:reggio-calabria|Rhegium]] Iulium, and is today Reggio [[e:calabria|Calabria]].

republic-of-tarnobrzeg.t: A short-lived peasant republic in south-eastern Poland, led by a radical priest who demanded land reform after the First World War.
republic-of-tarnobrzeg.o: In November 1918, as Austrian authority in [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]] collapsed, a radical priest, [[e:eugeniusz-okon|Eugeniusz Okon]], and the peasant activist [[e:tomasz-dabal|Tomasz Dabal]] called on peasants and returning soldiers around [[e:tarnobrzeg|Tarnobrzeg]] to take power. At a rally on 6 November they proclaimed a republic in the district.
republic-of-tarnobrzeg.r: The movement demanded the division of large estates among peasants and the removal of landlords and officials. Its leaders formed a local council and militia, and peasants seized estate grain and forests. It never had a settled administration or defined borders and was more a social revolt than a state.
republic-of-tarnobrzeg.e: The new Polish government sent troops to restore order, and by spring 1919 the movement had been suppressed and its leaders arrested. Both [[e:eugeniusz-okon|Okon]] and [[e:tomasz-dabal|Dabal]] were later elected to the [[e:sejm|Sejm]] of the [[s:second-polish-republic|Second Polish Republic]], and Dabal became a communist.

republic-of-ancona.t: Self-governing Adriatic port and maritime republic that traded with Dalmatia and the Levant until the papacy took full control in 1532.
republic-of-ancona.o: Ancona, a port founded by [[e:greeks|Greeks]] from [[s:syracuse|Syracuse]] in about 387 BCE, kept trading links across the Adriatic through the early [[e:middle-ages|Middle Ages]]. Around the start of the 11th century it began governing itself as a commune within the [[e:march-of-ancona|March of Ancona]], under loose papal and imperial overlordship.
republic-of-ancona.r: Ancona was ruled by elected consuls, later by a council of elders, and was a merchant republic with trading houses in [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]], [[e:alexandria|Alexandria]] and the Dalmatian ports, often allied with [[s:republic-of-ragusa|Ragusa]] against [[e:venice|Venice]]. It famously resisted [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa's]] siege in 1173 with Byzantine support; the widow Stamura became a local heroine. Its maritime statutes regulated Adriatic trade.
republic-of-ancona.e: In 1532 [[e:pope-clement-vii|Pope Clement VII]] brought Ancona under direct papal rule, installing a garrison and building a fortress. The city remained the main port of the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]] until it joined the [[s:kingdom-of-italy|Kingdom of Italy]] in 1860.

rasulid-dynasty.t: The most brilliant medieval dynasty of Yemen, whose scholar-sultans ruled from Ta'izz, grew rich on Aden's trade and built famous madrasas.
rasulid-dynasty.o: [[e:nur-al-din-umar-ibn-rasul|Nur al-Din Umar ibn Rasul]], a commander of [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] origin, was left as deputy when the last ruler of [[s:ayyubid-yemen|Ayyubid Yemen]] departed in 1229. He soon declared himself sultan and obtained recognition from the [[e:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasid]] [[e:caliphate|caliph]] in 1235, founding a dynasty based in [[e:taiz|Ta'izz]] and [[e:zabid|Zabid]].
rasulid-dynasty.r: Under [[e:al-muzaffar-yusuf-i|al-Muzaffar Yusuf]], who reigned for 45 years and took [[e:dhofar|Dhofar]] in 1279, the state reached from [[e:mecca|Mecca's]] borders to Dhofar. The Rasulids taxed the spice and textile trade of [[e:aden|Aden]], exchanged embassies with [[e:egypt|Egypt]], [[e:india|India]] and [[e:china|China]], and received [[e:ming-empire|Ming]] fleets in the 15th century. Several sultans were scholars: [[e:al-ashraf-umar-ii|al-Ashraf Umar]] wrote on [[e:babylonian-astronomy|astronomy]], medicine and farming. [[e:taiz|Ta'izz]] and [[e:zabid|Zabid]] gained mosques and [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni]] [[e:shafii-school|Shafi'i]] [[e:madrasa|madrasas]].
rasulid-dynasty.e: From the late 14th century revolts by slave troops, tribes and family rivals weakened the dynasty. After disputed successions in the 1440s, the [[s:tahirid-sultanate|Tahirid Sultanate]] took power in 1454. The Rasulid period is remembered as [[e:yemen|Yemen's]] medieval golden age.

russian-republic.t: Russia's brief democratic republic between the fall of the tsar and the Bolshevik seizure of power in 1917.
russian-republic.o: The [[e:february-revolution|February Revolution]] of 1917 forced [[e:nicholas-ii|Nicholas II]] to abdicate, ending the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]]. A Provisional Government formed from the [[e:state-duma|Duma]], first under Prince [[e:georgy-lvov|Georgy Lvov]], shared power with the [[e:petrograd|Petrograd]] Soviet. On 1 September 1917 [[e:alexander-kerensky|Alexander Kerensky]], by then its head, formally proclaimed [[e:russia|Russia]] a republic.
russian-republic.r: The government granted civil liberties, abolished the death penalty and promised a Constituent Assembly, but it kept fighting the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] and postponed land reform. A failed offensive in June, the July Days and General [[e:lavr-kornilov|Lavr Kornilov's]] attempted march on [[e:petrograd|Petrograd]] in August weakened it, while the Bolsheviks gained support in the soviets.
russian-republic.e: The Bolsheviks overthrew the Provisional Government in the [[e:october-revolution|October Revolution]] and created the [[s:russian-sfsr|Russian SFSR]]. The Constituent Assembly, elected in November, met in January 1918 under [[e:viktor-chernov|Viktor Chernov]] and proclaimed a Russian Democratic Federative Republic, but the Bolsheviks dispersed it the next day.

ratlam-state.t: A Rathore Rajput state of Malwa founded under Shah Jahan, later known for its trade in opium and gold.
ratlam-state.o: Ratlam was granted in 1652 by the Mughal emperor [[e:shah-jahan|Shah Jahan]] to [[e:ratan-singh-of-ratlam|Ratan Singh]], a [[e:rathore|Rathore]] descended from [[e:udai-singh-of-marwar|Raja Udai Singh of Marwar]], in reward for service. [[s:sailana-state|Sailana]] and [[s:sitamau-state|Sitamau]] later branched off from the same family.
ratlam-state.r: The [[e:maharaja|Maharajas]] ruled a fertile plateau of wheat and opium. Ratlam became a trading town known for its markets, gold and the savoury sev that still carries its name. Under British paramountcy it was a salute state of the [[e:malwa-agency|Malwa Agency]]; [[e:sajjan-singh-of-ratlam|Sajjan Singh]] reigned from 1893 to 1947.
ratlam-state.e: Ratlam joined [[s:madhya-bharat|Madhya Bharat]] in 1948 and [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]] in 1956. It is now a district headquarters and a railway junction.

republic-of-alsace-lorraine.t: A short-lived republic declared in Strasbourg as German rule collapsed in November 1918, swept away when French troops arrived days later.
republic-of-alsace-lorraine.o: As the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] collapsed in November 1918, soldiers' and workers' councils formed in [[s:free-imperial-city-of-strasbourg|Strasbourg]] and other towns of the [[s:imperial-territory-of-alsace-lorraine|Imperial Territory of Alsace-Lorraine]]. On 11 November the regional parliament constituted itself as a national council, and a republic was declared amid competing plans for autonomy.
republic-of-alsace-lorraine.r: Power was divided between the soldiers' councils, some influenced by revolutionary socialism, and the national council and Strasbourg's socialist mayor, [[e:jacques-peirotes|Jacques Peirotes]]. The new authorities tried to keep order as German troops withdrew, but the republic had no recognition or real administration.
republic-of-alsace-lorraine.e: French troops entered [[s:free-imperial-city-of-strasbourg|Strasbourg]] on 22 November 1918 and the councils dissolved. The [[e:treaty-of-versailles|Treaty of Versailles]] confirmed the return of [[s:imperial-territory-of-alsace-lorraine|Alsace-Lorraine]] to [[e:france|France]].

republic-of-vietnam.t: South Vietnam, the US-backed anti-communist state of 1955 to 1975, whose fall to North Vietnamese forces ended the Vietnam War.
republic-of-vietnam.o: In October 1955 [[e:ngo-dinh-diem|Ngo Dinh Diem]], prime minister of the [[s:state-of-vietnam|State of Vietnam]], deposed [[e:bao-dai|Bao Dai]] through a referendum and proclaimed the Republic of [[s:socialist-republic-of-vietnam|Vietnam]] with himself as president. It controlled the territory south of the 17th parallel, with nearly a million northern refugees, many Catholic, among its people.
republic-of-vietnam.r: [[e:ngo-dinh-diem|Diem]]'s government, dominated by his family, was authoritarian and repressed communists, sects and, in 1963, Buddhist protesters. It fought a growing insurgency led by the [[e:viet-cong|National Liberation Front]]. After Diem's overthrow and murder in November 1963, a series of generals ruled until [[e:nguyen-van-thieu|Nguyen Van Thieu]] became president in 1967. More than half a million US troops fought in the country by 1968.
republic-of-vietnam.e: After the [[e:paris-peace-accords|Paris Peace Accords]] of 1973 US forces withdrew, and [[s:democratic-republic-of-vietnam|North Vietnam]]'s spring offensive of 1975 overran the south. [[e:ho-chi-minh-city|Saigon]] fell on 30 April 1975. Authority passed to the [[s:republic-of-south-vietnam|Republic of South Vietnam]], and many South Vietnamese fled abroad as boat people.

rusellae.t: Etruscan hill city near modern Grosseto, ringed by massive walls, which overlooked the Lake Prile lagoon until Rome captured it in 294 BCE.
rusellae.o: Rusellae, modern Roselle, occupied two hills above the coastal plain of the [[e:ombrone|Ombrone]], then bordering the lagoon of [[e:lake-prile|Lake Prile]]. Settled from the Villanovan period, it grew into a city in the 7th century BCE, when houses of unbaked brick were built, and in the 6th century it was enclosed by walls of huge polygonal blocks some 3 km long.
rusellae.r: Its prosperity came from farming the [[e:ombrone|Ombrone]] plain, fishing and salt in the lagoon, and links with the mining districts of [[s:vetulonia|Vetulonia]], which it overtook in importance during the 6th century BCE. Excavation has revealed a forum area, houses and craft quarters, but little is known of its government beyond the general Etruscan pattern of aristocratic magistrates.
rusellae.e: [[e:livy|Livy]] records that [[e:lucius-postumius-megellus|Lucius Postumius Megellus]] stormed Rusellae in 294 BCE, taking 2,000 prisoners. As a Roman ally it sent grain and [[e:timber|timber]] for [[e:scipio-africanus|Scipio]]'s fleet in 205 BCE, and later became a Roman colony with a forum, baths and amphitheatre. It remained a bishopric until the see moved to [[e:grosseto|Grosseto]] in 1138.

republic-of-ezo.t: A short-lived breakaway regime in Hokkaido set up by shogunate loyalists, whose leaders were chosen by an election of officers.
republic-of-ezo.o: When the [[e:shogun|shogunate]] surrendered [[e:edo-tokyo|Edo]] in 1868, Admiral [[e:enomoto-takeaki|Enomoto Takeaki]] sailed north with much of the shogunal navy, picking up defeated soldiers and French military advisers including [[e:jules-brunet|Jules Brunet]]. In late 1868 his forces landed in Ezo, took the star fort of [[e:goryokaku|Goryokaku]] at [[e:hakodate|Hakodate]] and captured Matsumae.
republic-of-ezo.r: In January 1869 officers voted to elect [[e:enomoto-takeaki|Enomoto]] as president, with other posts filled by election, an unprecedented step in [[e:japan|Japan]]. The regime sought recognition from foreign powers as a de facto authority and asked to develop Ezo under a Tokugawa lord, but received only cautious neutrality.
republic-of-ezo.e: Imperial forces landed in spring 1869. The warship [[e:kaiyo-maru|Kaiyo Maru]] had already been lost, and after the battle of [[e:hakodate|Hakodate]], where [[e:hijikata-toshizo|Hijikata Toshizo]] was killed, [[e:enomoto-takeaki|Enomoto]] surrendered [[e:goryokaku|Goryokaku]] in June 1869. He was later pardoned and served the Meiji government.

red-river-colony.t: A settlement founded by Lord Selkirk at the forks of the Red and Assiniboine rivers, cradle of the Métis nation and of the province of Manitoba.
red-river-colony.o: In 1811 the [[e:hudsons-bay-company|Hudson's Bay Company]] granted [[e:thomas-douglas-5th-earl-of-selkirk|Thomas Douglas]], Earl of Selkirk, about 300,000 square kilometres of [[s:ruperts-land|Rupert's Land]] for a farming colony. Scottish settlers, many displaced by the [[e:highland-clearances|Highland Clearances]], arrived in 1812 under Governor [[e:miles-macdonell|Miles Macdonell]]. The rival [[e:north-west-company|North West Company]] and its [[e:metis|Métis]] allies saw the colony as a threat to the pemmican supply of the [[e:fur-trade|fur trade]].
red-river-colony.r: Conflict culminated in the [[e:battle-of-seven-oaks|Battle of Seven Oaks]] in 1816, in which Governor [[e:robert-semple|Robert Semple]] and about twenty colonists were killed. After [[e:thomas-douglas-5th-earl-of-selkirk|Selkirk]]'s heirs sold it back to the Company in 1836, the district was governed by the [[e:council-of-assiniboia|Council of Assiniboia]]. Its population was mostly [[e:metis|Métis]] and English-speaking country-born families living by farming, freighting and the buffalo hunt.
red-river-colony.e: When the Company sold [[s:ruperts-land|Rupert's Land]] to [[s:province-of-canada|Canada]] without consulting residents, the [[e:metis|Métis]] under [[e:louis-riel|Louis Riel]] formed the [[s:provisional-government-of-assiniboia|Provisional Government of Assiniboia]] in 1869. Negotiations led to the creation of [[e:manitoba|Manitoba]] as a province of [[e:canada|Canada]] in 1870.

republic-of-marseille.t: A brief maritime commune in which the merchants of Marseille governed their port independently before Charles of Anjou crushed it.
republic-of-marseille.o: In the early 13th century the citizens of the lower town of [[s:massalia|Marseille]] bought out the rights of their viscounts and formed a commune, organised around the Confraternity of the Holy Spirit. The register dates the republic from 1214, while the upper town remained under the [[e:bishop|bishop]].
republic-of-marseille.r: The commune elected a podestà on the Italian model and a council of citizens, issued statutes and ran its own trade with the [[e:levant|Levant]], [[e:sicily|Sicily]] and [[e:north-africa|North Africa]], rivalling [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] and [[e:pisa|Pisa]]. It joined the opposition to the counts of [[s:county-of-provence|Provence]] and backed [[e:raymond-vii-count-of-toulouse|Raymond VII]] of [[s:county-of-toulouse|Toulouse]].
republic-of-marseille.e: [[e:charles-i-of-anjou|Charles of Anjou]], the new count of [[s:county-of-provence|Provence]], forced the city to submit in 1252 and, after further revolts, imposed the Chapters of Peace in 1257, ending its independence. [[s:massalia|Marseille]] kept municipal privileges within the County of Provence.

republic-of-costa-rica.t: Central America's most stable democracy, independent since 1848, known for coffee, abolishing its army in 1948 and its long peaceful elections.
republic-of-costa-rica.o: Having left the Central American federation in 1838, Costa Rica formally declared itself a republic on 31 August 1848 under President [[e:jose-maria-castro-madriz|José María Castro Madriz]]. [[e:coffee-economy|Coffee]] exports through the port of [[e:puntarenas|Puntarenas]] had already created a prosperous [[e:central-valley-costa-rica|Central Valley]] elite and a large class of smallholders.
republic-of-costa-rica.r: [[e:juan-rafael-mora-porras|Juan Rafael Mora Porras]] led the Central American war that defeated [[e:william-walker|William Walker]] in 1856 to 1857, in which the drummer [[e:juan-santamaria|Juan Santamaría]] became a national hero. [[e:tomas-guardia-gutierrez|Tomás Guardia]]'s rule from 1870 began the railway to [[e:puerto-limon|Limón]], built by [[e:minor-c-keith|Minor Keith]], which spawned the banana industry. The death penalty was abolished in 1882, and the 1889 election is often regarded as the first truly free one. The [[e:federico-tinoco-granados|Tinoco]] dictatorship of 1917 to 1919 was a rare break.
republic-of-costa-rica.e: After a short civil war in 1948, [[e:jose-figueres-ferrer|José Figueres]] abolished the army, and the 1949 constitution confirmed it. Costa Rica has since held regular peaceful elections, became a leader in ecotourism and conservation, and [[e:oscar-arias|Óscar Arias]] won the [[e:nobel-peace-prize|Nobel Peace Prize]] in 1987 for Central American peace efforts.

cr.a: See File history below for details.

russian-state.t: The White government of Admiral Kolchak, based in Omsk, which claimed to rule all of Russia against the Bolsheviks in 1918 to 1920.
russian-state.o: In September 1918 anti-Bolshevik groups meeting at Ufa created an All-[[e:russian-provisional-government|Russian Provisional Government]], a five-member Directory led by [[e:nikolai-avksentiev|Nikolai Avksentiev]]. Based in [[e:omsk|Omsk]], it called its territory the Russian State. On 18 November 1918 officers overthrew the Directory and made Admiral [[e:alexander-kolchak|Alexander Kolchak]] Supreme Ruler.
russian-state.r: [[e:alexander-kolchak|Kolchak]] ruled as a military dictator, and other White leaders, including [[e:anton-denikin|Denikin]], formally recognised his authority. His government controlled [[e:siberia|Siberia]] and the [[e:ural-mountains|Urals]] and held most of the Russian gold reserve. Its armies advanced towards the [[e:volga|Volga]] in spring 1919, but reprisals, corruption and failure to win over peasants undermined it.
russian-state.e: The [[e:red-army|Red Army]] counter-attacked, and [[e:omsk|Omsk]] fell in November 1919. [[e:alexander-kolchak|Kolchak]] was handed over by the [[e:czechoslovak-legion|Czechoslovak Legion]] in [[e:irkutsk|Irkutsk]] and shot in February 1920. Remnants of his forces retreated to the Far East.

republic-of-florence.t: The city-republic of bankers and wool merchants that minted the florin and nurtured Dante, Giotto, Brunelleschi and the Medici-led Renaissance.
republic-of-florence.o: After [[e:matilda-of-tuscany|Matilda of Canossa]] died in 1115, [[e:florence|Florence's]] citizens took control of the city, and consuls are recorded by the 1130s. The commune conquered its rural territory, destroyed nearby [[e:fiesole|Fiesole]] in 1125 and became the strongest power in [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Tuscany]] during the 13th century.
republic-of-florence.r: [[s:duchy-of-florence|Florence]] was ruled by priors elected from the [[e:guild|guilds]], under the Ordinances of Justice of 1293 that excluded [[e:magnates|magnates]]. The gold florin, first minted in 1252, became [[e:europe|Europe's]] standard coin, and banks such as the [[e:bardi-family|Bardi]], [[e:peruzzi-family|Peruzzi]] and Medici lent across Europe. [[e:guelphs-and-ghibellines|Guelph-Ghibelline]] and Black-White feuds exiled [[e:dante-alighieri|Dante]]. From 1434 [[e:cosimo-de-medici|Cosimo de' Medici]] and his grandson [[e:lorenzo-de-medici|Lorenzo]] steered the republic informally while patronising [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]] art and learning.
republic-of-florence.e: The Medici were expelled in 1494; [[e:girolamo-savonarola|Savonarola]] and then [[e:piero-soderini|Piero Soderini]] led the restored republic until the Medici returned in 1512. A last republic fell after the siege of 1529–1530, and in 1532 [[e:alessandro-de-medici|Alessandro de' Medici]] became duke, creating the [[s:duchy-of-florence|Duchy of Florence]].

rajpipla-state.t: A Gohil Rajput state in the Narmada valley of Gujarat, the largest in the Rewa Kantha Agency, whose last Maharaja won the English Derby in 1934.
rajpipla-state.o: Tradition holds that a [[e:gohil|Gohil]] [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] prince inherited the hill country south of the [[e:narmada-river|Narmada]] from his maternal grandfather, a [[e:parmar-rajputs|Parmar]] chief, in the mid-14th century, founding the dynasty that ruled until 1948.
rajpipla-state.r: Rajpipla was hilly and forested, with a large [[e:bhils|Bhil]] and Vasava population. It faced pressure from the [[s:gujarat-sultanate|Gujarat Sultanate]], the [[e:mughal-empire|Mughals]] and later the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads]] of [[s:baroda-state|Baroda State]], to whom it paid tribute. Under the British it was the leading state of the [[e:rewa-kantha-agency|Rewa Kantha Agency]]. [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]] Vijaysinhji built a new palace, and his horse Windsor Lad won the [[e:epsom-derby|Derby]] in 1934.
rajpipla-state.e: Rajpipla merged into [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]] in 1948 and is now in [[e:narmada-river|Narmada]] district, [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]].

rhenish-republic.t: Separatist state proclaimed in the occupied Rhineland in 1923 with French backing, which collapsed amid popular hostility.
rhenish-republic.o: During the hyperinflation and the Franco-Belgian occupation of the [[e:ruhr|Ruhr]] in 1923, Rhenish separatists sought a state independent of [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] and [[e:berlin|Berlin]]. In October 1923 armed groups seized town halls in [[s:free-imperial-city-of-aachen|Aachen]], [[e:koblenz|Koblenz]], [[e:trier|Trier]] and other towns, and a Rhenish Republic was proclaimed, with a provisional government in Koblenz led by [[e:josef-friedrich-matthes|Josef Friedrich Matthes]] and [[e:hans-adam-dorten|Hans Adam Dorten]].
rhenish-republic.r: The republic controlled little beyond public buildings occupied with the tolerance of French and Belgian troops. It had no administration, money or popular support, and its armed bands requisitioned food and goods. In November 1923 local residents fought separatists in the [[e:siebengebirge|Siebengebirge]] near Aegidienberg, and a related separatist government in the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]] was ended by the assassination of its leader in January 1924.
rhenish-republic.e: Faced with hostility and British opposition, [[e:france|France]] withdrew support, and the movement collapsed by early 1924. The [[e:rhineland|Rhineland]] remained part of [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] within the [[s:weimar-republic|Weimar Republic]].

republic-of-peru.t: The Andean republic that grew from the heart of the Inca Empire and Spain's richest viceroyalty, declared independent in 1821.
republic-of-peru.o: [[e:jose-de-san-martin|José de San Martín]] proclaimed [[e:peru|Peru's]] independence in [[e:lima|Lima]] on 28 July 1821, establishing the [[s:protectorate-of-peru|Protectorate of Peru]]. A constituent congress met in 1822, and [[e:simon-bolivar|Bolívar]] took command in 1823. The victory of [[e:antonio-jose-de-sucre|Antonio José de Sucre]] at [[e:battle-of-ayacucho|Ayacucho]] in December 1824 ended Spanish power, and the last royalists at [[e:callao|Callao]] surrendered in 1826.
republic-of-peru.r: Early decades were marked by rivalry between military caudillos and the [[s:peru-bolivian-confederation|Peru-Bolivian Confederation]]. The guano boom of the 1840s to 1870s funded railways, and [[e:ramon-castilla|Ramón Castilla]] abolished [[e:slavery|slavery]] and the Indian tribute in 1854. In the [[e:war-of-the-pacific|War of the Pacific]] [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]] occupied [[e:lima|Lima]] in 1881 and took [[e:tarapaca|Tarapacá]]. Twentieth-century politics swung between oligarchic, military and populist governments, including [[e:juan-velasco-alvarado|Juan Velasco Alvarado's]] reformist regime from 1968.
republic-of-peru.e: [[e:peru|Peru]] returned to civilian rule in 1980 but suffered the [[e:shining-path|Shining Path]] insurgency. [[e:alberto-fujimori|Alberto Fujimori]] ruled from 1990 to 2000. Since then it has seen strong growth based on mining and frequent clashes between presidents and Congress.

redones.t: Gallic people of eastern Brittany whose chief town Condate became the city of Rennes.
redones.o: The Redones lived in the basin of the [[e:vilaine|Vilaine]], in the modern [[e:ille-et-vilaine|Ille-et-Vilaine]]. Caesar lists them among the Armorican peoples who submitted to [[e:publius-licinius-crassus|Publius Crassus]] in 57 BCE.
redones.r: Their oppidum of [[e:rennes|Condate]] stood at the confluence of the Ille and the [[e:vilaine|Vilaine]], as its Gaulish name, meaning confluence, indicates. They struck gold coins of Armorican type.
redones.e: They sent troops to relieve [[e:battle-of-alesia|Alesia]] in 52 BCE. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] [[e:rennes|Condate]] became a walled civitas capital, called Redones in late antiquity, the origin of Rennes, later the capital of the [[s:duchy-of-brittany|Duchy of Brittany]].

republic-of-turkey.t: The nation state founded by Mustafa Kemal Ataturk on the ruins of the Ottoman Empire, spanning Anatolia and eastern Thrace.
republic-of-turkey.o: The [[s:government-of-the-grand-national-assembly|Government of the Grand National Assembly]] won the [[e:turkish-war-of-independence|War of Independence]], abolished the Ottoman sultanate and secured recognition at [[e:treaty-of-lausanne|Lausanne]] in July 1923. On 29 October 1923 the assembly proclaimed the republic, with [[e:ankara|Ankara]] as capital and [[e:mustafa-kemal-ataturk|Mustafa Kemal]] as president.
republic-of-turkey.r: [[e:mustafa-kemal-ataturk|Ataturk]]'s reforms abolished the [[e:caliphate|caliphate]] (1924), replaced Islamic law with European-based codes, introduced the [[e:latin|Latin]] alphabet (1928), gave women the vote (1934) and made secularism a constitutional principle. [[e:ismet-inonu|Ismet Inonu]] continued one-party rule until multi-party elections brought [[e:adnan-menderes|Adnan Menderes]] to power in 1950. [[e:turkey|Turkey]] joined [[e:nato|NATO]] in 1952. The army intervened in 1960, 1971 and 1980, and Kurdish insurgency began in 1984.
republic-of-turkey.e: [[e:turkey|Turkey]] became an EU candidate in 1999. [[e:recep-tayyip-erdogan|Recep Tayyip Erdogan]], prime minister from 2003, became president in 2014, survived a coup attempt in 2016 and introduced a presidential system in 2018. In 2022 the country adopted Turkiye as its international name.

rajgarh-state.t: An Umat Parmar Rajput state of Malwa, sister state of Narsinghgarh, ruled from Rajgarh on the Newaj river.
rajgarh-state.o: Rajgarh was ruled by the Umat clan of [[e:parmar-rajputs|Parmar Rajputs]], settled in the region of [[e:malwa|Malwa]] known after them as Umatwara. The capital was established at Rajgarh around 1640. In 1681 the estate was divided and [[s:narsinghgarh-state|Narsinghgarh State]] formed from part of it.
rajgarh-state.r: The rulers, styled Rawat and later Raja, governed a rolling plateau of wheat and opium farming. In the 18th century they paid tribute to the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]], especially [[e:scindias|Sindhia]], before British paramountcy in 1818. Rajgarh was an eleven-gun salute state of the [[e:bhopal-agency|Bhopal Agency]].
rajgarh-state.e: Rajgarh joined [[s:madhya-bharat|Madhya Bharat]] in 1948 and [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]] in 1956. It is now a district headquarters.

republic-of-entre-rios.t: A short-lived federal republic of the Argentine Littoral, created by the caudillo Francisco Ramírez in 1820.
republic-of-entre-rios.o: After defeating [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]] at [[e:battle-of-cepeda-1820|Cepeda]] in 1820 and signing the [[e:treaty-of-pilar|Treaty of Pilar]], [[e:francisco-ramirez|Francisco Ramírez]] broke with his former leader [[e:jose-gervasio-artigas|José Artigas]] of the [[s:federal-league|Federal League]] and defeated him. In September 1820 he proclaimed the Republic of [[e:entre-rios-province|Entre Ríos]], uniting Entre Ríos, [[e:corrientes|Corrientes]] and [[e:misiones-province|Misiones]], with himself as Supreme Chief.
republic-of-entre-rios.r: [[e:francisco-ramirez|Ramírez]] organised the republic with its seat at [[e:concepcion-del-uruguay|Concepción del Uruguay]]. He issued regulations on administration, justice and the army, promoted schools and set up a [[e:printing-press|printing]] press. The republic was largely a military creation built around his personal authority and his gaucho cavalry.
republic-of-entre-rios.e: In 1821 [[e:francisco-ramirez|Ramírez]] launched a campaign against [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]] and [[e:santa-fe-argentina|Santa Fe]]. He was defeated and killed in July 1821, and [[e:estanislao-lopez|Estanislao López]] displayed his head in Santa Fe. The republic broke up, and [[e:entre-rios-province|Entre Ríos]], [[e:corrientes|Corrientes]] and [[e:misiones-province|Misiones]] became separate provinces.

republic-of-prekmurje.t: Week-long republic proclaimed in 1919 in the Slovene-speaking Prekmurje region, caught between Hungary and the new Yugoslav state.
republic-of-prekmurje.o: [[e:prekmurje|Prekmurje]], between the [[e:mur-river|Mura]] river and the Hungarian border, had a Slovene-speaking majority but had long belonged to [[e:hungary|Hungary]]. In the chaos of 1919, with Hungary under the [[s:hungarian-soviet-republic|Hungarian Soviet Republic]], the local politician [[e:vilmos-tkalecz|Vilmos Tkálecz]] proclaimed an independent Mura Republic at [[e:murska-sobota|Murska Sobota]] on 29 May 1919, hoping for foreign recognition.
republic-of-prekmurje.r: [[e:vilmos-tkalecz|Tkálecz]] formed a small government and tried to raise a militia, but the republic had no real army, money or international support. Most of the population was rural, Slovene and Hungarian-speaking, Catholic and Lutheran, and was more concerned with food and order than with independence.
republic-of-prekmurje.e: Troops of the [[e:hungarian-red-army|Hungarian Red Army]] retook [[e:murska-sobota|Murska Sobota]] on 6 June 1919, ending the republic after about a week; [[e:vilmos-tkalecz|Tkálecz]] fled. In August 1919 the Yugoslav army occupied [[e:prekmurje|Prekmurje]], and the [[e:treaty-of-trianon|Treaty of Trianon]] in 1920 assigned it to the [[s:kingdom-of-yugoslavia|Kingdom of Yugoslavia]]. It is now part of [[e:slovenia|Slovenia]].

republic-of-latvia.t: The Latvian nation-state, proclaimed in Riga in 1918, annexed by the Soviet Union in 1940 and restored to independence in 1990-1991.
republic-of-latvia.o: The [[e:peoples-council-of-latvia|People's Council]] proclaimed the Republic of Latvia on 18 November 1918, with [[e:karlis-ulmanis|Kārlis Ulmanis]] as prime minister. It had to fight the [[s:latvian-socialist-soviet-republic|Latvian Socialist Soviet Republic]], the [[e:freikorps|German Freikorps]] and the [[e:west-russian-volunteer-army|Bermontians]] in the [[e:latvian-war-of-independence|War of Independence]], which ended with the peace treaty with [[s:russian-sfsr|Soviet Russia]] in August 1920.
republic-of-latvia.r: The [[e:constitution-of-latvia|Satversme]], adopted in 1922, created a parliamentary democracy, with [[e:janis-cakste|Jānis Čakste]] as first president, and a land reform redistributed [[e:baltic-germans|Baltic German]] estates. [[e:karlis-ulmanis|Ulmanis]] seized power in 1934 and ruled as an authoritarian leader. In 1940 the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] occupied and annexed Latvia as the [[s:latvian-soviet-socialist-republic|Latvian Soviet Socialist Republic]], followed by Nazi occupation and further Soviet rule.
republic-of-latvia.e: The [[e:popular-front-of-latvia|Popular Front]] and events such as the [[e:baltic-way|Baltic Way]] of 1989 led to a declaration restoring independence on 4 May 1990, completed on 21 August 1991. The [[e:constitution-of-latvia|Satversme]] was restored, and Latvia joined the EU and [[e:nato|NATO]] in 2004 and the eurozone in 2014.

republic-of-mirdita.t: Short-lived breakaway state of the Catholic Mirdita highlands in northern Albania, backed by Yugoslavia in 1921.
republic-of-mirdita.o: The Catholic [[e:mirdita|Mirdita]] clan region in northern [[s:albania|Albania]] had long enjoyed autonomy under its hereditary captains. Opposing the new government in [[e:tirana|Tirana]], the clan leader [[e:gjon-marka-gjoni|Gjon Marka Gjoni]], with backing from the [[s:kingdom-of-yugoslavia|Kingdom of Yugoslavia]], proclaimed the Republic of Mirdita in July 1921, the declaration being made in [[e:prizren|Prizren]] on Yugoslav territory.
republic-of-mirdita.r: The republic existed mainly as an armed revolt of [[e:mirdita|Mirdita]] tribesmen, supplied and armed from [[e:yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]], which hoped to weaken [[s:albania|Albania]] and claim border areas. It appealed to the [[e:league-of-nations|League of Nations]] for recognition, but had no institutions beyond the clan leadership.
republic-of-mirdita.e: Albanian government forces, with commanders including [[e:zog-i|Ahmet Zogu]], crushed the revolt in November 1921, while the [[e:conference-of-ambassadors|Conference of Ambassadors]] confirmed Albania's 1913 borders, ending Yugoslav claims. [[e:gjon-marka-gjoni|Gjon Marka Gjoni]] fled to [[e:yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]] and later reconciled with the government.

republic-of-guatemala.t: Guatemala as an independent republic since 1847, marked by coffee dictatorships, a CIA-backed coup in 1954 and a long civil war with genocide against the Maya.
republic-of-guatemala.o: After the collapse of the [[s:federal-republic-of-central-america|Federal Republic of Central America]], the conservative caudillo [[e:rafael-carrera|Rafael Carrera]] formally proclaimed the Republic of [[e:guatemala|Guatemala]] on 21 March 1847. Carrera ruled, with short interruptions, until his death in 1865, from 1854 as president for life, in close alliance with the Catholic Church and the [[e:guatemala-city|Guatemala City]] merchants.
republic-of-guatemala.r: The [[e:liberal-revolution-of-1871|Liberal Revolution of 1871]] brought [[e:justo-rufino-barrios|Justo Rufino Barrios]], who expropriated church lands and drove [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] expansion using forced Maya labour. Dictators [[e:manuel-estrada-cabrera|Manuel Estrada Cabrera]] and [[e:jorge-ubico|Jorge Ubico]] favoured the [[e:united-fruit-company|United Fruit Company]]. After the 1944 revolution, [[e:juan-jose-arevalo|Juan José Arévalo]] and [[e:jacobo-arbenz|Jacobo Árbenz]] pursued reform, but Árbenz's land reform provoked a [[e:1954-guatemalan-coup-detat|CIA-backed coup]] in 1954. Civil war from 1960 to 1996 killed about 200,000 people, most of them Maya.
republic-of-guatemala.e: Peace accords in 1996 ended the war, and a UN-backed truth commission found that acts of [[e:genocide|genocide]] had been committed against Maya communities. [[e:guatemala|Guatemala]] remains a presidential republic; [[e:bernardo-arevalo|Bernardo Arévalo]], son of the reformist president, took office in 2024.

raurici.t: Celtic people of the Rhine bend around Basel who joined the Helvetii's failed migration and later saw Rome found Augusta Raurica.
raurici.o: The Raurici lived along the upper [[e:rhine|Rhine]] around the [[s:canton-of-basel|Basel]] region and in the southern [[e:alsace|Alsace]] and [[e:jura-mountains|Jura]]. Caesar records them as neighbours and allies of the [[s:helvetii|Helvetii]].
raurici.r: Their oppidum on the Münsterhügel in [[s:canton-of-basel|Basel]] and the earlier open settlement at Basel-Gasfabrik show a wealthy community trading on the [[e:rhine|Rhine]].
raurici.e: In 58 BCE they burned their homes and joined the migration of the [[s:helvetii|Helvetii]], but after the defeat at [[e:bibracte|Bibracte]] they were sent back. Around 44 BCE [[e:lucius-munatius-plancus|Lucius Munatius Plancus]] founded the colony of [[e:augusta-raurica|Augusta Raurica]] (Augst) in their land.

rhode.t: A small Greek colony at Roses on the Catalan coast, linked to Emporion and Massalia, whose silver coins bore a rose.
rhode.o: Ancient writers credited Rhode to settlers from [[s:rhodes|Rhodes]], but archaeology shows a Greek settlement founded in the 5th to 4th century BCE, probably by [[s:massalia|Massalia]] or nearby [[s:emporion|Emporion]], on the [[e:gulf-of-roses|Gulf of Roses]] in north-east [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]].
rhode.r: Rhode was a small Greek trading town with its own pottery workshops. In the 3rd century BCE it minted [[e:silver|silver]] drachms showing a rose, a pun on its name, widely copied in southern [[e:gaul|Gaul]]. Excavations in the [[e:ciutadella-de-roses|Ciutadella of Roses]] have uncovered its houses and streets.
rhode.e: During the north-eastern revolt of 195 BCE Rhode was held against [[e:rome|Rome]] and was captured by [[e:cato-the-elder|Cato]]. It continued as a small town under Roman rule, later giving its name to Roses.

realm-of-the-gyulas.t: Semi-independent realm of the gyulas in Transylvania, whose Orthodox-leaning rulers were subdued by Stephen I of Hungary in 1003.
realm-of-the-gyulas.o: After the Hungarian conquest, [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]] was held by a branch of chiefs bearing the title gyula. Byzantine sources record that a gyula was baptised in [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] around 952 and brought back the monk [[e:hierotheos|Hierotheos]] as [[e:bishop|bishop]]. Their seat was probably at [[e:alba-iulia|Gyulafehérvár]] (Alba Iulia), on a Roman fort.
realm-of-the-gyulas.r: The gyulas ruled largely independently of the [[e:arpad|Árpád]] grand princes, controlling Transylvanian salt and the routes to [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]]. Their daughter [[e:sarolt|Sarolt]] married [[e:geza-grand-prince-of-the-hungarians|Grand Prince Géza]] and was the mother of Stephen I. Their [[e:christianity|Christianity]] was oriented to [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantium]], unlike the Western church favoured at [[e:esztergom|Esztergom]].
realm-of-the-gyulas.e: In 1003 Stephen I attacked his maternal uncle, [[e:gyula-the-younger|Gyula the Younger]], captured him and annexed [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]] to the [[s:kingdom-of-hungary-1000-1301|Kingdom of Hungary]] (1000-1301). The region later became the [[s:voivodeship-of-transylvania|Voivodeship of Transylvania]].

ravala.t: Coastal Estonian county around Lindanise, the site of modern Tallinn, conquered by King Valdemar II of Denmark in 1219.
ravala.o: Rävala occupied the northern coast of [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]] around the bay where [[s:reval|Tallinn]] now stands. A harbour and stronghold at Lindanise served Baltic shipping, and the Arab geographer [[e:muhammad-al-idrisi|al-Idrisi's]] 1154 map may record it as a town called Qlwry. The county appears in [[e:henry-of-livonia|Henry of Livonia's]] chronicle in the early 13th century.
ravala.r: Its elders controlled the harbour and the trade passing between [[e:scandinavia|Scandinavia]], [[s:grand-duchy-of-finland|Finland]] and [[e:veliky-novgorod|Novgorod]]. The county farmed the coastal plain and kept close ties with [[s:harjumaa|Harjumaa]] inland. Little else is known of its institutions.
ravala.e: In 1219 [[e:valdemar-ii-of-denmark|Valdemar II of Denmark]] landed with a crusading army, defeated the [[e:estonians|Estonians]] at the [[e:battle-of-lindanise|Battle of Lindanise]] and built a castle on [[e:toompea|Toompea]]; legend places the falling of the Danish flag, the [[e:flag-of-denmark|Dannebrog]], from the sky at this battle. Rävala became the core of the [[s:duchy-of-estonia-1219-1346|Duchy of Estonia]] (1219-1346), and Lindanise grew into [[s:reval|Reval]].

republic-of-burundi.t: The republic that replaced Burundi's monarchy in 1966, marked by military rule, mass killings and civil war before a fragile peace from 2000.
republic-of-burundi.o: In November 1966 Captain [[e:michel-micombero|Michel Micombero]] deposed the young king [[e:ntare-v-of-burundi|Ntare V]], ending the [[s:kingdom-of-burundi|Kingdom of Burundi]] and proclaiming a republic. Power rested with a Tutsi-dominated army and the single party [[e:union-for-national-progress|UPRONA]], founded by the independence hero [[e:louis-rwagasore|Prince Louis Rwagasore]], who had been assassinated in 1961.
republic-of-burundi.r: After a [[e:hutu|Hutu]] rebellion in 1972 the army killed perhaps 100,000 to 200,000 Hutu, mainly the educated, in the killings known as the [[e:ikiza|Ikiza]]. Further coups brought [[e:jean-baptiste-bagaza|Jean-Baptiste Bagaza]] in 1976 and [[e:pierre-buyoya|Pierre Buyoya]] in 1987. In 1993 [[e:melchior-ndadaye|Melchior Ndadaye]] became the first elected Hutu president, but his assassination months later started a civil war that killed some 300,000 people.
republic-of-burundi.e: The [[e:arusha-peace-and-reconciliation-agreement-for-burundi|Arusha Accords]] of 2000 and a 2005 constitution introduced ethnic power-sharing, and [[e:pierre-nkurunziza|Pierre Nkurunziza]] ruled from 2005 to 2020, his disputed third term sparking a crisis in 2015. The political capital moved to [[e:gitega|Gitega]] in 2019, and [[e:evariste-ndayishimiye|Evariste Ndayishimiye]] succeeded Nkurunziza in 2020.

royal-audiencia-of-quito.t: The Spanish colonial province of the northern Andes, governed from Quito, famed for its textile workshops and baroque art, and the forerunner of Ecuador.
royal-audiencia-of-quito.o: After the Spanish conquest of [[e:quito|Quito]] in 1534, the region was governed from [[e:lima|Lima]]. In 1563 [[e:philip-ii-of-spain|Philip II]] created the Royal [[e:audiencia|Audiencia]] of Quito, a high court with governing powers, covering the territory of modern [[s:republic-of-ecuador|Ecuador]] and parts of southern [[s:republic-of-colombia|Colombia]] and northern [[e:peru|Peru]], within the [[s:viceroyalty-of-peru|Viceroyalty of Peru]].
royal-audiencia-of-quito.r: The [[e:audiencia|Audiencia]] was headed by a president. Its economy rested on textile workshops called obrajes, which used indigenous labour to produce woollen cloth sold across the [[s:andecavi|Andes]], and on [[e:hacienda|haciendas]]. [[e:guayaquil|Guayaquil]] was the main port and shipbuilding centre. [[e:quito|Quito]] became renowned for the [[e:quito-school|Quito School]] of painting and sculpture and for churches such as [[e:church-of-the-society-of-jesus-quito|La Compañía]]. The [[e:rebellion-of-the-barrios|Rebellion of the Barrios]] in 1765 protested new taxes.
royal-audiencia-of-quito.e: [[e:quito|Quito]] was attached to the [[s:viceroyalty-of-new-granada|Viceroyalty of New Granada]] in 1739. A junta in Quito on 10 August 1809 was one of the first in [[e:spanish-america|Spanish America]], followed by the [[s:state-of-quito|State of Quito]]. [[e:sucre|Sucre's]] victory at [[e:battle-of-pichincha|Pichincha]] in 1822 brought Quito into [[s:gran-colombia|Gran Colombia]].

republic-of-iraq.t: The Iraqi state since the 1958 revolution: military regimes, Ba'athist dictatorship under Saddam Hussein, war and occupation, and a federal democracy since 2005.
republic-of-iraq.o: On 14 July 1958 the [[e:free-officers-movement-iraq|Free Officers]] under [[e:abd-al-karim-qasim|Abd al-Karim Qasim]] overthrew the [[s:kingdom-of-iraq|Kingdom of Iraq]] and proclaimed a republic. Qasim left the [[e:baghdad-pact|Baghdad Pact]], began land reform and claimed [[s:state-of-kuwait|Kuwait]], but was killed in a [[e:baath-party|Ba'athist]] coup in 1963. The Arif brothers then ruled until the Ba'ath Party took power again in 1968.
republic-of-iraq.r: Under [[e:ahmed-hassan-al-bakr|Ahmad Hasan al-Bakr]] and, from 1979, [[e:saddam-hussein|Saddam Hussein]], oil wealth funded development alongside a pervasive police state. [[e:iraq|Iraq]] fought [[e:iran|Iran]] from 1980 to 1988, conducted the [[e:anfal-campaign|Anfal campaign]] against the [[e:kurds|Kurds]], including the gas attack on [[e:halabja-massacre|Halabja]], and invaded [[s:state-of-kuwait|Kuwait]] in 1990, leading to the [[e:gulf-war|Gulf War]] and [[e:sanctions|sanctions]]. A US-led invasion in 2003 overthrew Saddam, and a 2005 constitution created a federal parliamentary system with a [[e:kurdistan|Kurdistan]] Region.
republic-of-iraq.e: Sectarian war followed in 2006 to 2008, and the Islamic State seized [[e:mosul|Mosul]] in 2014 before its defeat in 2017. [[e:iraq|Iraq]] remains a federal parliamentary republic, governed through power-sharing between Shia, [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni]] and Kurdish parties.

rouran-khaganate.t: The steppe empire that dominated Mongolia between the Xianbei and the Turks, and whose rulers made the title khagan the mark of supreme steppe rule.
rouran-khaganate.o: The Rouran traced their origin to Mugulü, a slave of the [[e:tuoba|Tuoba]] [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] in the 4th century, whose followers formed a band in the Mongolian steppe. [[e:yujiulu-shelun|Shelun]] united the tribes in 402, defeated the [[s:gaoche|Gaoche]] and took the title [[e:khagan|khagan]], establishing a confederation that stretched from [[e:manchuria|Manchuria]] to the [[e:tarim-basin|Tarim Basin]].
rouran-khaganate.r: The Rouran [[e:khagan|khagans]] ruled a mobile court over many subject peoples, including the Turks, whom they used as ironsmiths in the [[e:altai-mountains|Altai]]. Their main rival was the [[s:northern-wei|Northern Wei]], which mounted repeated campaigns against them; the Chinese called them Ruanruan, 'wriggling insects', as an insult. They also exercised influence over the [[e:tarim-basin|Tarim]] oasis states and the [[s:yueban|Yueban]].
rouran-khaganate.e: In 552 their Turkic [[e:vassal|vassals]] under [[e:bumin-qaghan|Bumin]], angered when the [[e:khagan|khagan]] Anagui refused him a bride, revolted and destroyed the khaganate, founding the [[e:first-turkic-khaganate|Turkic Khaganate]]. The last Rouran remnants were wiped out in 555. Some historians link them to the [[s:avar-khaganate|Pannonian Avars]], though this is disputed.

republic-of-baden.t: Democratic successor of the Grand Duchy of Baden, a stable Weimar-era state on the French border, divided after 1945.
republic-of-baden.o: In November 1918 a provisional government was formed in [[e:karlsruhe|Karlsruhe]] and [[e:frederick-ii-grand-duke-of-baden|Grand Duke Frederick II]] abdicated. In January 1919 [[e:baden|Baden]] elected a constituent assembly, one of the first German elections in which women could vote, and its constitution, approved by referendum in 1919, made Baden a democratic republic.
republic-of-baden.r: [[e:baden|Baden]] was governed by a stable [[e:weimar|Weimar]] coalition of the Catholic Centre, Social Democrats and liberals. As a border state facing [[e:france|France]], it suffered from the demilitarised zone along the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] and economic isolation. The [[e:nazism|Nazis]] took control in March 1933 under Reich governor [[e:robert-wagner-gauleiter|Robert Wagner]], who in 1940 deported Baden's [[e:jews|Jews]] to the [[e:gurs-internment-camp|Gurs]] camp in France.
republic-of-baden.e: In 1945 [[e:baden|Baden]] was divided between the American zone in the north, joined to Württemberg-Baden, and the French zone in the south, which became the state of Baden. All were merged into [[e:baden-wurttemberg|Baden-Württemberg]] in 1952.

republic-of-finland.t: Nordic republic that won independence from Russia in 1917, survived a civil war and two wars with the Soviet Union, and became a prosperous democracy.
republic-of-finland.o: [[e:finland|Finland's]] parliament declared independence from [[e:russia|Russia]] on 6 December 1917, under the Senate led by [[e:pehr-evind-svinhufvud|Pehr Evind Svinhufvud]]. A brutal civil war in 1918 between Reds and Whites ended in a White victory, and after a failed attempt at monarchy in the [[s:kingdom-of-finland-1918|Kingdom of Finland]] (1918), the 1919 constitution made [[s:grand-duchy-of-finland|Finland]] a republic with [[e:k-j-stahlberg|K. J. Ståhlberg]] as first president.
republic-of-finland.r: [[s:grand-duchy-of-finland|Finland]] built a parliamentary democracy with a strong presidency, bilingual in Finnish and Swedish. The [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] attacked in the [[e:winter-war|Winter War]] of 1939-1940, and [[e:finland|Finland]] fought again alongside [[e:germany|Germany]] in the [[e:continuation-war|Continuation War]] of 1941-1944, losing [[s:karelians|Karelia]] but keeping its independence. During the [[e:cold-war|Cold War]] President [[e:urho-kekkonen|Urho Kekkonen]] pursued neutrality and close relations with [[e:moscow|Moscow]].
republic-of-finland.e: Post-war [[s:grand-duchy-of-finland|Finland]] industrialised quickly, developing forestry, engineering and later electronics, and created a Nordic welfare state with a celebrated school system. It joined the [[e:european-union|European Union]] in 1995, adopted the euro in 1999 and joined [[e:nato|NATO]] in 2023 after [[e:russia|Russia's]] full-scale invasion of [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]].

republic-of-uhtua.t: Finnish-backed provisional government of East Karelia in 1919-1920, based in the village of Uhtua, which sought union with Finland.
republic-of-uhtua.o: After the [[e:russian-revolution|Russian Revolution]], Finnish nationalists hoped to join [[e:east-karelia|East Karelia]], [[e:bantustan|homeland]] of much [[e:kalevala|Kalevala]] folk poetry, to [[s:republic-of-finland|Finland]]. Finnish volunteer expeditions entered the region in 1918-1919, and in 1919 local [[s:karelians|Karelians]] and Finnish activists set up a Provisional Government of East [[e:karelia|Karelia]] at [[e:uhtua|Uhtua]] (now Kalevala).
republic-of-uhtua.r: The government controlled only the area around [[e:uhtua|Uhtua]] in the [[e:white-sea|White Sea]] [[s:karelians|Karelia]] region. It held a meeting of Karelian representatives that voted for separation from [[e:russia|Russia]], issued its own stamps and relied on Finnish volunteers and supplies.
republic-of-uhtua.e: The [[e:red-army|Red Army]] retook the area in 1920, and the government fled to [[s:republic-of-finland|Finland]]. The [[e:treaty-of-tartu-finnish-russian|Treaty of Tartu]] of 1920 left [[e:east-karelia|East Karelia]] in [[s:russian-sfsr|Soviet Russia]], which had already set up a Karelian Labour Commune that June. A further uprising in 1921-1922 also failed, and the area later formed the [[s:karelo-finnish-soviet-socialist-republic|Karelo-Finnish Soviet Socialist Republic]].

royal-niger-company-territories.t: The lands along the Niger and Benue ruled by George Goldie's chartered company, which secured the region for Britain against French and German rivals.
royal-niger-company-territories.o: [[e:george-taubman-goldie|George Taubman Goldie]] merged rival British trading firms on the [[e:niger-river|Niger]] into the [[e:royal-niger-company|United African Company]] in 1879, renamed the National African Company in 1882. He bought out French competitors, and his agents signed hundreds of treaties with local rulers. In 1886 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] granted the firm a royal charter as the Royal Niger Company, with power to govern the lower Niger and the [[e:benue-river|Benue]].
royal-niger-company-territories.r: The company used its charter to enforce a trade monopoly, charging heavy duties that ruined African middlemen such as the [[s:nembe-kingdom|Nembe]] traders of Brass, who attacked its depot at [[e:akassa-raid|Akassa]] in 1895. It kept its own constabulary, administrative centre at [[e:asaba|Asaba]] and trading posts up the rivers. In 1897 its forces defeated the [[s:bida-emirate|Bida Emirate]] and the [[s:ilorin-emirate|Ilorin Emirate]].
royal-niger-company-territories.e: Criticism of the monopoly and the need for state forces against French expansion led [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] to revoke the charter on 1 January 1900. The territories passed to the [[e:protectorate|Protectorates]] of Northern and [[s:protectorate-of-southern-nigeria|Southern Nigeria]], and the company continued as a trading business.

republic-of-noli.t: A tiny Ligurian seaside republic that kept its independence, under Genoese protection, from 1192 until 1797.
republic-of-noli.o: Noli, a small port on the western [[e:italian-riviera|Riviera]], freed itself from the [[e:del-carretto|Del Carretto]] marquises and became a self-governing commune in 1192. It soon placed itself under the protection of the [[s:republic-of-genoa|Republic of Genoa]] while keeping its own institutions.
republic-of-noli.r: Noli was governed by consuls and later by a council and podestà, and lived from fishing, shipbuilding and sea trade. Its ships joined Genoese expeditions, including crusading voyages. In 1239 [[e:pope-gregory-ix|Pope Gregory IX]] made it a bishopric, a sign of its standing. The town kept its medieval walls, towers and the Romanesque church of [[e:san-paragorio|San Paragorio]].
republic-of-noli.e: Noli survived as a nominal republic allied to [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] for six centuries. It was absorbed into the French-backed [[s:ligurian-republic|Ligurian Republic]] in 1797.

republic-of-lydenburg.t: A breakaway Boer republic in the eastern Transvaal that resisted union with Pretoria for four years.
republic-of-lydenburg.o: [[e:voortrekkers|Voortrekkers]] abandoned malaria-ridden [[e:ohrigstad|Andries-Ohrigstad]] and founded [[e:lydenburg|Lydenburg]] in 1849. Its leaders distrusted [[e:marthinus-wessel-pretorius|Marthinus Wessel Pretorius]] and the western [[s:south-african-republic|Transvaal]], and in 1856 the Lydenburg community declared itself a separate republic, De Republiek Lydenburg in Zuid-Afrika.
republic-of-lydenburg.r: The small republic had its own [[e:volksraad|Volksraad]] and a church tradition closer to the [[e:dutch-reformed-church|Dutch Reformed]] establishment of the Cape. Its farmers lived from [[e:cattle|cattle]], hunting and trade towards [[e:delagoa-bay|Delagoa Bay]], and lived alongside the [[s:pedi-kingdom|Pedi Kingdom]] to the west, with whom relations were uneasy.
republic-of-lydenburg.e: [[e:lydenburg|Lydenburg]] absorbed the [[s:republic-of-utrecht|Republic of Utrecht]] in 1858, and in 1860 the combined state rejoined the [[s:south-african-republic|South African Republic]]. The town remained a district centre and later a base in wars against the Pedi.

revolutionary-serbia.t: Insurgent Serbian state of the First Serbian Uprising, which drove out Ottoman janissaries and laid the foundations of modern Serbia.
revolutionary-serbia.o: In 1801 renegade [[e:janissaries|janissaries]], the dahije, seized power in the [[e:sanjak-of-smederevo|Pashalik of Belgrade]] and terrorised the Serbian population. After they murdered dozens of Serbian notables, an assembly at [[e:orasac|Orašac]] in February 1804 chose [[e:karadorde|Karađorđe Petrović]] to lead a revolt. The uprising soon turned against Ottoman rule itself, winning battles at [[e:battle-of-ivankovac|Ivankovac]] in 1805 and [[e:battle-of-misar|Mišar]] in 1806.
revolutionary-serbia.r: The insurgents took [[e:belgrade|Belgrade]] in 1806 and created a Governing Council in 1805, alongside assemblies of local leaders and [[e:karadorde|Karađorđe's]] growing personal power as supreme leader. [[e:russia|Russia]] supported them during its war with the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]]. The scholar [[e:dositej-obradovic|Dositej Obradović]] became the first minister of education, and a Great School opened in Belgrade in 1808.
revolutionary-serbia.e: When [[e:russia|Russia]] made peace at [[e:treaty-of-bucharest-1812|Bucharest]] in 1812 to face [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]], the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] reconquered [[s:serbia|Serbia]] in 1813 and [[e:karadorde|Karađorđe]] fled to [[e:austria|Austria]]. The [[e:second-serbian-uprising|Second Serbian Uprising]] of 1815 under [[e:milos-obrenovic|Miloš Obrenović]] led to the autonomous [[s:principality-of-serbia|Principality of Serbia]].

republic-of-zamboanga.t: Short-lived revolutionary republic in western Mindanao, formed as Spanish rule collapsed in 1899.
republic-of-zamboanga.o: [[e:zamboanga-city|Zamboanga]] was the main Spanish stronghold in [[e:mindanao|Mindanao]]. In 1899, as [[e:spain|Spain]] prepared to withdraw after ceding the islands, local revolutionaries under General [[e:vicente-alvarez|Vicente Alvarez]] fought the garrison, and after the Spanish departure in May they proclaimed a republic with Alvarez as president.
republic-of-zamboanga.r: The republic governed the Christian, Chavacano-speaking town and its surroundings, but it was divided by rivalries between revolutionary factions and with neighbouring Muslim datus, who distrusted a Christian-led government. [[e:vicente-alvarez|Alvarez]] was ousted, and [[e:isidoro-midel|Isidoro Midel]] led the government that negotiated with the Americans.
republic-of-zamboanga.e: [[e:isidoro-midel|Midel]] surrendered [[e:zamboanga-city|Zamboanga]] to American forces in November 1899. A local government using the republic's name survived under American supervision until 1903, when Zamboanga became the capital of the new [[s:moro-province|Moro Province]].

rauracian-republic.t: Short-lived revolutionary republic in the Jura, the first sister republic created by the French Revolution.
rauracian-republic.o: The French army occupied the northern part of the [[s:prince-bishopric-of-basel|Prince-Bishopric of Basel]] in 1792, driving out the prince-[[e:bishop|bishop]]. Local revolutionaries proclaimed the Rauracian Republic on 27 November 1792 at [[e:porrentruy|Porrentruy]], naming it after the [[s:raurici|Rauraci]], a Celtic people of the area recorded by Caesar.
rauracian-republic.r: The republic had a national assembly and adopted French revolutionary institutions, but it was deeply divided between those who wanted independence and those who sought union with [[e:france|France]]. It depended entirely on the French army and had no real independent existence; most of its history consists of debates over annexation.
rauracian-republic.e: On 23 March 1793 the [[e:national-convention|French National Convention]] annexed the territory as the [[e:departement|department]] of [[e:mont-terrible|Mont-Terrible]]. It later merged into [[e:haut-rhin|Haut-Rhin]], and in 1815 the area was given to the Swiss canton of Bern, much of it now forming the canton of [[e:jura-mountains|Jura]].

recuay.t: A highland culture of Peru's Callejón de Huaylas known for fine kaolin pottery, stone sculpture of warriors and elite residences built around fortified compounds.
recuay.o: The Recuay culture arose around the start of the Common Era in the [[e:callejon-de-huaylas|Callejón de Huaylas]] and the upper valleys of [[e:ancash-region|Ancash]], in the same region where [[s:chavin|Chavín]] had flourished. Communities built hilltop settlements and stone compounds above the [[e:santa-river-peru|Santa]] river valley.
recuay.r: Recuay society was led by local chiefs and warrior elites who lived in walled compounds and were buried in stone tombs with offerings. Herding of llamas and alpacas and high-altitude farming supported the economy. The culture is known for white kaolin pottery painted in red and black, often modelled as figures of chiefs, women and llamas, and for stone sculptures and lintels showing warriors with shields and trophy heads. Its contacts with the [[s:moche|Moche]] on the coast were close.
recuay.e: Recuay declined around 600 to 700 CE, possibly under pressure from the expanding [[s:wari-empire|Wari Empire]], whose influence reached [[e:ancash-region|Ancash]]. Its stone sculpture tradition remained a reference point for later highland cultures.

republic-of-austria.t: The Second Austrian Republic, restored in 1945 and rebuilt as a neutral, prosperous democracy in the heart of Europe.
republic-of-austria.o: As the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] took [[e:vienna|Vienna]] in April 1945, [[e:karl-renner|Karl Renner]] formed a provisional government and declared [[e:austria|Austria's]] independence from [[e:germany|Germany]] on 27 April 1945, restoring the 1920 constitution. Austria was divided into four Allied occupation zones, with Vienna under four-power control.
republic-of-austria.r: Governments were long formed by grand coalitions of the conservative [[e:austrian-peoples-party|People's Party]] and the Social Democrats, with social partnership between employers and unions. The [[e:austrian-state-treaty|State Treaty]] of 15 May 1955 ended the occupation, and [[e:austria|Austria]] declared permanent neutrality. [[e:vienna|Vienna]] became a seat of [[e:united-nations|United Nations]] agencies. The [[e:waldheim-affair|Waldheim affair]] of 1986 prompted a reckoning with Austrians' role under [[e:nazism|Nazism]].
republic-of-austria.e: [[e:austria|Austria]] joined the [[e:european-union|European Union]] in 1995 and adopted the euro in 1999. It remains a federal parliamentary republic of nine states, with [[e:vienna|Vienna]] as capital.

restored-hanthawaddy-kingdom.t: A Mon revival kingdom in Lower Burma that captured Ava in 1752, ending the Toungoo dynasty, but fell to Alaungpaya five years later.
restored-hanthawaddy-kingdom.o: In 1740 the [[e:mon-people|Mon]] of [[e:lower-burma|Lower Burma]], together with [[e:karen-people|Karen]] and Burmese allies, rebelled against the weakened [[s:restored-toungoo-kingdom|Restored Toungoo Kingdom]]. They chose [[e:smim-htaw|Smim Htaw]], a former monk, as king at [[e:bago|Pegu]], reviving the name of the old [[s:hanthawaddy-kingdom|Hanthawaddy Kingdom]].
restored-hanthawaddy-kingdom.r: [[e:smim-htaw|Smim Htaw]] was replaced in 1747 by [[e:binnya-dala|Binnya Dala]], who with French assistance from [[e:pondicherry|Pondicherry]] built up an army and in 1752 captured Ava, deporting the last Toungoo king. The kingdom's base remained the [[e:mon-people|Mon]] delta ports, where French and British traders competed for influence.
restored-hanthawaddy-kingdom.e: [[e:alaungpaya|Alaungpaya]], a village headman of [[e:shwebo|Moksobo]], raised an army in [[e:upper-burma|Upper Burma]], retook Ava at the start of 1754 and swept south, capturing [[s:portuguese-syriam|Syriam]] and finally [[e:bago|Pegu]] in 1757. The capital was sacked and many [[e:mon-people|Mon]] fled to Siam. [[e:lower-burma|Lower Burma]] became part of the [[s:konbaung-dynasty|Konbaung dynasty]].

republic-of-san-marco.t: The revolutionary Venetian republic of 1848–1849 led by Daniele Manin, which held out against an Austrian siege for seventeen months.
republic-of-san-marco.o: As revolution spread across [[e:europe|Europe]], crowds freed the lawyer [[e:daniele-manin|Daniele Manin]] from prison on 17 March 1848, and on 22 March the [[e:venice|Venetians]] rose against the [[s:kingdom-of-lombardy-venetia|Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia]] and took the Arsenal. Manin proclaimed the Republic of San Marco, reviving the name of the old [[s:republic-of-venice|Republic of Venice]].
republic-of-san-marco.r: [[e:daniele-manin|Manin]] led the government, with the writer [[e:niccolo-tommaseo|Niccolò Tommaseo]] among its ministers. The republic briefly voted in July 1848 to join the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]], but after [[e:piedmont|Piedmont's]] defeat at [[e:battle-of-custoza-1848|Custoza]] it returned to independence. [[e:venice|Venetians]] raised loans, printed [[e:paper-money|paper money]] and organised a national guard and defence of the lagoon, which became a symbol of Italian resistance.
republic-of-san-marco.e: Austrian forces besieged [[e:venice|Venice]] from 1849, bombarding the city while cholera and hunger spread. The republic surrendered in August 1849, and [[e:daniele-manin|Manin]] went into exile in [[e:paris|Paris]]. [[e:venetia|Venetia]] joined the [[s:kingdom-of-italy|Kingdom of Italy]] in 1866.

ryukyu-kingdom.t: The island kingdom of Okinawa that thrived as a trading hub between China, Japan and Southeast Asia for four centuries before Japanese annexation.
ryukyu-kingdom.o: [[e:sho-hashi|Sho Hashi of Chuzan]] completed the unification of [[e:okinawa-island|Okinawa]] in 1429 by conquering [[s:nanzan|Nanzan]], and ruled from Shuri castle as a tributary king of [[e:ming-empire|Ming China]]. In 1470 a coup brought [[e:sho-en|Sho En]] to power, founding the [[e:second-sho-dynasty|Second Sho dynasty]] that reigned until the end.
ryukyu-kingdom.r: King [[e:sho-shin|Sho Shin]] centralised power by bringing local aji lords to live at Shuri and organised priestesses under a royal high priestess. Ryukyu prospered as an [[e:entrepot|entrepot]], carrying Chinese [[e:silk|silk]] and ceramics, Japanese swords and Southeast Asian [[e:spice-trade|spices]] and sappanwood. After the [[s:satsuma-domain|Satsuma Domain]] invaded in 1609, Ryukyu secretly paid tribute to [[e:satsuma-domain|Satsuma]] while remaining a Chinese tributary, and a distinctive court culture of dance, lacquer and textiles developed.
ryukyu-kingdom.e: [[e:empire-of-japan|Meiji Japan]] made the kingdom the [[s:ryukyu-domain|Ryukyu Domain]] in 1872, and [[e:sho-tai|King Sho Tai]] lost his throne when it was annexed as [[e:okinawa-prefecture|Okinawa Prefecture]] in 1879.

rajpur-state-kathiawar.t: A minor chiefship of the Kathiawar peninsula, one of its many small hereditary estates.
rajpur-state-kathiawar.o: Rajpur was a small estate in [[e:kathiawar|Kathiawar]] held by a local chiefly family from around 1700. Its founding is not well documented.
rajpur-state-kathiawar.r: The ruler held a handful of villages and, after 1807, came under British supervision in the [[e:kathiawar-agency|Kathiawar Agency]]. Little else is recorded in standard works.
rajpur-state-kathiawar.e: Rajpur merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960.

reichskommissariat-norwegen.t: German civilian occupation regime in Norway in 1940-1945, headed by Josef Terboven, with Vidkun Quisling's collaborationist government.
reichskommissariat-norwegen.o: [[e:germany|Germany]] invaded [[e:norway|Norway]] on 9 April 1940. [[e:vidkun-quisling|Vidkun Quisling]], leader of the fascist [[e:nasjonal-samling|Nasjonal Samling]], proclaimed himself head of government the same day, but the Germans soon pushed him aside. [[e:haakon-vii|King Haakon VII]] and the government refused to surrender and went into exile in [[e:london|London]], and in April 1940 [[e:adolf-hitler|Hitler]] appointed [[e:josef-terboven|Josef Terboven]] as [[e:reichskommissar|Reich Commissioner]].
reichskommissariat-norwegen.r: [[e:josef-terboven|Terboven]] held real power from [[e:oslo|Oslo]], banning all parties except [[e:nasjonal-samling|Nasjonal Samling]]. In 1942 [[e:vidkun-quisling|Quisling]] became Minister-President of a collaborationist government, which tried to Nazify schools and the church but met mass resistance from teachers and clergy. [[e:norway|Norway's]] resistance sabotaged the heavy water plant at [[e:vemork|Vemork]], and in 1942 Norwegian [[e:jews|Jews]] were deported to [[e:auschwitz-concentration-camp|Auschwitz]].
reichskommissariat-norwegen.e: German forces in [[e:norway|Norway]] surrendered on 8 May 1945, and [[e:josef-terboven|Terboven]] killed himself. [[e:vidkun-quisling|Quisling]] was tried and executed in October 1945, and his name became a byword for traitor. The legal government returned and [[e:haakon-vii|King Haakon VII]] came home to the [[s:kingdom-of-norway|Kingdom of Norway]] in June 1945.

republic-of-amalfi.t: Maritime republic on the Sorrento peninsula whose merchants traded with Constantinople, Egypt and Jerusalem in the 10th and 11th centuries.
republic-of-amalfi.o: Amalfi was a small fortified town on the steep coast of the [[e:sorrento|Sorrento]] peninsula, part of the [[e:duchy-of-naples|Byzantine Duchy of Naples]]. In 839, after the [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] prince [[e:sicard-of-benevento|Sicard of Benevento]] had attacked it and taken its people away, the Amalfitans broke from [[e:naples|Naples]] and elected their own leaders, first [[e:prefect|prefects]] and later judges.
republic-of-amalfi.r: From 958 Amalfi was ruled by dukes, among them Manso I, who also controlled [[s:principality-of-salerno|Salerno]]. With little farmland, it lived from trade: its merchants had colonies in [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]], [[s:principality-of-antioch|Antioch]] and [[e:cairo|Cairo]] and founded a hospital in [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] from which the [[e:knights-hospitaller|Knights Hospitaller]] later emerged. It minted gold tari, and the maritime code known as the [[e:tabula-amalphitana|Tabula Amalphitana]] was used across the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]].
republic-of-amalfi.e: [[e:robert-guiscard|Robert Guiscard]] took Amalfi in 1073. It revolted and was absorbed by [[e:roger-ii-of-sicily|Roger II]]'s [[s:kingdom-of-sicily|Kingdom of Sicily]] in 1131. [[e:pisa|Pisa]] sacked it in 1135 and 1137, and a storm in 1343 destroyed much of the lower town. Its cathedral and the [[e:amalfi-coast|Amalfi Coast]] are now famous.

republic-of-indian-stream.t: A tiny self-governing republic on the disputed border between New Hampshire and Lower Canada, home to about 300 settlers.
republic-of-indian-stream.o: The [[e:treaty-of-paris-1783|Treaty of Paris]] of 1783 set the border at the 'northwesternmost head of the [[e:connecticut-river|Connecticut River]]', which could be read as several different streams. Settlers in the disputed valley found themselves taxed and called for service by both the [[s:united-states|United States]] and British [[s:lower-canada|Lower Canada]]. In 1832 they adopted a constitution and declared their own republic.
republic-of-indian-stream.r: Indian Stream was governed by an assembly of all adult male citizens, an elected council and its own courts, and it promised to last only until the boundary was settled. Its inhabitants were farmers and lumbermen. Divisions grew between residents loyal to [[e:new-hampshire|New Hampshire]] and those leaning to [[s:province-of-canada|Canada]], and an arrest by a New [[e:hampshire|Hampshire]] sheriff's deputy sparked clashes in 1835.
republic-of-indian-stream.e: [[e:new-hampshire|New Hampshire]] sent militia in 1835 and annexed the territory in 1836. The [[e:webster-ashburton-treaty|Webster-Ashburton Treaty]] of 1842 confirmed it as American. The area is now the town of [[e:pittsburg-new-hampshire|Pittsburg, New Hampshire]].

republic-of-mulhouse.t: A Protestant city-republic in Alsace allied to the Swiss, which grew rich on printed cotton and chose to join France in 1798.
republic-of-mulhouse.o: Mulhouse was an imperial town in [[e:upper-alsace|Upper Alsace]] that gradually freed itself from local lords and, by the mid-14th century, governed itself through a council and mayor under the emperor. In 1354 it joined the [[s:decapole|Décapole]], the league of ten Alsatian imperial cities.
republic-of-mulhouse.r: Threatened by the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]], Mulhouse allied with [[s:canton-of-basel|Basel]] and the Swiss cantons, becoming an associate of the [[s:swiss-confederation|Swiss Confederation]] in 1515 and leaving the [[s:decapole|Décapole]]. It adopted the Reformed faith in the 1520s. From 1746 its merchants founded calico-[[e:printing-press|printing]] works, making printed [[e:cotton|cotton]], the indiennes, the basis of a major textile industry.
republic-of-mulhouse.e: Surrounded by French territory and strangled by customs barriers after the Revolution, the citizens voted in January 1798 to join the [[s:french-first-republic|French First Republic]]. Mulhouse became a leading French industrial city.

republic-of-hawaii.t: The oligarchic republic proclaimed by the overthrow's leaders in 1894, which held Hawaii until it was annexed by the United States in 1898.
republic-of-hawaii.o: When President [[e:grover-cleveland|Grover Cleveland]] refused to annex [[e:hawaii|Hawaii]], the [[s:provisional-government-of-hawaii|Provisional Government of Hawaii]] called a constitutional convention. The new constitution was proclaimed on 4 July 1894, creating a republic with [[e:sanford-b-dole|Sanford B. Dole]] as president.
republic-of-hawaii.r: The constitution restricted voting through property, income and literacy tests and loyalty oaths, excluding most [[e:native-hawaiians|Native Hawaiians]] and all Asian immigrants. Power stayed with the American-descended business elite tied to [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]]. In January 1895 royalists led by [[e:robert-william-wilcox|Robert Wilcox]] attempted a counter-revolution, which failed; Liliʻuokalani was arrested, forced to abdicate and imprisoned in [[e:iolani-palace|ʻIolani Palace]]. Japanese and Chinese labour remained central to the plantations.
republic-of-hawaii.e: The [[e:spanish-american-war|Spanish-American War]] made [[e:hawaii|Hawaii]] strategically valuable, and after a treaty failed in the Senate despite petitions by many [[e:native-hawaiians|Native Hawaiians]], Congress annexed the islands by the [[e:newlands-resolution|Newlands Resolution]] in July 1898. [[e:sovereignty|Sovereignty]] was transferred on 12 August 1898, and the islands became the [[s:territory-of-hawaii|Territory of Hawaii]].
