republic-of-new-granada.t: The centralist republic formed from Gran Colombia's core around Bogotá, during which Colombia's Liberal and Conservative parties were born.
republic-of-new-granada.o: After [[s:venezuela|Venezuela]] and [[s:republic-of-ecuador|Ecuador]] left [[s:gran-colombia|Gran Colombia]] in 1830, the remaining provinces, including [[s:republic-of-panama|Panama]], formed the Republic of New Granada under a constitution of 1832. [[e:francisco-de-paula-santander|Francisco de Paula Santander]] returned from exile and served as president from 1832 to 1837.
republic-of-new-granada.r: The republic faced regional revolts, notably the [[e:war-of-the-supremes|War of the Supremes]] from 1839 to 1842. Colombia's Liberal and Conservative parties emerged in 1848 and 1849. The liberal president [[e:jose-hilario-lopez|José Hilario López]] carried out major reforms, abolishing [[e:slavery|slavery]] in 1851 and expelling the [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]]. The [[e:panama-railroad|Panama Railway]], completed in 1855 during the [[e:california|California]] gold rush, made the isthmus a world trade route. The constitution of 1853 introduced [[e:universal-suffrage|universal male suffrage]].
republic-of-new-granada.e: Pressure for federalism grew, and [[s:republic-of-panama|Panama]] became a self-governing state in 1855. The constitution of 1858 turned the republic into the [[s:granadine-confederation|Granadine Confederation]]. Its Liberal and Conservative parties dominated Colombian politics into the 21st century.

reichskommissariat-ostland.t: Nazi German occupation regime of the Baltic states and western Belarus from 1941 to 1945, scene of some of the largest massacres of the Holocaust.
reichskommissariat-ostland.o: After the invasion of the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] in 1941, [[e:germany|Germany]] placed the occupied Baltic states and western [[e:belarus|Belarus]] under a civil administration, Reichskommissariat Ostland, created in July 1941 under Alfred Rosenberg's [[e:reich-ministry-for-the-occupied-eastern-territories|Ministry for the Occupied Eastern Territories]]. [[e:hinrich-lohse|Hinrich Lohse]] became [[e:reichskommissar|Reich Commissioner]], with his seat in Riga.
reichskommissariat-ostland.r: Ostland was divided into general commissariats for [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]], [[s:republic-of-latvia|Latvia]], [[s:republic-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] and White Ruthenia, each with local auxiliary administrations. The occupiers exploited labour and food and planned eventual German colonisation. [[e:holocaust|The Holocaust]] was carried out on a vast scale: [[e:jews|Jews]] were murdered at [[e:rumbula-massacre|Rumbula]] near Riga, [[e:ponary-massacre|Ponary]] near [[e:vilnius|Vilnius]], the Ninth Fort in [[e:kaunas|Kaunas]] and [[e:maly-trostenets|Maly Trostenets]] near [[e:minsk|Minsk]].
reichskommissariat-ostland.e: Soviet offensives in 1944 retook most of the territory, and [[e:hinrich-lohse|Lohse]] fled. German forces trapped in the [[e:courland-pocket|Courland Pocket]] held out until May 1945. The region returned to Soviet rule as the Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republics and [[s:byelorussian-ssr|Soviet Belarus]].

riau-lingga-sultanate.t: Malay sultanate of the Riau islands, a centre of Malay literature under its Bugis viceroys until the Dutch deposed its last sultan.
riau-lingga-sultanate.o: The [[e:anglo-dutch-treaty-of-1824|Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824]] split the old [[s:johor-sultanate|Johor-Riau]] realm. The mainland and [[s:singapore|Singapore]] fell in the British sphere, while the [[e:riau-archipelago|Riau]] and [[e:lingga-islands|Lingga]] islands stayed with the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] under a separate line of sultans based at [[e:daik|Daik]] on Lingga, descended from the Bendahara dynasty of [[e:johor|Johor]].
riau-lingga-sultanate.r: Real power lay with the [[e:yang-dipertuan-muda|Yang Dipertuan Muda]], [[e:bugis|Bugis]] [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroys]] based on [[e:penyengat|Penyengat]] island. Gambier and [[e:pepper|pepper]] planted by Chinese settlers on Bintan funded the court. Penyengat became a cradle of Malay letters, where [[e:raja-ali-haji|Raja Ali Haji]] wrote the [[e:gurindam-dua-belas|Gurindam Dua Belas]] and an early Malay grammar, laying foundations for standard Malay.
riau-lingga-sultanate.e: Growing friction with the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] led them to depose [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:abdul-rahman-muazzam-shah|Abdul Rahman Muazzam Shah]] in 1911; he fled to [[s:singapore|Singapore]] and the sultanate was formally abolished in 1913, its lands absorbed into the [[s:dutch-east-indies|Dutch East Indies]]. [[e:riau-malay|Riau Malay]] later became the basis of Indonesian.

ranasan-state.t: A minor chiefship of the Mahi Kantha country in northern Gujarat, known mainly from colonial lists of tributary estates.
ranasan-state.o: Ranasan was one of the many petty holdings of the [[e:mahi-kantha-agency|Mahi Kantha]] region, held by a local [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] or Koli family from around 1600. Its founding is not well documented.
ranasan-state.r: Its Thakor ruled a few villages, paid tribute through the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads of Baroda]] and was supervised by the [[e:mahi-kantha-agency|British Mahi Kantha Agency]]. Standard references record little about its rulers.
ranasan-state.e: Ranasan was merged into [[s:bombay-presidency|Bombay Province]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960.

republic-of-mountainous-armenia.t: An anti-Bolshevik Armenian state in Zangezur, led by Garegin Nzhdeh in 1921, whose resistance helped keep the region within Armenia.
republic-of-mountainous-armenia.o: After the [[s:armenian-ssr|Armenian SSR]] replaced the [[s:first-republic-of-armenia|First Republic of Armenia]] in December 1920, the southern mountain district of [[e:zangezur|Zangezur]], defended by the commander [[e:garegin-nzhdeh|Garegin Nzhdeh]], refused to accept Soviet rule. Following the failed February 1921 uprising in [[e:yerevan|Yerevan]], the anti-Bolshevik forces retreated there and in April 1921 proclaimed an autonomous [[s:kingdom-of-syunik|Syunik]], renamed the Republic of Mountainous [[s:armenia|Armenia]] in June, with its seat at [[e:goris|Goris]].
republic-of-mountainous-armenia.r: The republic was a wartime state led by [[e:garegin-nzhdeh|Nzhdeh]] as commander and later prime minister, with [[e:simon-vratsian|Simon Vratsian]] and other former leaders of the [[s:french-first-republic|First Republic]]. It relied on local militias and the mountainous terrain of [[s:kingdom-of-syunik|Syunik]] and controlled a population swollen with refugees. It sought union with the rest of [[s:armenia|Armenia]] once free of Bolshevik rule.
republic-of-mountainous-armenia.e: In July 1921, after the Soviets reportedly promised to keep [[e:zangezur|Zangezur]] in [[s:armenian-ssr|Soviet Armenia]], the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] took the region and [[e:garegin-nzhdeh|Nzhdeh]] withdrew to [[e:iran|Iran]]. The area remained part of the Armenian SSR.

rampur-state.t: The Rohilla Nawabi state of Rampur in Rohilkhand, the only Rohilla principality to survive and home of the Raza Library.
rampur-state.o: After the British-backed Nawab of [[e:awadh|Awadh]] defeated the [[e:rohillas|Rohillas]] in 1774, the Rohilla chief [[e:faizullah-khan|Faizullah Khan]], son of [[e:ali-mohammed-khan|Ali Muhammad Khan]], was allowed to keep Rampur and surrounding lands by the [[e:treaty-of-lal-dhang|Treaty of Lal Dhang]]. He founded the city and a library that became the [[e:raza-library|Raza Library]].
rampur-state.r: Rampur stayed loyal to the British in 1857 and was rewarded with land. Nawabs such as [[e:kalb-ali-khan|Kalb Ali Khan]] and [[e:hamid-ali-khan-of-rampur|Hamid Ali Khan]] patronised [[e:urdu|Urdu]] poetry, Hindustani music and scholarship, making Rampur a refuge for artists from [[e:delhi|Delhi]] and [[e:lucknow|Lucknow]]. The state had a 15-gun salute and a roughly equal [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] and Muslim population.
rampur-state.e: [[e:raza-ali-khan|Raza Ali Khan]] acceded to [[e:india|India]], and Rampur was merged into [[e:uttar-pradesh|Uttar Pradesh]] in 1949. The [[e:raza-library|Raza Library]], with its Persian [[e:manuscript|manuscripts]] and Mughal paintings, is now a national institution.

republic-of-tucuman.t: A short-lived provincial republic in northwestern Argentina created by the caudillo Bernabé Aráoz during the anarchy of 1820.
republic-of-tucuman.o: After central government in the [[s:united-provinces-of-the-rio-de-la-plata|United Provinces of the Río de la Plata]] collapsed in 1820, the governor of Tucumán, [[e:bernabe-araoz|Bernabé Aráoz]], proclaimed the Republic of Tucumán. It claimed the provinces of Tucumán, [[e:catamarca-province|Catamarca]] and [[e:santiago-del-estero|Santiago del Estero]], and adopted a constitution that year.
republic-of-tucuman.r: [[e:bernabe-araoz|Aráoz]] governed as supreme president, seeking to keep the northern provinces together under Tucumán's leadership. [[e:santiago-del-estero|Santiago del Estero]], under [[e:juan-felipe-ibarra|Juan Felipe Ibarra]], rejected his authority and declared its own autonomy, and the two sides went to war. [[e:catamarca-province|Catamarca]] also broke away. The republic faced constant conflict with [[e:salta|Salta]], governed by [[e:martin-miguel-de-guemes|Martín Miguel de Güemes]].
republic-of-tucuman.e: [[e:bernabe-araoz|Aráoz]] was overthrown in 1821, and the republic dissolved into the separate provinces of Tucumán, [[e:catamarca-province|Catamarca]] and [[e:santiago-del-estero|Santiago del Estero]], which later joined the [[s:argentine-confederation|Argentine Confederation]]. Aráoz was executed in 1824.

republic-of-san-marino.t: Tiny republic on Monte Titano that claims to be the oldest surviving sovereign state and republic in the world, traditionally founded in 301.
republic-of-san-marino.o: Tradition holds that [[e:saint-marinus|Saint Marinus]], a Christian stonemason from the island of Rab in [[e:dalmatia|Dalmatia]], founded a monastic community on [[e:monte-titano|Monte Titano]] on 3 September 301 to escape persecution under [[e:diocletian|Diocletian]]. A self-governing community around the monastery and fortress is documented from the early [[e:middle-ages|Middle Ages]], with an assembly of household heads, the [[e:arengo-san-marino|Arengo]].
republic-of-san-marino.r: San Marino has been governed since at least the 13th century by two Captains Regent elected every six months, with a Great and General Council as legislature. Its statutes of 1600 served as a written constitution. It kept its independence through its mountain position, alliances with the [[e:house-of-montefeltro|Montefeltro]] and recognition by the [[e:papacy|Papacy]] in 1631. [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]] and Italian are dominant; the economy today rests on tourism, banking and stamps.
republic-of-san-marino.e: San Marino survived the occupation by [[e:giulio-alberoni|Cardinal Alberoni]] in 1739–40, declined [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] offer of more territory in 1797, sheltered [[e:giuseppe-garibaldi|Garibaldi]] in 1849 and was left independent at Italian unification. It joined the [[e:council-of-europe|Council of Europe]] in 1988 and the [[e:united-nations|United Nations]] in 1992.

rewa-state.t: The kingdom of the Baghel Rajputs, which gave its name to Baghelkhand, sent the singer Tansen to Akbar's court and whose Maharaja captured Mohan, ancestor of most captive white tigers.
rewa-state.o: The [[e:baghel|Baghel Rajputs]], a branch of the Solanki clan of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]], moved into the region in the 13th century; tradition credits Vyaghra Deva with the founding. Their early stronghold was the hill fort of [[e:bandhavgarh|Bandhogarh]] (Bandhavgarh).
rewa-state.r: Raja [[e:ramchandra-singh-of-rewa|Ramchandra]] was patron of the musician [[e:tansen|Tansen]], who left his court for [[e:akbar|Akbar's]] in the 1560s. [[e:bandhavgarh|Bandhogarh]] was taken by the [[e:mughal-empire|Mughals]] in 1597, and the capital moved to Rewa. The state was large and rural, with forests rich in game. In 1812 Rewa entered treaty relations with the British, and its rulers later sent troops to help against the rebels of 1857.
rewa-state.e: In 1948 Rewa became the leading member and capital of [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]], which merged into [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]] in 1956. In 1951 [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]] [[e:martand-singh|Martand Singh]] captured the white tiger Mohan, ancestor of many captive white tigers.

rogaland.t: West Norwegian kingdom whose seat at Avaldsnes guarded the Karmsund strait, the 'north way' that gave Norway its name.
rogaland.o: Rogaland, around modern [[e:stavanger|Stavanger]], was home to a powerful [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] elite. At [[e:avaldsnes|Avaldsnes]] on [[e:karmoy|Karmøy]], great mounds and a ship burial of the late 8th century mark a seat of kings who controlled shipping through the narrow [[e:karmsund|Karmsund]] strait along the coast.
rogaland.r: Control of the sea route allowed the rulers to tax or plunder traffic passing north and south. The district had good farmland on [[e:jaeren|Jæren]] and close links across the [[e:north-sea|North Sea]]. Its kings, known only from the sagas, were rivals of the kings of [[s:vestfold|Vestfold]].
rogaland.e: The decisive [[e:battle-of-hafrsfjord|Battle of Hafrsfjord]], traditionally dated around 872, was fought in Rogaland, where [[e:harald-fairhair|Harald Fairhair]] defeated the western kings. He made [[e:avaldsnes|Avaldsnes]] one of his royal residences, and Rogaland became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-norway|Kingdom of Norway]].

rohilla-state.t: An Afghan state in the plains of Rohilkhand, north-east of Delhi, built by Rohilla soldiers in the decline of the Mughal Empire.
rohilla-state.o: Afghan soldiers, known as [[e:rohillas|Rohillas]], settled in the [[e:katehr|Katehr]] region east of the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges]] from the late 17th century. [[e:ali-mohammed-khan|Ali Muhammad Khan]], adopted son of a Rohilla chief, built a power base there from the 1720s, making [[e:aonla|Aonla]] his capital, and was recognised by the Mughal court as nawab.
rohilla-state.r: After [[e:ali-mohammed-khan|Ali Muhammad]]'s death in 1748, [[e:hafiz-rahmat-khan|Hafiz Rahmat Khan]] ruled as regent for his sons and led a confederacy of [[e:rohillas|Rohilla]] chiefs from [[e:bareilly|Bareilly]]. The Rohillas supported [[e:ahmad-shah-abdali|Ahmad Shah Durrani]] at the [[e:third-battle-of-panipat|Third Battle of Panipat]] in 1761. They promoted Afghan settlement, built towns and mosques, and patronised Persian and [[e:pashto|Pashto]] learning.
rohilla-state.e: In 1774 the Nawab of the [[s:awadh-state|Awadh State]], with [[e:east-india-company|East India Company]] troops, defeated and killed [[e:hafiz-rahmat-khan|Hafiz Rahmat Khan]] in the [[e:rohilla-war|Rohilla War]]. Most of [[e:rohilkhand|Rohilkhand]] was annexed to [[e:awadh|Awadh]], while the [[e:rohillas|Rohilla]] chief [[e:faizullah-khan|Faizullah Khan]] kept the small state of [[s:rampur-state|Rampur]].

republic-of-aras.t: A short-lived Muslim republic in Nakhchivan and the Araxes valley, set up in 1918 to resist incorporation into Armenia.
republic-of-aras.o: After the Ottoman withdrawal from the [[e:south-caucasus|South Caucasus]] at the end of the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]], the mainly Muslim population of [[e:nakhchivan|Nakhchivan]], [[e:sharur-district|Sharur]] and [[e:ordubad|Ordubad]], backed by former Ottoman officers, proclaimed the Republic of Aras in November 1918 to block the claims of the [[s:first-republic-of-armenia|First Republic of Armenia]] to these districts.
republic-of-aras.r: The republic was led by [[e:jafar-qulu-khan-nakhchivanski|Jafar Qulu Khan Nakhchivanski]], of the family of the former khans of [[e:nakhchivan|Nakhichevan]], and had a small administration and militias drawn from the local Muslim population. It sought union with the [[s:azerbaijan-democratic-republic|Azerbaijan Democratic Republic]] or Ottoman protection and contested control of villages with Armenian forces amid widespread intercommunal violence and refugee movements.
republic-of-aras.e: In 1919 British forces and then Armenian troops took control of [[e:nakhchivan|Nakhchivan]], ending the republic. After further fighting, Nakhchivan became an autonomous republic within [[s:azerbaijan-ssr|Soviet Azerbaijan]] in the 1920s, an exclave status it keeps today.

royal-prussia.t: The western part of Prussia that rebelled against the Teutonic Knights and lived for three centuries under the Polish Crown, keeping its own diet and privileges.
royal-prussia.o: In 1454 the towns and nobles of the Prussian Confederation rose against the [[s:state-of-the-teutonic-order|State of the Teutonic Order]] and placed themselves under King [[e:casimir-iv-jagiellon|Casimir IV of Poland]]. After the Thirteen Years' War, the [[e:second-peace-of-thorn|Second Peace of Thorn]] in 1466 gave [[e:poland|Poland]] [[e:pomerelia|Pomerelia]], [[e:chelmno-land|Chelmno Land]], [[e:malbork|Malbork]], [[e:elblag|Elblag]] and the [[s:prince-bishopric-of-warmia|Prince-Bishopric of Warmia]], which together formed Royal [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]].
royal-prussia.r: Royal [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] kept wide autonomy, with its own diet, council and laws, and its great cities of Gdansk, [[e:torun|Torun]] and [[e:elblag|Elblag]] were largely German-speaking and Lutheran after the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]]. Gdansk shipped Polish grain to [[e:amsterdam|Amsterdam]] and became the Commonwealth's richest city. [[e:nicolaus-copernicus|Nicolaus Copernicus]] was born in Torun in 1473. After the [[e:union-of-lublin|Union of Lublin]] in 1569 the province was drawn more closely into the Crown.
royal-prussia.e: The [[e:first-partition-of-poland|First Partition of Poland]] in 1772 gave most of Royal [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] to the [[s:kingdom-of-prussia|Kingdom of Prussia]], which made it the province of [[e:west-prussia|West Prussia]], and Gdansk and [[e:torun|Torun]] followed in 1793. Gdansk later became the [[s:free-city-of-danzig-1807-1814|Free City of Danzig]] (1807-1814).

republic-of-winburg.t: One of the first Voortrekker states north of the Orange River, a loose Boer community between the Vet and Vaal rivers.
republic-of-winburg.o: [[e:voortrekkers|Voortrekkers]] under [[e:andries-hendrik-potgieter|Andries Hendrik Potgieter]] obtained land between the [[e:vet-river|Vet]] and [[e:vaal-river|Vaal]] rivers from the Taung chief Makwana in 1836. After the defeat of [[e:ndebele-kingdom|Mzilikazi's Ndebele]] in 1837, a settlement was laid out whose name, Winburg, is said to recall that victory.
republic-of-winburg.r: Government was a simple [[e:volksraad|Volksraad]] of elected [[e:burghers|burghers]] with a commandant leading the commando. The farmers raised [[e:cattle|cattle]] and sheep and dealt with [[e:sotho-people|Sotho]] and [[e:tswana-people|Tswana]] neighbours by treaty and raid. From 1843 Winburg was loosely joined with the settlements north of the [[e:vaal-river|Vaal]] as [[s:potchefstroom-republic|Potchefstroom-Winburg]].
republic-of-winburg.e: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] declared the [[s:orange-river-sovereignty|Orange River Sovereignty]] in 1848 and defeated [[e:andries-pretorius|Andries Pretorius]] at [[e:battle-of-boomplaats|Boomplaats]]. Winburg came under British rule and was later part of the [[s:orange-free-state|Orange Free State]].

rhodes.t: Island republic created in 408 BCE that became the leading Hellenistic naval and commercial power of the eastern Mediterranean, home of the Colossus.
rhodes.o: The three old Dorian cities of the island, [[s:ialysos|Ialysos]], [[s:kamiros|Kamiros]] and [[s:lindos|Lindos]], joined in 408-407 BCE to found a single new city of Rhodes at the island's northern tip. Laid out on a regular grid with fine harbours, it quickly drew population and trade, while the old towns survived as districts of the unified state.
rhodes.r: Rhodes was governed by an assembly, council and annual prytaneis, with a moderate democracy that favoured its wealthy shipowners. It lived by trade in grain and wine, policed the sea against [[e:piracy|pirates]], and its maritime law influenced later [[e:roman-law|Roman law]]. Withstanding the siege of [[e:demetrius-i-of-macedon|Demetrius Poliorcetes]] in 305-304 BCE, it built the [[e:colossus-of-rhodes|Colossus]]. Its schools of rhetoric and philosophy attracted [[e:roman-empire|Romans]].
rhodes.e: Siding with [[e:rome|Rome]] against Philip V and [[e:antiochus-iii-the-great|Antiochus III]] won Rhodes lands in [[s:hecatomnid-caria|Caria]] and [[s:lycian-dynasts|Lycia]], but Rome punished its wavering by making [[s:delos|Delos]] a free port in 167 BCE. [[e:gaius-cassius-longinus|Cassius]] sacked it in 43 BCE. [[e:claudius|Claudius]] withdrew its freedom in 44 CE; restored in 53 CE, it was lost for good under Vespasian.

roman-republic-1798-1799.t: A French-sponsored republic proclaimed in Rome in 1798 after Pope Pius VI was deposed and sent into exile.
roman-republic-1798-1799.o: After the French general [[e:mathurin-leonard-duphot|Duphot]] was killed in a riot in [[e:rome|Rome]] in December 1797, French troops under General [[e:louis-alexandre-berthier|Berthier]] occupied the city. On 15 February 1798 a republic was proclaimed in the [[e:roman-forum|Forum]], ending the temporal power of the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]]. [[e:pope-pius-vi|Pope Pius VI]] was deported and died in exile at [[e:valence|Valence]] in 1799.
roman-republic-1798-1799.r: The republic adopted a constitution modelled on the [[s:french-first-republic|French Directory]] but using ancient Roman titles, with consuls, a senate and a tribunate. It absorbed the [[s:anconine-republic|Anconine Republic]] and the [[s:tiberina-republic|Tiberina Republic]]. French commissioners controlled it, heavy levies and confiscations of art and church property caused hardship, and peasant revolts broke out.
roman-republic-1798-1799.e: In November 1798 the [[s:kingdom-of-naples|Kingdom of Naples]] briefly occupied [[e:rome|Rome]]. As the French retreated from [[e:italy|Italy]] in 1799, Neapolitan troops ended the republic in September, and the [[e:papacy|papacy]] was restored under [[e:pope-pius-vii|Pius VII]].

republic-of-anguilla.t: Self-declared republic of a small Caribbean island that rebelled against rule from Saint Kitts and, unusually, asked to stay British.
republic-of-anguilla.o: Anguillians had long resented being governed from [[e:basseterre|Basseterre]] as part of [[s:saint-christopher-nevis-anguilla|Saint Christopher-Nevis-Anguilla]]. When the colony became an [[e:west-indies-associated-states|Associated State]] in 1967, islanders expelled the [[s:colony-of-saint-christopher|Saint Kitts]] police on 30 May 1967, and a referendum in July voted for separation. [[e:ronald-webster|Ronald Webster]] emerged as the leader of the movement.
republic-of-anguilla.r: An island council under [[e:ronald-webster|Webster]] ran affairs, with little money and a few thousand people living from fishing, salt and remittances. Negotiations with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] produced an interim arrangement, but when it broke down [[e:anguilla|Anguilla]] declared itself a republic in February 1969 and expelled a British envoy. Its aim was not independence for its own sake but freedom from [[s:colony-of-saint-christopher|Saint Kitts]], preferably under direct British rule.
republic-of-anguilla.e: On 19 March 1969 British paratroopers and [[e:london|London]] police landed unopposed in [[e:operation-sheepskin|Operation Sheepskin]], an episode widely mocked in the press. A British commissioner took over, the [[e:anguilla|Anguilla]] Act of 1971 confirmed direct rule, and Anguilla was formally separated in 1980. It is now a [[e:british-overseas-territories|British Overseas Territory]].

rapa-nui.t: The Polynesian society of Easter Island, the most remote inhabited island in the Pacific, famous for its giant moai statues and the undeciphered rongorongo script.
rapa-nui.o: Polynesian voyagers reached [[e:easter-island|Rapa Nui]] around 1200, probably from eastern [[e:polynesia|Polynesia]] via [[e:mangareva|Mangareva]] or the [[e:marquesas-islands|Marquesas]]. Island tradition names the founding chief as [[e:hotu-matua|Hotu Matuʻa]], who landed at [[e:anakena|Anakena Bay]] and divided the land among his sons, ancestors of the island's clans. Over the next centuries the population grew to several thousand.
rapa-nui.r: Kin groups (mata) each held a wedge of coast and built stone platforms (ahu) carrying moai carved from the [[e:rano-raraku|Rano Raraku]] crater, nearly 900 in all. A paramount ariki of the Miru clan held sacred rank. Later the [[e:tangata-manu|Tangata manu]] or birdman cult at [[e:orongo|Orongo]] chose a yearly leader through a race to collect the first sooty tern egg. People farmed sweet [[e:potato|potato]] in stone-mulched gardens and rock shelters on a largely treeless island.
rapa-nui.e: [[e:jacob-roggeveen|Jacob Roggeveen]] arrived on Easter Day 1722. Peruvian slave raids in 1862 and the [[e:smallpox|smallpox]] that followed cut the population to around 110 by 1877. In 1888 [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]] annexed the island through an agreement between [[e:policarpo-toro|Policarpo Toro]] and the ariki [[e:atamu-tekena|Atamu Tekena]]. [[e:easter-island|Rapa Nui]] remains part of Chile.

republic-of-biak-na-bato.t: Short-lived revolutionary republic proclaimed by Emilio Aguinaldo in the hills of Bulacan, with the first Filipino constitution.
republic-of-biak-na-bato.o: After Spanish offensives drove the revolutionaries from Cavite in 1897, [[e:emilio-aguinaldo|Emilio Aguinaldo]] retreated to the caves of Biak-na-Bato in [[e:san-miguel-bulacan|San Miguel, Bulacan]]. There, on 1 November 1897, his followers adopted a provisional constitution drafted by Isabelo Artacho and Felix Ferrer, modelled on a Cuban revolutionary charter.
republic-of-biak-na-bato.r: The constitution created a Supreme Council with [[e:emilio-aguinaldo|Aguinaldo]] as president, declared separation from [[e:spain|Spain]] and guaranteed basic rights such as freedom of religion. In practice the republic controlled little beyond its mountain base and the [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrilla]] bands loyal to it, and it lacked money and arms.
republic-of-biak-na-bato.e: Exhausted, both sides accepted the [[e:pact-of-biak-na-bato|Pact of Biak-na-Bato]], mediated by [[e:pedro-paterno|Pedro Paterno]] in December 1897. [[e:emilio-aguinaldo|Aguinaldo]] and other leaders went into exile in [[e:hong-kong|Hong Kong]] in return for payment, ending the republic. Aguinaldo returned in 1898 to found the [[s:revolutionary-government-of-the-philippines|Revolutionary Government of the Philippines]].

republic-of-yemen.t: The unified Yemeni state created in 1990, troubled by civil wars and since 2014 divided by a devastating conflict.
republic-of-yemen.o: On 22 May 1990 the [[s:yemen-arab-republic|Yemen Arab Republic]] and [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]] united as the Republic of [[e:yemen|Yemen]], with [[e:ali-abdullah-saleh|Ali Abdullah Saleh]] as president, [[e:ali-salim-al-beidh|Ali Salim al-Beidh]] as vice-president and Sanaa as capital. Unification was rushed, and the two armies and administrations were never fully merged.
republic-of-yemen.r: In 1994 southern leaders tried to secede; northern forces won a short civil war and took [[e:aden|Aden]]. [[e:ali-abdullah-saleh|Saleh]] ruled through patronage among tribes, the army and his party, while oil revenues declined. In the north the [[e:houthi-movement|Houthi movement]] fought six wars with the government from 2004. [[e:yemen|Yemen]] remained the poorest country in the Arab world.
republic-of-yemen.e: After the 2011 uprising [[e:ali-abdullah-saleh|Saleh]] handed power to [[e:abd-rabbuh-mansur-hadi|Abd Rabbuh Mansur Hadi]]. The [[e:houthi-movement|Houthis]] seized Sanaa in 2014, and a Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015. The war caused a severe humanitarian crisis; since 2022 a Presidential Leadership Council has led the recognised government.

republic-of-egypt.t: Modern republican Egypt, founded after the 1952 revolution, a leading Arab state under Nasser, Sadat, Mubarak and their successors.
republic-of-egypt.o: After the Free Officers overthrew [[e:farouk-of-egypt|King Farouk]] in 1952, they abolished the [[s:kingdom-of-egypt|Kingdom of Egypt]] on 18 June 1953, proclaiming a republic with [[e:muhammad-naguib|Muhammad Naguib]] as president. [[e:gamal-abdel-nasser|Gamal Abdel Nasser]] sidelined Naguib in 1954 and became president in 1956.
republic-of-egypt.r: [[e:gamal-abdel-nasser|Nasser]] nationalised the [[e:suez-canal|Suez Canal]] in 1956, surviving the [[e:suez-crisis|Anglo-French-Israeli invasion]], built the Aswan High Dam and pursued Arab socialism and [[e:pan-arabism|pan-Arabism]], merging with [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] as the [[s:united-arab-republic|United Arab Republic]] from 1958 to 1961. After defeat in 1967, [[e:anwar-sadat|Anwar Sadat]] fought the 1973 war and made peace with [[s:kingdom-of-israel|Israel]] in 1979. [[e:hosni-mubarak|Hosni Mubarak]] ruled from 1981 for three decades.
republic-of-egypt.e: [[e:hosni-mubarak|Mubarak]] fell in the 2011 uprising. The elected president [[e:mohamed-morsi|Mohamed Morsi]] was removed by the army in 2013, and [[e:abdel-fattah-el-sisi|Abdel Fattah el-Sisi]] has ruled since 2014. The Arab Republic of [[e:egypt|Egypt]] remains the most populous Arab state.

cr.a: See File history below for details.

roxolani.t: A Sarmatian people of the steppe between the Don and the Danube, famous for heavy cavalry and repeated raids on Roman Moesia.
roxolani.o: The Roxolani were one of the main Sarmatian tribes, first recorded between the [[e:don-river|Don]] and the [[e:dnieper|Dnieper]] in the 2nd century BCE. Under their leader Tasius they fought on the Scythian side against [[e:diophantes|Diophantes]], general of [[e:mithridates-vi-of-pontus|Mithridates VI]], around 107 BCE. Over the following century they moved west towards the lower [[e:danube|Danube]].
roxolani.r: Like other [[s:sarmatians|Sarmatians]] they were mounted pastoralists ruled by kings and nobles. Roman writers describe their [[e:lance|lancers]] in scale armour, terrifying in a charge but helpless when unhorsed. Their relations with [[e:rome|Rome]] swung between raids across the [[e:danube|Danube]] and treaties paid for with [[e:subsidy|subsidies]].
roxolani.e: In 69 CE a large Roxolani raid into [[e:moesia|Moesia]] was destroyed in winter, and Hadrian later restored payments to their king Rasparaganus. Gothic expansion in the 3rd century and the Hunnic invasion of the 370s broke them up, and their remnants merged with [[e:goths|Goths]], [[s:alans|Alans]] and [[e:huns|Huns]].

robogdii.t: People of the north coast of Ireland recorded by Ptolemy, near a headland he called Robogdium, probably in County Antrim.
robogdii.o: The Robogdii are known only from [[e:geography-ptolemy|Ptolemy's Geography]] of about 150, which places them on the north coast of Ireland. A nearby headland, Robogdium Promontorium, is usually identified with Fair Head or a neighbouring point in north [[e:county-antrim|Antrim]], facing [[e:kintyre|Kintyre]] across the [[e:north-channel|North Channel]].
robogdii.r: Nothing is recorded of their rulers, settlements or customs. Their coast lay only a short sea crossing from [[e:scotland|Scotland]], a route that in later centuries carried the [[s:dal-riata|Dál Riata]] between [[e:county-antrim|Antrim]] and [[e:argyll|Argyll]], and similar close contact across the channel was probably already important in their time.
robogdii.e: The Robogdii are not mentioned again, and no Irish population name has been securely matched with theirs. North [[e:county-antrim|Antrim]] later formed part of the lands of [[s:dal-riata|Dál Riata]] and the [[s:dal-naraidi|Dal nAraidi]].

republic-of-cuba.t: Revolutionary Cuba since 1959, the only communist state in the Americas, ruled by Fidel and Raúl Castro and their successors for over six decades.
republic-of-cuba.o: [[e:fidel-castro|Fidel Castro's]] 26th of July Movement overthrew [[e:fulgencio-batista|Fulgencio Batista]], who fled on 1 January 1959. [[s:duchy-of-castro|Castro]] became prime minister and launched land reform and nationalisation of American and Cuban businesses. The [[s:united-states|United States]] imposed an embargo, and Castro declared the revolution socialist in April 1961, during the failed [[e:bay-of-pigs-invasion|Bay of Pigs invasion]].
republic-of-cuba.r: [[e:cuba|Cuba]] allied with the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]], and the stationing of Soviet missiles caused the crisis of October 1962. The Communist Party, founded in 1965, rules as the sole party under the 1976 and 2019 constitutions. The state provided free health care and education while suppressing dissent, and over a million Cubans emigrated, many in the [[e:mariel-boatlift|Mariel boatlift]] of 1980. Cuban troops fought in [[s:portuguese-angola|Angola]] and [[s:federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia|Ethiopia]]. [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar]] sold to the Soviet bloc was the economic mainstay.
republic-of-cuba.e: Soviet collapse brought the Special Period of severe shortages in the 1990s. [[e:raul-castro|Raúl Castro]] succeeded [[e:fidel-castro|Fidel]] in 2008, and [[e:miguel-diaz-canel|Miguel Díaz-Canel]] became president in 2018. Mass protests in 2021, blackouts and record emigration mark the republic's current crisis.

cr.a: Miguel Teurbe Tolón and Narciso López

republic-of-nicaragua.t: The independent Nicaraguan state since 1838, shaped by foreign intervention, the Somoza dynasty and the Sandinista revolution.
republic-of-nicaragua.o: Nicaragua was the first state to leave the [[s:federal-republic-of-central-america|Federal Republic of Central America]], on 30 April 1838. The rivalry between liberal León and conservative [[e:granada|Granada]] continued, and in 1852 the small town of [[e:managua|Managua]], between the two, was chosen as a compromise capital.
republic-of-nicaragua.r: Nicaragua's possible canal route drew foreign powers. The American filibuster [[e:william-walker|William Walker]], invited by León's liberals, made himself president in 1856 before a Central American coalition expelled him. Conservative governments then ruled until the liberal [[e:jose-santos-zelaya|José Santos Zelaya]], who took the [[s:mosquito-reserve|Mosquito Reserve]] in 1894. [[s:united-states|United States]] [[e:united-states-marine-corps|Marines]] occupied the country from 1912 to 1933, resisted by [[e:augusto-cesar-sandino|Augusto Sandino]]. The [[e:somoza-family|Somoza family]] ruled from 1936 to 1979.
republic-of-nicaragua.e: The [[e:sandinista-national-liberation-front|Sandinista]] revolution overthrew [[e:anastasio-somoza-debayle|Anastasio Somoza Debayle]] in 1979, followed by the [[e:contras|Contra]] war. [[e:violeta-chamorro|Violeta Chamorro's]] election in 1990 brought peace, but [[e:daniel-ortega|Daniel Ortega]] returned to power in 2007 and has since ruled in an increasingly authoritarian manner.

rajahnate-of-butuan.t: A gold-working trading state in northeastern Mindanao, which sent embassies to Song China from 1001 and built the famous balangay boats.
rajahnate-of-butuan.o: Butuan grew at the mouth of the Agusan River, where excavations have found plank boats called balangay, some dated to the 4th century and later. In 1001 it sent its first mission to the [[e:song-dynasty|Song]] court, and Chinese records name rulers who sought the same status as [[s:champa|Champa]].
rajahnate-of-butuan.r: Butuan's wealth came from gold, worked into fine jewellery and regalia found in large hoards, and from trade with [[e:china|China]], [[s:champa|Champa]] and the Malay world. In 1007 its ruler Kiling asked for equal rank with [[e:champa|Champa]], and in 1011 [[e:sri-bata-shaja|Sri Bata Shaja]] sent another embassy. The [[e:golden-tara-of-agusan|Golden Tara of Agusan]] suggests [[e:hindu-buddhist|Hindu-Buddhist]] influence.
rajahnate-of-butuan.e: Butuan's prominence faded by the 14th century as trade shifted to [[e:cebu|Cebu]] and Sulu. [[e:rajah-siagu|Rajah Siagu]] met [[e:ferdinand-magellan|Ferdinand Magellan's]] expedition in 1521. Butuan came gradually under Spanish rule, and its archaeology is now central to Philippine national history.

republic-of-panama.t: Isthmian republic created in 1903 with US backing to build the Panama Canal, which it finally took full control of in 1999.
republic-of-panama.o: Panama had been part of [[s:republic-of-colombia|Colombia]] since 1821. When the Colombian senate rejected the [[e:hay-herran-treaty|Hay-Herrán Treaty]] for a canal, Panamanian leaders, encouraged by [[e:philippe-bunau-varilla|Philippe Bunau-Varilla]] and protected by US warships, declared independence on 3 November 1903. Weeks later the [[e:hay-bunau-varilla-treaty|Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty]] granted the [[s:united-states|United States]] the [[s:panama-canal-zone|Panama Canal Zone]].
republic-of-panama.r: [[e:manuel-amador-guerrero|Manuel Amador Guerrero]] became the first president, and the canal, opened in 1914, dominated the economy and politics. The [[s:united-states|United States]] intervened repeatedly in early decades. [[e:arnulfo-arias|Arnulfo Arias]] was elected and overthrown three times. In 1968 the [[e:national-guard-panama|National Guard]] seized power, and [[e:omar-torrijos|Omar Torrijos]] negotiated the [[e:torrijos-carter-treaties|Torrijos-Carter Treaties]] of 1977, which provided for the canal's transfer. Ship registration, banking and the [[e:colon-free-zone|Colón Free Zone]] diversified the economy.
republic-of-panama.e: After [[e:manuel-noriega|Manuel Noriega's]] rule, the [[s:united-states|United States]] invaded in December 1989 and removed him. Democracy was restored, and Panama took full control of the canal on 31 December 1999. An expanded canal with larger locks opened in 2016.

rawwadid-emirate.t: An Arab-Kurdish dynasty that ruled Tabriz and Azerbaijan in the late 10th and 11th centuries until the Seljuk Turks absorbed it.
rawwadid-emirate.o: The Rawwadids descended from an Arab family of the Azd tribe settled near [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]] in the 8th century, which became Kurdified over time. In the 950s Muhammad ibn Husayn al-Rawwadi made himself master of Tabriz, and around 981 his successors took over the remaining lands of the [[s:sallarid-emirate|Sallarid Emirate]].
rawwadid-emirate.r: The [[e:emir|emirs]] ruled north-western [[e:iran|Iran]] from [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]], which grew into a major city, and fought the Armenian kingdoms and [[e:georgians|Georgians]]. [[e:abul-hayja-wahsudan|Abu'l-Hayja Wahsudan]], who ruled from about 1019, welcomed the poet [[e:qatran-tabrizi|Qatran Tabrizi]], whose verses record the destructive earthquake of 1042 at Tabriz.
rawwadid-emirate.e: Wahsudan submitted to the [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuk Turks]] under [[e:tughril|Tughril Beg]] in 1054, and the dynasty became Seljuk [[e:vassal|vassals]]. [[e:alp-arslan|Alp Arslan]] removed the last emir in 1071, and [[s:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]] passed directly under [[s:seljuk-empire|Seljuk Empire]] rule.

republic-of-pechina.t: A self-governing community of Andalusi sailors near Almería that traded across the Mediterranean and founded Oran in 902.
republic-of-pechina.o: Around 884 a community of Andalusi seafarers, the bahriyyun, settled at [[e:pechina|Bajjana]] (Pechina) in the lower [[e:andarax|Andarax]] valley near [[e:almeria|Almería]], with the permission of the emir and alongside local Arab families. They formed a self-governing body during the decline of central authority in [[e:al-andalus|al-Andalus]].
republic-of-pechina.r: [[e:pechina|Pechina]] was run by a council of sailors rather than a single ruler, recognising the emir only nominally. It lived from maritime trade with [[e:north-africa|North Africa]], and its sailors founded trading posts on the African coast, including [[e:oran|Oran]] in 902. [[e:almeria|Almería]] served as its harbour and watchtower, and the town grew wealthy as a port for the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]].
republic-of-pechina.e: [[e:abd-al-rahman-iii|Abd al-Rahman III]] brought [[e:pechina|Pechina]] under direct control around 922. Its harbour, [[e:almeria|Almería]], then eclipsed it, becoming the main naval base of the [[s:caliphate-of-cordoba|Caliphate of Córdoba]], and Pechina declined into a village.

republic-of-acre.t: A short-lived state proclaimed by Brazilian rubber tappers in Bolivian territory, whose struggle ended with Brazil buying Acre in 1903.
republic-of-acre.o: During the [[e:amazon|Amazon]] [[e:rubber|rubber]] boom, thousands of Brazilian rubber tappers settled in [[e:acre|Acre]], which belonged to [[s:republic-of-bolivia|Bolivia]] by treaty. When [[e:bolivia|Bolivia]] set up a customs post at [[e:puerto-alonso|Puerto Alonso]] in 1899, the Spanish adventurer [[e:luis-galvez-rodriguez-de-arias|Luis Gálvez Rodríguez de Arias]], backed by local interests, proclaimed the Independent State of Acre on 14 July 1899.
republic-of-acre.r: [[e:luis-galvez-rodriguez-de-arias|Gálvez]] declared himself president and set up ministries and decrees in [[e:puerto-alonso|Puerto Alonso]], intending eventual union with [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]]. [[e:brazil|Brazil]], which still recognised Bolivian [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]], sent a force that removed him in 1900. Conflict revived in 1902 when [[s:republic-of-bolivia|Bolivia]] leased the region to an Anglo-American company, the Bolivian Syndicate, and the Brazilian [[e:placido-de-castro|José Plácido de Castro]] led an armed uprising of [[e:rubber|rubber]] tappers.
republic-of-acre.e: [[e:placido-de-castro|Plácido de Castro]] took [[e:puerto-alonso|Puerto Alonso]] in 1903, and [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] occupied the territory. By the [[e:treaty-of-petropolis|Treaty of Petrópolis]] in 1903 the [[s:republic-of-bolivia|Republic of Bolivia]] ceded [[e:acre|Acre]] to [[e:brazil|Brazil]] for £2 million and the promise of the [[e:madeira-mamore-railway|Madeira-Mamoré]] railway.

roman-republic-1849.t: The republic proclaimed in Rome in 1849 and led by Mazzini, whose defence by Garibaldi against French troops became a legend of Italian unification.
roman-republic-1849.o: After the murder of [[e:pope-pius-ix|Pope Pius IX's]] minister [[e:pellegrino-rossi|Pellegrino Rossi]] in November 1848, the pope fled to [[e:gaeta|Gaeta]] in the [[s:kingdom-of-the-two-sicilies|Kingdom of the Two Sicilies]]. An elected Constituent Assembly met in [[e:rome|Rome]] and on 9 February 1849 abolished the temporal power of the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]] and proclaimed a republic.
roman-republic-1849.r: A triumvirate of [[e:giuseppe-mazzini|Giuseppe Mazzini]], [[e:aurelio-saffi|Aurelio Saffi]] and [[e:carlo-armellini|Carlo Armellini]] governed. The republic abolished the death penalty, introduced religious freedom and drafted a democratic constitution, promulgated on 3 July 1849. [[e:giuseppe-garibaldi|Giuseppe Garibaldi]] led volunteers in defence of the city, notably on the [[e:janiculum|Janiculum]] hill.
roman-republic-1849.e: Louis-[[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] [[e:france|France]] sent an army under General [[e:nicolas-charles-victor-oudinot|Oudinot]], which besieged [[e:rome|Rome]] from June and entered the city in early July 1849. [[e:giuseppe-garibaldi|Garibaldi]] retreated with his volunteers, and papal rule was restored under French protection.

restored-toungoo-kingdom.t: The Burmese kingdom rebuilt from Ava after the collapse of Bayinnaung's empire, with a compact, centralised state that lasted until 1752.
restored-toungoo-kingdom.o: After the [[s:first-toungoo-empire|First Toungoo Empire]] disintegrated in 1599, [[e:nyaungyan-min|Nyaungyan Min]], a son of [[e:bayinnaung|Bayinnaung]], rebuilt royal power from Ava in [[e:upper-burma|Upper Burma]]. His son [[e:anaukpetlun|Anaukpetlun]] retook [[e:lower-burma|Lower Burma]], destroying the [[s:portuguese-syriam|Portuguese Syriam]] of [[e:filipe-de-brito-e-nicote|Filipe de Brito]] in 1613 and reconquering [[s:lan-na|Lan Na]] in 1615.
restored-toungoo-kingdom.r: [[e:thalun|Thalun]], king from 1629, moved the capital back to Ava in 1635, ordered a revenue inquest and organised royal service groups, the ahmudan, to supply soldiers and labour. The state was smaller and more centralised than [[e:bayinnaung|Bayinnaung]]'s empire, ruling Upper and [[e:lower-burma|Lower Burma]], the Shan states and [[s:lan-na|Lan Na]]. Buddhist learning and court literature flourished.
restored-toungoo-kingdom.e: In the 18th century Manipuri raids devastated [[e:upper-burma|Upper Burma]], and in 1740 the [[e:mon-people|Mon]] rose and founded the [[s:restored-hanthawaddy-kingdom|Restored Hanthawaddy Kingdom]]. Its forces captured Ava in 1752, ending the dynasty, but [[e:alaungpaya|Alaungpaya]] then rallied resistance, founding the [[s:konbaung-dynasty|Konbaung dynasty]].

rwanda.t: A small, densely populated republic of the Great Lakes, which suffered the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi and has since been rebuilt under the RPF.
rwanda.o: After the [[e:rwandan-revolution|Hutu revolution]] of 1959 to 1961 abolished the [[s:kingdom-of-rwanda|Kingdom of Rwanda]], the country became independent from [[s:ruanda-urundi|Belgian Ruanda-Urundi]] on 1 July 1962 as a republic led by [[e:gregoire-kayibanda|Gregoire Kayibanda]] and his [[e:parmehutu|Parmehutu]] party. Hundreds of thousands of Tutsi fled abroad as violence against them recurred.
rwanda.r: [[e:gregoire-kayibanda|Kayibanda]]'s [[s:french-first-republic|First Republic]] was overthrown in 1973 by [[e:juvenal-habyarimana|Juvenal Habyarimana]], who ruled a one-party state. In 1990 the [[e:rwandan-patriotic-front|Rwandan Patriotic Front]], formed by Tutsi exiles in [[s:uganda|Uganda]], invaded. After Habyarimana's plane was shot down in April 1994, [[e:hutu|Hutu]] extremists organised a [[e:genocide|genocide]] that killed some 800,000 people, mostly Tutsi, in about 100 days, until the RPF took power in July.
rwanda.e: Under the [[e:rwandan-patriotic-front|RPF]] and [[e:paul-kagame|Paul Kagame]], president since 2000, [[s:kingdom-of-rwanda|Rwanda]] has rebuilt its economy and institutions, held community gacaca courts and switched to English as a main language, while critics point to restrictions on political freedom. It remains a republic with [[e:kigali|Kigali]] as capital.

republic-of-north-ingria.t: Breakaway state of the Ingrian Finns near Petrograd in 1919-1920, backed by Finland and returned to Soviet Russia by the Treaty of Tartu.
republic-of-north-ingria.o: The [[e:ingrian-finns|Ingrian Finns]], Lutheran Finnish-speakers living around [[e:petrograd|Petrograd]], resisted Bolshevik requisitions and conscription. In 1919, with help from [[s:republic-of-finland|Finland]], inhabitants of the northern Ingrian parishes near the Finnish border rose in revolt and declared the Republic of North [[s:swedish-ingria|Ingria]], based in the village of Kirjasalo.
republic-of-north-ingria.r: The small republic had its own government, flag, stamps and an armed force of a few hundred men, and sought union with [[s:republic-of-finland|Finland]]. It controlled only a narrow strip of territory and depended on Finnish supplies and volunteers.
republic-of-north-ingria.e: In the [[e:treaty-of-tartu-finland-russia|Treaty of Tartu]] between [[s:republic-of-finland|Finland]] and [[s:russian-sfsr|Soviet Russia]] in October 1920, [[e:finland|Finland]] agreed to return North [[s:swedish-ingria|Ingria]], while [[e:russia|Russia]] promised the [[e:ingrian-finns|Ingrians]] cultural autonomy. The republic was dissolved in December 1920, and many inhabitants fled to Finland. The promised autonomy was later revoked, and Ingrian [[e:finns|Finns]] suffered [[e:stalinism|Stalinist]] [[e:deportation|deportations]].

republic-of-honduras.t: The independent Honduran state since 1838, the original 'banana republic', shaped by American fruit companies, military rule and Cold War politics.
republic-of-honduras.o: Honduras declared its separation from the [[s:federal-republic-of-central-america|Federal Republic of Central America]] on 26 October 1838. Its early decades were marked by intervention from [[s:republic-of-guatemala|Guatemala]] and [[s:republic-of-nicaragua|Nicaragua]] and by attempts to revive the union. [[e:comayagua|Comayagua]] remained capital until [[e:marco-aurelio-soto|Marco Aurelio Soto]] moved the government to [[e:tegucigalpa|Tegucigalpa]] in 1880.
republic-of-honduras.r: [[e:marco-aurelio-soto|Soto]]'s liberal reforms opened the country to foreign mining and investment. From the 1900s the [[e:united-fruit-company|United Fruit]], Standard Fruit and [[e:cuyamel-fruit-company|Cuyamel]] companies built banana plantations and railways on the north coast and wielded great political influence, inspiring the term 'banana republic'. [[e:tiburcio-carias-andino|Tiburcio Carías Andino]] ruled as dictator from 1933 to 1949. Frequent coups and military governments followed, and in 1969 Honduras fought the brief [[e:football-war|Football War]] with [[s:republic-of-el-salvador|El Salvador]].
republic-of-honduras.e: Civilian rule returned in 1982, while the country served as a base for the [[e:contras|Contras]]. [[e:hurricane-mitch|Hurricane Mitch]] devastated it in 1998. A coup removed President [[e:manuel-zelaya|Manuel Zelaya]] in 2009, and Honduras remains a presidential republic struggling with poverty and violence.

restoration-spain.t: The restored Bourbon monarchy of Alfonso XII and Alfonso XIII, a stable but rigged parliamentary system that lost Spain's last colonies in 1898.
restoration-spain.o: In December 1874 General [[e:arsenio-martinez-campos|Arsenio Martínez Campos]] proclaimed [[e:alfonso-xii|Alfonso XII]], son of [[e:isabella-ii-of-spain|Isabella II]], at [[s:saguntum|Sagunto]], ending the [[s:sexenio-democratico|Sexenio Democrático]]. The conservative statesman [[e:antonio-canovas-del-castillo|Antonio Cánovas del Castillo]] designed the new order and its Constitution of 1876.
restoration-spain.r: Under the turno pacífico, [[e:antonio-canovas-del-castillo|Cánovas]]'s Conservatives and [[e:praxedes-mateo-sagasta|Sagasta]]'s Liberals alternated in power through elections managed by local bosses, the caciques. The system kept order but excluded workers and regionalists. Defeat by the [[s:united-states|United States]] in 1898 cost [[e:cuba|Cuba]], [[e:puerto-rico|Puerto Rico]] and the [[s:philippines|Philippines]], and the Tragic Week of 1909 and the disaster of Annual in [[s:kingdom-of-morocco|Morocco]] in 1921 shook the regime.
restoration-spain.e: [[e:alfonso-xiii|Alfonso XIII]] backed [[e:miguel-primo-de-rivera|Miguel Primo de Rivera's]] dictatorship from 1923 to 1930. After republican victories in the municipal elections of April 1931, the king left [[e:spain|Spain]], and the [[s:second-spanish-republic|Second Spanish Republic]] was proclaimed.

republic-of-formosa.t: A short-lived republic proclaimed on Taiwan in 1895 to resist the island's cession to Japan, among the first republics declared in East Asia.
republic-of-formosa.o: The [[e:treaty-of-shimonoseki|Treaty of Shimonoseki]] of April 1895 forced the [[s:qing-empire|Qing Empire]] to cede [[s:republic-of-china|Taiwan]] to [[e:japan|Japan]] after the [[e:first-sino-japanese-war|First Sino-Japanese War]]. Local [[e:gentry|gentry]] and officials, hoping for foreign intervention, proclaimed the Republic of Formosa on 25 May 1895 with the Qing governor [[e:tang-jingsong|Tang Jingsong]] as president and a tiger flag.
republic-of-formosa.r: The republic was essentially a resistance government. It had a president, a parliament of [[e:gentry|gentry]] and its own stamps and banknotes, but it professed loyalty to the Qing and relied on Chinese garrison troops, local militias and the [[e:black-flag-army|Black Flag Army]] of [[e:liu-yongfu|Liu Yongfu]] in the south.
republic-of-formosa.e: Japanese troops landed at the end of May; [[e:tang-jingsong|Tang Jingsong]] fled to the mainland and [[e:taipei|Taipei]] fell in early June. [[e:liu-yongfu|Liu Yongfu]] continued resistance from [[e:tainan|Tainan]] as leader, but the city fell in October 1895 and he escaped. [[s:taiwan-under-japanese-rule|Taiwan under Japanese rule]] followed.

ranpur-state.t: A small Odisha princely state near Khurda, where a popular uprising in 1939 led to the killing of the British Political Agent.
ranpur-state.o: Ranpur's ruling family claimed very ancient descent, and tradition dates the state to around 1400. Its early history is not reliably documented.
ranpur-state.r: Ranpur was a hilly, wooded state south-west of [[e:cuttack|Cuttack]], tributary first to the kings of [[s:kingdom-of-khurda|Khurda]] and later, from 1803, to the British as one of the [[e:orissa-tributary-states|Orissa Tributary Mahals]]. In January 1939, during agitation by the [[e:praja-mandal|Praja Mandal]] against the Raja's exactions, a crowd killed the Political Agent, Major R. L. Bazalgette; the rising was put down and leaders were hanged.
ranpur-state.e: Ranpur merged into [[e:odisha|Orissa]] on 1 January 1948 and is now in [[s:nayagarh-state|Nayagarh]] district.

republic-of-maldives.t: The Indian Ocean island republic of the Maldives, transformed by tourism and threatened by rising sea levels.
republic-of-maldives.o: After independence from British protection in 1965, a referendum in 1968 abolished the Sultanate of the Maldives and established a presidential republic. [[e:ibrahim-nasir|Ibrahim Nasir]], the former prime minister, became the first president on 11 November 1968, governing the atolls from Male.
republic-of-maldives.r: Nasir developed tourism from 1972 and fishing modernisation. [[e:maumoon-abdul-gayoom|Maumoon Abdul Gayoom]] ruled from 1978 to 2008, surviving a coup attempt in 1988 that was defeated with Indian help, while restricting opposition. [[e:islam|Islam]] is the state religion. The 2004 tsunami devastated many islands, and the low-lying country has become a voice for climate action.
republic-of-maldives.e: A new constitution in 2008 introduced multiparty elections, won by [[e:mohamed-nasheed|Mohamed Nasheed]]. His resignation under pressure in 2012 began a period of political turmoil, and the republic continues with competitive elections.

republic-of-bergamo.t: A republic proclaimed when Bergamo rose against Venetian rule with French backing in March 1797, before joining the Cisalpine Republic.
republic-of-bergamo.o: [[s:commune-of-bergamo|Bergamo]] had been a mainland city of the [[s:republic-of-venice|Republic of Venice]] since 1428. In March 1797, with French troops in the city, local [[e:jacobin-club|Jacobins]] proclaimed Bergamo's independence from [[e:venice|Venice]] and set up a provisional government.
republic-of-bergamo.r: The Bergamasque Republic was a provisional regime of local patriots under French protection. It abolished Venetian institutions, planted liberty trees and sought union with the new republics of [[e:lombardy|Lombardy]]. Its revolt helped trigger risings in [[s:commune-of-brescia|Brescia]] and [[e:crema|Crema]], which weakened [[e:venice|Venice]] in the last weeks before its fall.
republic-of-bergamo.e: [[e:venice|Venice]] fell in May 1797, and later that year [[s:commune-of-bergamo|Bergamo]] was united to the [[s:cisalpine-republic|Cisalpine Republic]], created by [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]].

rharhabe-xhosa-kingdom.t: The western Xhosa kingdom between the Kei and Fish rivers, which bore the brunt of the frontier wars with the Cape Colony.
rharhabe-xhosa-kingdom.o: Rharhabe, a son of [[e:phalo|Phalo]], quarrelled with his brother [[s:gcaleka-xhosa-kingdom|Gcaleka]] and led followers west of the Kei, founding a separate kingdom when the [[s:xhosa-kingdom|Xhosa Kingdom]] split around 1775. His successors ruled the [[e:xhosa-people|Xhosa]] closest to the advancing Cape frontier.
rharhabe-xhosa-kingdom.r: The kingdom was weakened by rivalry between the regent [[e:ndlambe|Ndlambe]] and Rharhabe's grandson [[e:ngqika|Ngqika]], who sought British support; Ndlambe's forces defeated Ngqika at the [[e:battle-of-amalinde|Battle of Amalinde]] in 1818. Under Ngqika's sons [[e:maqoma|Maqoma]] and [[e:sandile|Sandile]], the Rharhabe fought repeated frontier wars, losing land as the Cape pushed its border from the Fish to the [[e:keiskamma-river|Keiskamma]] and beyond.
rharhabe-xhosa-kingdom.e: After the War of the Axe, [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] annexed the territory between the [[e:keiskamma-river|Keiskamma]] and Kei as [[s:british-kaffraria|British Kaffraria]] in 1847, ending Rharhabe independence. [[e:sandile|Sandile]] was killed in 1878 during the last frontier war.

republic-of-utrecht.t: A tiny Boer republic on the Buffalo River, created on land obtained from the Zulu king Mpande.
republic-of-utrecht.o: In 1854 [[e:boers|Boer]] farmers obtained a strip of land along the Buffalo River on the [[e:zulu-kingdom|Zulu]] border from King [[e:mpande|Mpande]] and founded the village of [[s:lordship-of-utrecht|Utrecht]], organising themselves as a small independent republic.
republic-of-utrecht.r: Little is known beyond its simple [[e:volksraad|Volksraad]] government and a population of a few hundred farming families, who depended on good relations with the [[s:zulu-kingdom|Zulu Kingdom]].
republic-of-utrecht.e: [[s:lordship-of-utrecht|Utrecht]] joined the [[s:republic-of-lydenburg|Republic of Lydenburg]] in 1858, and with it entered the [[s:south-african-republic|South African Republic]] in 1860. The district's border with [[s:zulu-kingdom|Zululand]] remained disputed, a grievance behind the [[e:anglo-zulu-war|Anglo-Zulu War]] of 1879.

riograndense-republic.t: A breakaway republic in southern Brazil born of the Ragamuffin War, which fought the empire for nearly a decade and gave Garibaldi his first battles.
riograndense-republic.o: In September 1835 ranchers of [[e:rio-grande-do-sul|Rio Grande do Sul]], angry at imperial taxes that favoured imported jerked beef, rose against the [[e:brazilian-empire|Empire of Brazil]] under [[e:bento-goncalves|Bento Gonçalves]] in the [[e:ragamuffin-war|Ragamuffin War]], or Farroupilha. After victory at [[e:battle-of-seival|Seival]], [[e:antonio-de-sousa-neto|Antônio de Sousa Neto]] proclaimed the Riograndense Republic on 11 September 1836.
riograndense-republic.r: [[e:bento-goncalves|Bento Gonçalves]] served as president, and the republic's capital moved between [[e:piratini|Piratini]], [[e:cacapava-do-sul|Caçapava]] and [[e:alegrete|Alegrete]] as fighting shifted. It was run by a ranching elite and recruited gauchos and enslaved black soldiers, the [[e:lanceiros-negros|Lanceiros Negros]], promising them freedom. The Italian revolutionary [[e:giuseppe-garibaldi|Giuseppe Garibaldi]] fought for it, leading an expedition that created the [[s:juliana-republic|Juliana Republic]] in 1839.
riograndense-republic.e: The imperial commander [[e:luis-alves-de-lima-e-silva-duke-of-caxias|Luís Alves de Lima e Silva]], later Duke of Caxias, combined military pressure with negotiation, and the [[e:treaty-of-ponche-verde|Treaty of Ponche Verde]] on 1 March 1845 ended the war with an amnesty. The republic's flag inspired the flag of [[e:rio-grande-do-sul|Rio Grande do Sul]].

republic-of-the-rio-grande.t: Federalist breakaway republic in northeastern Mexico, proclaimed at Laredo in January 1840 and defeated within the year.
republic-of-the-rio-grande.o: Opposition to the [[s:centralist-republic-of-mexico|Centralist Republic of Mexico]] ran deep in the northern frontier states of [[e:tamaulipas|Tamaulipas]], [[e:nuevo-leon|Nuevo León]] and [[e:coahuila|Coahuila]]. In January 1840 federalist leaders meeting near [[e:laredo|Laredo]] declared an independent republic, naming [[e:jesus-de-cardenas|Jesús de Cárdenas]] president and [[e:antonio-canales-rosillo|Antonio Canales]] commander of its army, with [[e:antonio-zapata|Antonio Zapata]] as a leading officer.
republic-of-the-rio-grande.r: The republic existed mainly as a military campaign. Its leaders hoped to restore the federal Constitution of 1824, and some sought help from the [[s:republic-of-texas|Republic of Texas]], recruiting Texan volunteers. Its government moved between [[e:laredo|Laredo]], Guerrero and other border towns, and it never controlled the main cities of the region or collected regular revenues.
republic-of-the-rio-grande.e: Centralist forces under [[e:mariano-arista|Mariano Arista]] defeated the rebels; [[e:antonio-zapata|Zapata]] was captured and executed in March 1840. [[e:antonio-canales-rosillo|Canales]] surrendered in November 1840 and later served the Mexican government. The flag of the republic is still displayed in [[e:laredo|Laredo]], [[e:texas|Texas]], as one of the city's historic flags.

republic-of-genoa-1814.t: A brief restoration of the old Genoese republic under British protection in 1814, before the Congress of Vienna gave Genoa to Piedmont.
republic-of-genoa-1814.o: In April 1814 British forces under [[e:lord-william-bentinck|Lord William Bentinck]] landed and took [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] from the French. Bentinck, hoping to rally Italians against [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]], proclaimed the restoration of the Republic of [[e:genoa|Genoa]] under its constitution as it stood before 1797, with a provisional government led by [[e:girolamo-serra|Girolamo Serra]].
republic-of-genoa-1814.r: The provisional government tried to revive the institutions of the old aristocratic republic and lobbied the allied powers for recognition. It controlled [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] and the Ligurian coast but had no army of its own and relied on British protection.
republic-of-genoa-1814.e: The great powers had already decided to strengthen [[e:piedmont|Piedmont]] as a barrier against [[e:france|France]]. The [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] gave [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] to the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]], which took possession in January 1815, despite Genoese protests.

russian-america.t: Russia's only overseas colony, a chain of fur-trading posts in Alaska run by the Russian-American Company until the territory was sold to the United States.
russian-america.o: After [[e:vitus-bering|Vitus Bering's]] voyage of 1741, Siberian traders hunted sea otters in the [[e:aleutian-islands|Aleutian Islands]], and [[e:grigory-shelikhov|Grigory Shelikhov]] founded a permanent settlement on [[e:kodiak-island|Kodiak Island]] in 1784. In 1799 [[e:paul-i-of-russia|Emperor Paul I]] granted a monopoly charter to the [[e:russian-american-company|Russian-American Company]], which was to govern the territory on the state's behalf.
russian-america.r: The Company's chief managers ruled from [[e:kodiak-island|Kodiak]] and, from 1808, from [[e:sitka|New Archangel]] (Sitka), built by [[e:alexander-baranov|Alexander Baranov]] after the [[e:tlingit|Tlingit]] destroyed an earlier fort in 1802. [[e:aleut|Aleut]] and [[e:alutiiq|Alutiiq]] hunters were forced to hunt sea otters, whose pelts were sold to [[e:china|China]]. The colony depended on imported food and briefly ran [[e:fort-ross|Fort Ross]] in [[e:california|California]]. [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] missionaries, including [[e:innocent-of-alaska|Innocent Veniaminov]], converted many Native people.
russian-america.e: With sea otters depleted and [[e:russia|Russia]] fearing it could not defend [[e:alaska|Alaska]] against [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] after the Crimean War, the territory was sold to the [[s:united-states|United States]] in 1867 for $7.2 million. The [[e:russian-orthodox-church|Russian Orthodox Church]] remains a lasting legacy in Alaska.

republic-of-pernambuco.t: A short-lived republic proclaimed in Recife in 1817, the first serious attempt to break part of Brazil away from the Portuguese crown.
republic-of-pernambuco.o: Pernambuco's planters and merchants resented the heavy taxes imposed to support the royal court in [[e:rio-de-janeiro|Rio de Janeiro]], and Masonic lodges spread liberal and republican ideas. On 6 March 1817 officers resisting arrest killed their commander in [[e:recife|Recife]], and a provisional republican government took power.
republic-of-pernambuco.r: The provisional government, including the merchant [[e:domingos-jose-martins|Domingos José Martins]] and the priest [[e:joao-ribeiro|João Ribeiro]], abolished some taxes, proclaimed freedom of conscience and the press, and drafted an organic law. It sent an envoy, [[e:antonio-goncalves-da-cruz|Antônio Gonçalves da Cruz]], to seek recognition from the [[s:united-states|United States]]. The revolt spread to [[e:paraiba|Paraíba]] and [[e:rio-grande-do-norte|Rio Grande do Norte]], but [[e:slavery|slavery]] was left untouched to keep planter support.
republic-of-pernambuco.e: Royal forces of the [[s:kingdom-of-brazil|Kingdom of Brazil]] blockaded [[e:recife|Recife]] by sea and advanced overland from [[e:bahia|Bahia]]. The republic fell in May 1817, after about 75 days. Several leaders, including [[e:domingos-jose-martins|Martins]], were executed, and others, such as [[e:frei-caneca|Frei Caneca]], imprisoned, later joining the [[s:confederation-of-the-equator|Confederation of the Equator]].

republic-of-south-vietnam.t: The provisional revolutionary government set up by the communist-led National Liberation Front in 1969, which formally ruled the south after Saigon's fall.
republic-of-south-vietnam.o: In June 1969 the [[e:viet-cong|National Liberation Front]] and allied groups formed the Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of [[s:republic-of-vietnam|South Vietnam]] to give the southern insurgency a governmental form for negotiations. It was led by the architect [[e:huynh-tan-phat|Huynh Tan Phat]], with [[e:nguyen-huu-tho|Nguyen Huu Tho]] as head of its advisory council.
republic-of-south-vietnam.r: The PRG operated from jungle bases near the Cambodian border and later in liberated zones, rather than a fixed capital. It was a party to the [[e:paris|Paris]] peace talks, where [[e:nguyen-thi-binh|Nguyen Thi Binh]] served as foreign minister and signed the 1973 accords. It was recognised by many communist and non-aligned states, though it was controlled by the Workers' Party in [[e:hanoi|Hanoi]].
republic-of-south-vietnam.e: After the fall of [[e:ho-chi-minh-city|Saigon]] on 30 April 1975 the PRG became the nominal government of the south. [[e:hanoi|Hanoi]] moved quickly to reunification, and on 2 July 1976 it merged with the [[s:democratic-republic-of-vietnam|Democratic Republic of Vietnam]] to form the [[s:socialist-republic-of-vietnam|Socialist Republic of Vietnam]].

royal-audiencia-of-charcas.t: The Spanish high court and province of Upper Peru, home to the silver mountain of Potosí, from which the Republic of Bolivia emerged.
royal-audiencia-of-charcas.o: The [[e:silver|silver]] deposits of [[e:cerro-rico|Cerro Rico]] at [[e:potosi|Potosí]] were discovered in 1545, making the highlands south of [[e:lake-titicaca|Lake Titicaca]] immensely valuable. In 1559 the crown created a [[e:audiencia|Royal Audiencia]] at [[e:sucre|La Plata]], also called Chuquisaca and now Sucre, to govern the region of [[e:upper-peru|Charcas]], or Upper [[e:peru|Peru]], within the [[s:viceroyalty-of-peru|Viceroyalty of Peru]].
royal-audiencia-of-charcas.r: The [[e:audiencia|Audiencia]] was both a high court and a governing body under a president. [[e:potosi|Potosí]], worked by indigenous labour drafted through the [[e:mita|mita]], became one of the largest cities in the world by 1600, and its [[e:silver|silver]] was minted into coins traded across the globe. [[e:sucre|La Plata]] held an archbishopric and the [[e:university-of-san-francisco-xavier|University of San Francisco Xavier]], founded in 1624, which educated many future revolutionaries. [[e:aymara|Aymara]] and [[e:quechua|Quechua]] communities paid tribute and labour.
royal-audiencia-of-charcas.e: In 1776 [[e:upper-peru|Charcas]] was transferred to the new [[s:viceroyalty-of-the-rio-de-la-plata|Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata]]. Revolts in [[e:sucre|Chuquisaca]] and [[e:la-paz|La Paz]] in 1809 began the struggle for independence. After Sucre's victories, the [[s:republic-of-bolivia|Republic of Bolivia]] was proclaimed in 1825.

reddi-kingdom.t: A Telugu kingdom of coastal Andhra founded after the fall of the Kakatiyas, known for its forts and its literary court.
reddi-kingdom.o: [[e:prolaya-vema-reddi|Prolaya Vema Reddi]], a former Kakatiya follower, joined the revolt of the [[s:musunuri-nayaks|Musunuri Nayaks]] against the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]] and around 1325 established his own rule in coastal [[e:andhra-region|Andhra]]. He made [[e:addanki|Addanki]] and then [[e:kondavidu|Kondavidu]] his capital, and the dynasty extended along the coast from the [[e:krishna-river|Krishna]] to the Godavari.
reddi-kingdom.r: The Reddi kings ruled through a network of [[e:hill-fort|hill forts]] such as [[e:kondavidu|Kondavidu]] and [[e:kondapalli|Kondapalli]] and controlled the port of [[e:motupalli|Motupalli]], encouraging trade. Their court supported [[e:telugu-language|Telugu]] and [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] literature: the great poet [[e:srinatha|Srinatha]] served [[e:pedakomati-vema-reddi|Pedakomati Vema]], and [[e:errana|Errana]] completed the [[e:andhra-mahabharatam|Telugu Mahabharata]]. The kings granted land generously to [[e:brahmins|Brahmins]] and temples.
reddi-kingdom.e: Caught between the [[s:vijayanagara-empire|Vijayanagara Empire]], the [[s:bahmani-sultanate|Bahmani Sultanate]] and the [[s:gajapati-kingdom|Gajapatis of Odisha]], the Reddis lost territory steadily. [[e:kondavidu|Kondavidu]] fell to Vijayanagara around 1424, and the [[e:rajahmundry|Rajahmundry]] branch was absorbed by the Gajapati Kingdom by 1448.

republic-of-zakopane.t: A local Polish government in the Tatra resort of Zakopane, headed by the novelist Stefan Zeromski in the first days of independence.
republic-of-zakopane.o: In late October 1918, as [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]] disintegrated, the citizens of [[e:zakopane|Zakopane]] and the [[e:podhale|Podhale]] highlands took over local power from Austrian officials. A National Organisation was formed, and on 13 November the writer [[e:stefan-zeromski|Stefan Zeromski]], who was living in the town, became chairman of its council.
republic-of-zakopane.r: The so-called republic was a temporary administration rather than a separate state: it declared loyalty to a reborn [[e:poland|Poland]], took control of the town's offices and police, and organised volunteers to guard the border with [[e:slovakia|Slovakia]]. It also had to deal with food shortages in the mountain region.
republic-of-zakopane.e: Within weeks the new Polish government in [[e:warsaw|Warsaw]] and [[e:krakow|Krakow]] extended its authority to [[e:podhale|Podhale]], and by the end of 1918 [[e:zakopane|Zakopane]] was simply part of the [[s:second-polish-republic|Second Polish Republic]].

rashtrakuta-dynasty.t: The Deccan empire that carved the Kailasa temple at Ellora and was ranked by Arab travellers among the four great kingdoms of the world.
rashtrakuta-dynasty.o: [[e:dantidurga|Dantidurga]], a feudatory of the [[s:chalukyas-of-badami|Chalukyas of Badami]], overthrew his overlord [[e:kirtivarman-ii|Kirtivarman II]] in 753 and founded the Rashtrakuta empire in the northern [[e:deccan|Deccan]]. His uncle [[e:krishna|Krishna]] I completed the conquest of the [[e:chalukya-dynasty|Chalukya]] lands and commissioned the [[e:kailasa-temple-ellora|Kailasa temple]] at [[e:ellora-caves|Ellora]], carved from a single mass of rock.
rashtrakuta-dynasty.r: [[e:dhruva-dharavarsha|Dhruva]] and [[e:govinda-iii|Govinda III]] led armies to the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges plain]], defeating the [[s:gurjara-pratihara|Gurjara-Pratihara]] and the [[s:pala-empire|Pala Empire]]. [[e:amoghavarsha-i|Amoghavarsha I]], ruling from 814 to 878, founded the capital [[e:manyakheta|Manyakheta]], was a patron of [[e:jainism|Jainism]] and is credited with the [[e:kavirajamarga|Kavirajamarga]], the earliest surviving work on [[e:kannada|Kannada]] poetics. The Arab merchant Sulaiman described him as one of the four great kings of the world. [[e:krishna-iii|Krishna III]] defeated the [[s:chola-empire|Cholas]] at [[e:battle-of-takkolam|Takkolam]] in 949.
rashtrakuta-dynasty.e: In 972 the Paramara king [[e:siyaka|Siyaka]] sacked [[e:manyakheta|Manyakheta]]. The next year [[e:tailapa-ii|Tailapa II]], a feudatory, overthrew [[e:karka-ii|Karka II]] and founded the [[s:western-chalukya-empire|Western Chalukya Empire]]; Rashtrakuta claimants held out until 982.

republic-of-negros.t: Republic of sugar planters on Negros island that broke from Spain in 1898 and soon sought American protection.
republic-of-negros.o: On 5 November 1898 revolutionaries on [[e:negros|Negros]], led by [[e:aniceto-lacson|Aniceto Lacson]] and [[e:juan-araneta|Juan Araneta]], rose against the Spanish garrison and secured the island within days. They established a cantonal republic centred on [[e:bacolod|Bacolod]], first linked to the [[s:federal-state-of-the-visayas|Federal State of the Visayas]].
republic-of-negros.r: Its leaders were wealthy [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] planters who wanted order and access to markets more than full independence. [[e:aniceto-lacson|Lacson]] served as president and [[e:juan-araneta|Araneta]] as war secretary. Unlike most revolutionary governments, it welcomed American forces in 1899 and became a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] under [[s:united-states|United States]] supervision, adopting its own constitution.
republic-of-negros.e: The [[s:united-states-military-government-of-the-philippine-islands|United States Military Government of the Philippine Islands]] gradually absorbed its functions, and the republic was dissolved in April 1901 when [[e:negros|Negros]] became a province under the [[s:insular-government-of-the-philippine-islands|Insular Government of the Philippine Islands]]. The rising is still commemorated on 5 November.

republic-of-pisa.t: A Tuscan maritime republic that dominated the western Mediterranean in the 12th century and left the Piazza dei Miracoli with its famous leaning tower.
republic-of-pisa.o: Pisan fleets attacked Muslim bases in [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]], [[e:sicily|Sicily]] and [[e:north-africa|North Africa]] in the 11th century, and booty from a raid on [[e:palermo|Palermo]] in 1063 paid for the cathedral. [[e:consul|Consuls]] governing the city are attested by 1085. Archbishop [[e:dagobert-of-pisa|Daibert]] led a Pisan fleet in the [[e:first-crusade|First Crusade]] and became the first [[e:latin|Latin]] Patriarch of [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]].
republic-of-pisa.r: [[e:pisa|Pisa]] built trading quarters in [[e:acre|Acre]], [[s:tyre|Tyre]], [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] and [[e:alexandria|Alexandria]], ruled much of [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]] and [[s:corsican-republic|Corsica]], and conquered the [[e:balearic-islands|Balearic Islands]] briefly in 1113–1115. Loyal to the emperors, it was a Ghibelline stronghold. Its merchants brought back Arabic learning: [[e:fibonacci|Leonardo Fibonacci's]] [[e:liber-abaci|Liber Abaci]] of 1202 introduced [[e:hindu-arabic-numeral-system|Hindu-Arabic numerals]] to [[e:europe|Europe]]. The cathedral square, with baptistery and bell tower begun in 1173, shows its wealth.
republic-of-pisa.e: [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] destroyed the Pisan fleet at [[e:battle-of-meloria-1284|Meloria]] in 1284, and the [[s:kingdom-of-aragon|Kingdom of Aragon]] took [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]] in 1324. Weakened by faction and the silting of its port, [[e:pisa|Pisa]] was sold to the [[s:republic-of-florence|Republic of Florence]] in 1405 and surrendered after a siege in 1406.
