romania.t: Present-day Romania, a democracy since the revolution of 1989 and a member of NATO and the European Union.
romania.o: The revolution of December 1989 overthrew [[e:nicolae-ceausescu|Nicolae Ceaușescu]] and ended the [[s:socialist-republic-of-romania|Socialist Republic of Romania]]. The [[e:national-salvation-front-romania|National Salvation Front]], led by [[e:ion-iliescu|Ion Iliescu]], took power and won the elections of May 1990, though violent interventions by miners in [[e:bucharest|Bucharest]] in 1990 cast doubt on its commitment to democracy. A new constitution was adopted in 1991.
romania.r: [[s:kingdom-of-romania|Romania]] is a semi-presidential republic with a directly elected president and a bicameral parliament. Power first passed peacefully to the opposition in 1996 under [[e:emil-constantinescu|Emil Constantinescu]]. Privatisation and reform were slow in the 1990s, but growth accelerated in the 2000s, driven by industry, services and IT. Millions of [[e:romanians|Romanians]] emigrated to work in [[e:western-europe|Western Europe]].
romania.e: [[s:kingdom-of-romania|Romania]] joined [[e:nato|NATO]] in 2004 and the [[e:european-union|European Union]] in 2007. Anti-corruption campaigns and mass protests in 2017 shaped politics, and the annulment of the 2024 presidential election over alleged foreign interference caused a political crisis before a rerun in 2025.

republic-of-china.t: One of the earliest republics in Asia, founded on the mainland in 1912, which after 1949 continued on Taiwan and became a prosperous democracy.
republic-of-china.o: The [[e:wuchang-uprising|Wuchang Uprising]] of October 1911 spread across the southern provinces, and on 1 January 1912 the Republic of [[e:china|China]] was proclaimed at [[e:nanjing|Nanjing]] with [[e:sun-yat-sen|Sun Yat-sen]] as provisional president. The last Qing emperor abdicated in February, and [[e:yuan-shikai|Yuan Shikai]] became president, ruling from [[e:beijing|Beijing]].
republic-of-china.r: After Yuan's death the [[s:beiyang-government|Beiyang government]] in [[e:beijing|Beijing]] lost control to regional warlords. [[e:chiang-kai-shek|Chiang Kai-shek's]] [[s:nationalist-government|Nationalist government]] reunified much of [[e:china|China]] in 1928 and led resistance to [[e:japan|Japan]] from 1937 to 1945, but lost the civil war to the Communists. In 1949 the government moved to [[e:taipei|Taipei]], ruling [[e:taiwan|Taiwan]] under martial law while presiding over rapid industrial growth.
republic-of-china.e: The [[s:peoples-republic-of-china|People's Republic of China]] took [[e:china|China's]] [[e:united-nations|United Nations]] seat in 1971. Martial law ended in 1987, President [[e:lee-teng-hui|Lee Teng-hui]] oversaw democratic reforms and the first direct presidential election in 1996, and power passed peacefully to the opposition in 2000. The Republic today governs [[e:taiwan|Taiwan]], [[e:penghu|Penghu]], [[e:kinmen|Kinmen]] and [[e:matsu-islands|Matsu]].

reval.t: Hanseatic port of medieval Tallinn, a self-governing merchant city under Danish and then Order rule whose old town survives almost intact.
reval.o: Reval grew around the Danish castle on [[e:toompea|Toompea]], built after the [[e:battle-of-lindanise|Battle of Lindanise]] in 1219. In 1248 King [[e:eric-iv-of-denmark|Eric IV of Denmark]] granted the town [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck|Lübeck]] law, giving it self-government, and it soon joined the Hanseatic network linking Novgorod with [[e:lubeck|Lübeck]] and the west.
reval.r: A council of German merchants ran the lower town, while the castle hill was the seat of the ruler and the nobility. The Great [[e:guild|Guild]], the [[e:brotherhood-of-blackheads|Brotherhood of the Blackheads]] and craft guilds organised trade and society. Reval prospered on the transit trade with Novgorod, building its Gothic town hall, completed in 1404, and the tall spire of [[e:st-olafs-church-tallinn|St Olaf's Church]].
reval.e: Reval passed from the [[s:duchy-of-estonia-1219-1346|Duchy of Estonia]] (1219-1346) to the [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]] in 1346 and adopted [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] in the 1520s. Threatened by [[e:russia|Russia]] during the [[e:livonian-war|Livonian War]], the city submitted to [[e:eric-xiv-of-sweden|Eric XIV of Sweden]] in 1561, becoming the capital of the Duchy of [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]] (1561-1721).

republic-of-siena-at-montalcino.t: The last stand of the Sienese republic, kept alive in the hill town of Montalcino with French support for four years after Siena fell.
republic-of-siena-at-montalcino.o: When [[s:republic-of-siena|Siena]] surrendered to imperial and Florentine forces in April 1555, several hundred citizens who refused to submit withdrew to the fortified town of [[e:montalcino|Montalcino]], south of the city, and continued the government of the Republic of Siena there under French protection.
republic-of-siena-at-montalcino.r: The exiles kept the republic's magistracies and seal, minted coins and governed [[e:montalcino|Montalcino]] and a few nearby towns. They depended on French troops and on [[e:piero-strozzi|Piero Strozzi]], the Florentine exile who commanded for [[e:france|France]] in [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Tuscany]]. The republic's territory was small, its resources were slight and it lived under the constant threat of the [[s:duchy-of-florence|Duchy of Florence]].
republic-of-siena-at-montalcino.e: The [[e:peace-of-cateau-cambresis|Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis]] between [[e:france|France]] and [[e:spain|Spain]] in 1559 withdrew French support, and [[e:montalcino|Montalcino]] surrendered to [[e:cosimo-i-de-medici|Cosimo I de' Medici]], joining the future [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Grand Duchy of Tuscany]]. The town's people are still nicknamed the last Sienese.

roman-numidia.t: Rome's frontier province in eastern Algeria, home of the Third Augustan Legion, the city of Timgad and the Donatist church.
roman-numidia.o: [[s:numidia|Numidia]] came under [[e:rome|Rome]] after the defeat of [[e:juba-i|Juba I]] in 46 BCE and was long administered as part of [[s:africa-proconsularis|Africa Proconsularis]], although the commander of the Third Augustan [[e:legion|Legion]] effectively governed it. Around 198 [[e:septimius-severus|Septimius Severus]] made it a separate province, governed by the legate from the fortress at [[e:lambaesis|Lambaesis]].
roman-numidia.r: The legion guarded the [[e:aures-mountains|Aurès]] mountains and the desert frontier, and veterans settled in new towns such as [[e:timgad|Thamugadi]] (Timgad), founded by [[e:trajan|Trajan]] in 100. [[e:cirta|Cirta]] was the leading city, renamed [[e:constantine-algeria|Constantina]] by Constantine. The high plains produced grain and [[e:olive-oil|olive oil]]. [[s:numidia|Numidia]] was the stronghold of the [[e:donatism|Donatist]] church and the birthplace of [[e:augustine-of-hippo|Augustine]] at [[e:thagaste|Thagaste]]. [[e:diocletian|Diocletian]] briefly split it into Numidia Cirtensis and Numidia Militiana.
roman-numidia.e: After 435 the [[e:vandals|Vandals]] took control of parts of [[s:numidia|Numidia]], and their capture of [[e:carthage|Carthage]] in 439 ended Roman rule. Byzantine forces later reoccupied much of it, while [[e:berbers|Berber]] kingdoms such as the [[s:kingdom-of-the-aures|Kingdom of the Aures]] held the mountains.

republic-of-tamrash.t: Self-governing community of Muslim Pomak villages in the Rhodope mountains that refused Russian and Bulgarian rule after the war of 1877 to 1878.
republic-of-tamrash.o: During the [[e:russo-turkish-war-1877-1878|Russo-Turkish War]] of 1877 to 1878, Muslim Bulgarian-speaking [[e:pomaks|Pomaks]] in the western [[e:rhodope-mountains|Rhodopes]] resisted the advancing Russian army. After the war, about twenty villages around Tamrash refused to submit to the Russian administration or to [[s:eastern-rumelia|Eastern Rumelia]], and organised their own defence and government in the mountains.
republic-of-tamrash.r: Known mainly from diplomatic reports, the community was governed by local Muslim notables and village councils, under the nominal suzerainty of the Ottoman sultan. It survived because of its remote terrain and because the Great Powers left its status unresolved.
republic-of-tamrash.e: When [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]] absorbed [[s:eastern-rumelia|Eastern Rumelia]] in 1885, the Bulgarian-Ottoman agreement of 1886 transferred the [[e:pomaks|Pomak]] villages and the Kardzhali district back to direct Ottoman rule. They became part of [[e:bulgaria|Bulgaria]] after the [[e:balkan-wars|Balkan Wars]] of 1912 to 1913.

republic-of-central-albania.t: Rival Albanian government set up by Essad Pasha Toptani in Durrës in 1913, a symptom of the struggle for power in the newly independent country.
republic-of-central-albania.o: [[e:essad-pasha-toptani|Essad Pasha Toptani]], an Ottoman general from a leading landowning family of central [[s:albania|Albania]], commanded the defence of [[e:shkoder|Shkodër]] in the [[e:first-balkan-war|First Balkan War]], then surrendered it to [[s:montenegro|Montenegro]] in April 1913 in exchange for safe passage. Opposing [[e:ismail-qemali|Ismail Qemali's]] [[s:provisional-government-of-albania|Provisional Government of Albania]], he set up his own government in [[e:durres|Durrës]] in October 1913.
republic-of-central-albania.r: [[e:essad-pasha-toptani|Essad]] ruled central [[s:albania|Albania]], from [[e:durres|Durrës]] to around [[e:tirana|Tirana]] and [[e:elbasan|Elbasan]], through a senate of local notables and the support of Muslim landowners and his own armed retainers. He cultivated ties with [[s:serbia|Serbia]] and [[e:italy|Italy]]. The state was essentially his personal domain and was never recognised by the Great Powers.
republic-of-central-albania.e: [[e:essad-pasha-toptani|Essad]] accepted the authority of [[e:william-prince-of-albania|Wilhelm of Wied]] in early 1914, becoming minister of the interior and war in the [[s:principality-of-albania|Principality of Albania]], but was expelled for intrigue in May 1914. He returned later in 1914 to rule central [[s:albania|Albania]] until 1916, and was assassinated in [[e:paris|Paris]] in 1920.

republic-of-ossola.t: The best-known partisan republic of wartime Italy, which governed the Alpine valleys around Domodossola for about forty days in 1944.
republic-of-ossola.o: In September 1944 Italian partisan formations drove German and Fascist garrisons out of the [[e:val-dossola|Val d'Ossola]], near the Swiss border, and entered [[e:domodossola|Domodossola]] on 10 September. A provisional government junta was formed, presided over by the socialist [[e:ettore-tibaldi|Ettore Tibaldi]].
republic-of-ossola.r: The junta brought together members of the different anti-Fascist parties. In a few weeks it reorganised local government, schools, justice and food supply, and planned democratic reforms, while the Swiss border allowed contacts with the [[e:allies|Allies]]. Its experience of self-government later influenced debates on the Italian constitution.
republic-of-ossola.e: In October 1944 German and Fascist troops of the [[s:italian-social-republic|Italian Social Republic]] launched an offensive and reoccupied the valley. Thousands of civilians and partisans fled into [[s:swiss-confederation|Switzerland]].

republic-of-poljica.t: Self-governing peasant and minor-noble community between Split and Omiš that kept its own law and elected rulers for nearly four centuries.
republic-of-poljica.o: [[e:poljica|Poljica]], a hilly district between the [[e:cetina|Cetina]] river and the coast near Split, had long enjoyed local autonomy under Croatian and Hungarian kings. Its customary law was written down in the [[e:poljica-statute|Poljica Statute]], traditionally dated to 1440, which fixed the rights of its villages and noble families. As the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] advanced, Poljica placed itself under Venetian protection.
republic-of-poljica.r: Each year an assembly at Gata elected a grand knez from the local nobility, assisted by village knezes, judges and a chancellor. Land was held by kin groups, and the statute regulated inheritance, feuds and grazing. The statute was written in Croatian in Bosnian Cyrillic script. [[e:poljica|Poljica]] paid tribute to the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] while serving [[e:venice|Venice]] as a frontier buffer.
republic-of-poljica.e: After [[e:venice|Venice]] fell in 1797, [[e:poljica|Poljica]] came under [[e:austria|Austria]] and then, in 1806, [[e:france|France]]. When Poljica men joined a Russian-backed rising, [[e:auguste-de-marmont|Marshal Marmont]] abolished the republic in 1807 and merged it into French [[e:dalmatia|Dalmatia]], later the [[s:illyrian-provinces|Illyrian Provinces]]. The statute remains a key source for Croatian law.

republic-of-cyrene.t: Cyrene after its kings, a quarrelsome Greek republic famous for silphium, horses and the Cyrenaic school of philosophy.
republic-of-cyrene.o: Around 440 BCE the last [[e:battiad-dynasty|Battiad]] king, [[e:arcesilaus-iv|Arcesilaus IV]], was overthrown and the [[s:kingdom-of-cyrene|Kingdom of Cyrene]] became a republic. The city remained the leading power of [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]], a group of Greek cities later called the [[e:pentapolis-cyrenaica|Pentapolis]], together with [[s:barca|Barca]], [[s:euesperides|Euesperides]], [[e:taucheira|Taucheira]] and its own port, [[e:apollonia-cyrenaica|Apollonia]].
republic-of-cyrene.r: Government swung between democracy and oligarchy, with bloody civil strife in the early 4th century BCE. [[s:kingdom-of-cyrene|Cyrene]] remained rich from silphium, grain and horses, and it treated with [[e:carthage|Carthage]] over its western border at the [[e:altars-of-the-philaeni|Altars of the Philaeni]]. It was an intellectual centre: [[e:aristippus-of-cyrene|Aristippus]] founded the Cyrenaic school of philosophy, and the mathematician [[e:theodorus-of-cyrene|Theodorus]] taught there. Cyrene submitted to [[e:alexander-the-great|Alexander the Great]] in 331 BCE.
republic-of-cyrene.e: In 324 to 322 BCE the Spartan adventurer [[e:thibron|Thibron]] attacked the city, and its factions called in [[e:ptolemy-i-soter|Ptolemy I]], whose general [[e:ophellas|Ophellas]] annexed [[s:kingdom-of-cyrene|Cyrene]] to the [[s:ptolemaic-empire|Ptolemaic Empire]] in 322 BCE. It later became the centre of the [[s:ptolemaic-kingdom-of-cyrene|Ptolemaic Kingdom of Cyrene]].

ruanda-urundi.t: The Belgian mandate over the kingdoms of Rwanda and Burundi, whose colonial policies sharpened the Hutu and Tutsi divide.
ruanda-urundi.o: Belgian troops from the Congo occupied the north-western part of [[s:german-east-africa|German East Africa]] in 1916. After the war the [[e:league-of-nations|League of Nations]] assigned the territory to [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Belgium]] as a mandate, confirmed in 1924, and in 1946 it became a [[e:united-nations|United Nations]] trust territory. Its administrative centre was [[e:bujumbura|Usumbura]], now Bujumbura.
ruanda-urundi.r: [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Belgium]] ruled indirectly through the mwami of the [[s:kingdom-of-rwanda|Kingdom of Rwanda]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-burundi|Kingdom of Burundi]] and their chiefs, favouring a Tutsi elite and replacing [[e:hutu|Hutu]] chiefs. Identity cards introduced in the 1930s fixed ethnic labels. The Catholic Church ran schools and missions, and [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] became the main cash crop, often grown under compulsion. The territory was administered jointly with the [[s:belgian-congo|Belgian Congo]] from 1925.
ruanda-urundi.e: From 1959 the [[e:hutu|Hutu]] revolution in [[s:kingdom-of-rwanda|Rwanda]] overthrew the monarchy, while [[s:kingdom-of-burundi|Burundi]] stayed a kingdom. The UN failed to keep the two together, and on 1 July 1962 they became independent as the republic of Rwanda and the Kingdom of Burundi.

republic-of-central-lithuania.t: A Polish-controlled state around Vilnius, created by a staged mutiny in 1920 and annexed by Poland in 1922.
republic-of-central-lithuania.o: In October 1920, days after an [[e:armistice-of-11-november-1918|armistice]] gave [[e:vilnius|Vilnius]] to [[s:republic-of-lithuania|Lithuania]], the Polish general [[e:lucjan-zeligowski|Lucjan Zeligowski]] led troops in a staged mutiny, approved secretly by Pilsudski, and captured the city. He proclaimed the Republic of Central [[e:lithuania|Lithuania]], claiming to act for the local Polish-speaking population.
republic-of-central-lithuania.r: Zeligowski ruled as supreme commander through a provisional governing commission, and the state had its own stamps, army and courts. Its population was mixed: [[e:poles|Poles]], [[e:jews|Jews]], [[e:lithuanians|Lithuanians]] and [[e:belarusians|Belarusians]]. [[e:league-of-nations|League of Nations]] attempts to arrange a plebiscite failed, and elections in January 1922 were boycotted by most Lithuanians, Jews and Belarusians.
republic-of-central-lithuania.e: The resulting assembly voted in February 1922 to join [[e:poland|Poland]], and the territory became part of the [[s:second-polish-republic|Second Polish Republic]]. [[s:republic-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] refused to recognise this and broke off relations until 1938, regaining [[e:vilnius|Vilnius]] from the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] in 1939.

real-audiencia-of-panama.t: The royal court and government of the Isthmus of Panama, the vital crossing through which Peruvian silver passed on its way to Spain.
real-audiencia-of-panama.o: The [[e:audiencia|Audiencia]] of [[s:republic-of-panama|Panama]] was established in 1538 to govern [[s:castilla-de-oro|Castilla de Oro]] and the surrounding provinces of Tierra Firme. It was briefly abolished in 1543 and restored in the 1560s, and from 1542 it fell within the sphere of the [[s:viceroyalty-of-peru|Viceroyalty of Peru]].
real-audiencia-of-panama.r: Panama's role was transit: [[e:silver|silver]] from [[e:potosi|Potosí]] was shipped to [[e:panama-city|Panama City]], carried across the isthmus by mule and river, and traded at the great fairs of [[e:nombre-de-dios-panama|Nombre de Dios]] and later [[e:portobelo|Portobelo]] for European goods. The trade attracted attacks: [[e:henry-morgan|Henry Morgan]] sacked [[s:republic-of-panama|Panama]] City in 1671, and it was rebuilt on a new site in 1673. [[e:edward-vernon|Edward Vernon]] captured Portobelo in 1739.
real-audiencia-of-panama.e: As [[e:spain|Spain]] shifted to sailing around [[e:cape-horn|Cape Horn]], the isthmus declined. The audiencia was abolished in 1751, and [[s:republic-of-panama|Panama]] was placed under the [[s:viceroyalty-of-new-granada|Viceroyalty of New Granada]]. It later joined [[s:gran-colombia|Gran Colombia]].

republic-of-upingtonia.t: A short-lived republic of Dorsland trekkers at Grootfontein in northern Namibia, swallowed by German South West Africa.
republic-of-upingtonia.o: [[e:boers|Boer]] [[e:dorsland-trek|Dorsland]] trekkers who had crossed the Kalahari settled around [[e:grootfontein|Grootfontein]], on land bought in 1885 from the [[s:kingdom-of-ondonga|Ndonga]] king Kambonde by the trader [[e:william-worthington-jordan|William Worthington Jordan]]. They proclaimed a republic, naming it Upingtonia after the Cape prime minister [[e:thomas-upington|Thomas Upington]].
republic-of-upingtonia.r: The settlement consisted of a few dozen families farming in a fertile but isolated area. Its title to the land was disputed by the [[s:herero-paramountcy|Herero Paramountcy]], which claimed the region, and the settlers lacked the means to defend themselves.
republic-of-upingtonia.e: [[s:hashemite-kingdom-of-jordan|Jordan]] was murdered in 1886, and the settlers, under pressure from the [[e:herero-people|Herero]] and with no outside support, renamed the state Lijdensrust and dissolved it in 1887. Many moved on to [[s:portuguese-angola|Angola]], and the area passed to [[s:german-south-west-africa|German South West Africa]].

republic-of-uzice.t: Liberated territory in western Serbia held by Tito's Partisans in autumn 1941, the first large free zone in occupied Europe.
republic-of-uzice.o: In the uprising of summer 1941 against the German occupation of [[s:serbia|Serbia]], [[e:yugoslav-partisans|Communist-led Partisans]] and [[e:chetniks|Chetnik]] units liberated much of western [[e:serbia|Serbia]]. The Partisans took [[e:uzice|Užice]] on 24 September 1941, and [[e:josip-broz-tito|Josip Broz Tito]] set up his headquarters there, making the town the centre of a liberated territory covering several districts.
republic-of-uzice.r: Local people's liberation committees took over administration, schools and supplies, while the town's arms factory produced rifles and ammunition in an underground vault, and the Communist newspaper [[e:borba-newspaper|Borba]] was printed there. Relations with [[e:draza-mihailovic|Draža Mihailović's]] [[e:chetniks|Chetniks]] broke down into open fighting in early November 1941.
republic-of-uzice.e: A German offensive in late November 1941 retook [[e:uzice|Užice]], and the [[e:yugoslav-partisans|Partisans]] withdrew into the [[e:sandzak|Sandžak]] and eastern [[e:bosnia|Bosnia]], where they formed the [[e:1st-proletarian-brigade|First Proletarian Brigade]]. Under the later [[s:socialist-federal-republic-of-yugoslavia|Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia]], Užice was renamed Titovo Užice.

republic-of-lucca.t: A silk-weaving Tuscan city-republic that kept its independence behind its great walls for over six centuries, until Napoleon.
republic-of-lucca.o: [[s:duchy-of-lucca|Lucca]] had been the capital of the march of [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Tuscany]], and a commune of consuls emerged in the late 11th century. In 1160 Duke [[e:welf-vi|Welf VI]] granted the city wide rights, confirming its self-government over the surrounding district.
republic-of-lucca.r: [[s:duchy-of-lucca|Lucca]] prospered from [[e:silk|silk]] weaving and banking, and venerated the [[e:volto-santo-of-lucca|Volto Santo]] crucifix. [[e:castruccio-castracani|Castruccio Castracani]] made himself lord from 1316 to 1328 and won a large state, but after his death the city was sold among foreign lords until [[e:charles-iv|Emperor Charles IV]] restored its freedom in 1369. [[e:paolo-guinigi|Paolo Guinigi]] ruled as lord from 1400 to 1430. Afterwards an oligarchy of merchant families governed, building the massive walls of the 16th and 17th centuries.
republic-of-lucca.e: The French occupied [[s:duchy-of-lucca|Lucca]] in 1799, and in 1805 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] replaced the republic with the [[s:principality-of-lucca-and-piombino|Principality of Lucca and Piombino]] for his sister [[e:elisa-bonaparte|Elisa]].

republic-of-afghanistan-1973-1978.t: The republic founded by Mohammad Daoud Khan after he overthrew his cousin King Zahir Shah, ended five years later by a communist coup.
republic-of-afghanistan-1973-1978.o: On 17 July 1973 the former prime minister [[e:mohammad-daoud-khan|Mohammad Daoud Khan]], cousin and brother-in-law of King [[e:mohammad-zahir-shah|Zahir Shah]], seized power in a bloodless coup with the support of army officers, including members of the communist [[e:parcham|Parcham]] faction. He abolished the [[s:kingdom-of-afghanistan|Kingdom of Afghanistan]] and declared a republic with himself as president.
republic-of-afghanistan-1973-1978.r: [[e:mohammad-daoud-khan|Daoud]] ruled in an authoritarian style, pursuing the Pashtunistan dispute with [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Pakistan]] and economic development with Soviet and Western aid. He suppressed Islamist opponents, many of whom fled to [[e:pakistan|Pakistan]], and gradually pushed the communists out of government. A new constitution in 1977 created a one-party state, and he sought closer ties with [[e:iran|Iran]] and the Gulf states, angering [[e:moscow|Moscow]].
republic-of-afghanistan-1973-1978.e: After the murder of the communist leader Mir [[e:akbar|Akbar]] Khyber led to mass protests, [[e:mohammad-daoud-khan|Daoud]] arrested communist leaders. On 27 April 1978 army officers loyal to the [[e:peoples-democratic-party-of-afghanistan|People's Democratic Party]] killed Daoud and his family in the [[e:saur-revolution|Saur Revolution]], establishing the [[s:democratic-republic-of-afghanistan|Democratic Republic of Afghanistan]].

radhanpur-state.t: A Babi Pathan Nawabi state in northern Gujarat, founded by a Mughal officer on the edge of the Rann of Kutch.
radhanpur-state.o: [[e:jawan-mard-khan|Kamal-ud-din Khan Babi]], known as Jawan Mard Khan, was a Mughal officer in [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] from the Babi family that also ruled [[s:junagadh-state|Junagadh State]]. After the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] took [[e:ahmedabad|Ahmedabad]] in 1753 he secured Radhanpur and nearby districts as his own principality.
radhanpur-state.r: The Nawabs ruled a dry territory on the trade route towards [[s:cutch-state|Kutch]] and [[e:sindh|Sindh]]. Under British protection Radhanpur was an 11-gun salute state, first under the [[s:palanpur-state|Palanpur]] Agency and later the [[e:western-india-states-agency|Western India States Agency]], with a largely [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] farming population.
radhanpur-state.e: After accession to [[e:india|India]] Radhanpur was merged into [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]] in 1948 and has been part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] since 1960; it is now in Patan district.

rabih-az-zubayrs-state.t: The conquest state of the Sudanese warlord Rabih, which overran Bornu before French forces destroyed it at Kousseri in 1900.
rabih-az-zubayrs-state.o: [[e:rabih-az-zubayr|Rabih az-Zubayr]] had served the slave-trading [[e:magnates|magnate]] al-[[e:al-zubayr-rahma-mansur|Zubayr Rahma Mansur]] in the [[e:bahr-al-ghazal|Bahr al-Ghazal]]. When Egyptian forces crushed al-Zubayr's son Sulayman in 1879, Rabih led an army of several hundred riflemen west into the borderlands of [[s:sultanate-of-dar-al-kuti|Dar al Kuti]] and the Chari basin, where he built a new power.
rabih-az-zubayrs-state.r: [[e:rabih-az-zubayr|Rabih]] ruled as a military chief, with a disciplined army of slave soldiers armed with rifles, raiding widely for captives. He made Muhammad al-Sanusi of [[s:sultanate-of-dar-al-kuti|Dar al Kuti]] his [[e:vassal|vassal]], attacked the [[s:kingdom-of-baguirmi|Kingdom of Baguirmi]] and in 1893 conquered the ancient [[s:kanem-bornu-empire|Kanem-Bornu Empire]], ruling from a new capital at [[e:dikwa|Dikwa]].
rabih-az-zubayrs-state.e: French columns converged on the Chari, and on 22 April 1900 [[e:rabih-az-zubayr|Rabih]] was killed at [[e:kousseri|Kousseri]], where the French commander [[e:amedee-francois-lamy|Lamy]] also died. His son Fadlallah was killed in 1901, and the lands were divided among [[e:france|France]], [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and [[e:germany|Germany]].

ran-wei.t: The brief empire of Ran Min, a Chinese general who seized the Later Zhao capital in 350 and ordered the massacre of the Jie and other northern peoples.
ran-wei.o: [[e:ran-min|Ran Min]] was a Chinese general adopted into the family of the [[s:later-zhao|Later Zhao]] emperor [[e:shi-hu|Shi Hu]]. In the civil war after Shi Hu's death he seized Ye, and in 350 he proclaimed himself emperor of a new [[e:cao-wei|Wei dynasty]].
ran-wei.r: [[e:ran-min|Ran Min]] ordered the killing of the [[e:jie-people|Jie]] and other non-Chinese in Ye; sources claim some 200,000 died. The massacre made his regime a rallying point for Chinese hostility to the northern conquerors but left it surrounded by enemies. Ran Wei held little more than the Ye region and was constantly at war with [[s:later-zhao|Later Zhao]] remnants.
ran-wei.e: In 352 the [[s:former-yan|Former Yan]] general [[e:murong-ke|Murong Ke]] defeated and captured [[e:ran-min|Ran Min]] at Liantai; he was executed, and Ye fell later that year. In modern times Ran Min has been both condemned for [[e:genocide|genocide]] and praised by nationalists.

rehoboth-basters.t: The self-governing community of the Rehoboth Basters in central Namibia, which kept its own captaincy and laws for more than a century.
rehoboth-basters.o: The Basters, descendants of [[e:cape-dutch|Cape Dutch]] settlers and [[e:khoekhoe|Khoekhoe]] women, left the northern Cape in 1868 and under Kaptein [[e:hermanus-van-wyk|Hermanus van Wyk]] settled at [[e:rehoboth-namibia|Rehoboth]], south of [[e:windhoek|Windhoek]], in 1870, acquiring land from the Swartbooi [[e:nama-people|Nama]].
rehoboth-basters.r: In 1872 they adopted written Paternal Laws, the Vaderlike Wette, establishing an elected kaptein, a Volksraad and courts. They farmed [[e:cattle|cattle]] and sheep, spoke [[e:afrikaans|Afrikaans]] and were Lutheran Christians. A protection treaty with [[e:germany|Germany]] in 1885 preserved their autonomy, and they fought on the German side against the [[e:nama-people|Nama]] in 1904, but clashed with German troops at [[e:battle-of-sam-khubis|Sam Khubis]] in 1915.
rehoboth-basters.e: Under South African rule the Basters kept partial self-government, becoming a self-governing [[e:bantustan|homeland]] in 1979. Their autonomy ended with Namibian independence in 1990, though the Kaptein's council continued to press its claims.

rif-republic.t: Abd el-Krim's Berber republic in northern Morocco, which crushed a Spanish army at Annual and inspired anticolonial movements worldwide.
rif-republic.o: [[e:abd-el-krim|Muhammad ibn Abd el-Krim al-Khattabi]], a Rifian judge and journalist, united the tribes of the Rif against the [[s:spanish-protectorate-in-morocco|Spanish protectorate in Morocco]]. In July 1921 his forces destroyed a Spanish army at Annual, killing thousands. He proclaimed a republic with its capital at [[e:ajdir|Ajdir]], formally constituted in 1923.
rif-republic.r: The republic had ministries, a national assembly of tribal representatives, taxes and a disciplined army that used captured artillery and trench warfare. [[e:abd-el-krim|Abd el-Krim]] banned feuds and enforced Islamic law, aiming at a modern state. In 1925 his offensive against the [[s:french-protectorate-in-morocco|French protectorate in Morocco]] brought [[e:france|France]] into the war.
rif-republic.e: A combined Franco-Spanish force of hundreds of thousands, with a landing at [[e:alhucemas-landing|Alhucemas]] in 1925 and Spanish use of [[e:chemical-weapons|chemical weapons]], overwhelmed the Rif. [[e:abd-el-krim|Abd el-Krim]] surrendered in May 1926 and was exiled to Réunion.

republic-of-chile.t: The South American republic along the Pacific that became independent in 1818 and is known for long periods of constitutional stability, broken by the 1973 coup.
republic-of-chile.o: After the collapse of the [[s:patria-vieja|Patria Vieja]], the [[e:army-of-the-andes|Army of the Andes]] under [[e:jose-de-san-martin|José de San Martín]] and [[e:bernardo-ohiggins|Bernardo O'Higgins]] defeated the royalists at [[e:battle-of-chacabuco|Chacabuco]] in 1817. O'Higgins, as Supreme Director, signed the declaration of independence dated 1 January 1818 and proclaimed on 12 February, and victory at [[e:battle-of-maipu|Maipú]] in April secured it.
republic-of-chile.r: After a decade of instability, the Constitution of 1833, shaped by [[e:diego-portales|Diego Portales]], created a strong presidential state. Chile defeated the [[s:peru-bolivian-confederation|Peru-Bolivian Confederation]] in 1839 and won the [[e:war-of-the-pacific|War of the Pacific]] from 1879 to 1883, gaining nitrate-rich [[e:tarapaca|Tarapacá]] and [[e:antofagasta|Antofagasta]]. It conquered [[s:araucania|Araucanía]] by 1883. [[e:copper|Copper]] later replaced nitrates. [[e:salvador-allende|Salvador Allende's]] socialist government was overthrown on 11 September 1973 by [[e:augusto-pinochet|Augusto Pinochet]], whose dictatorship lasted until 1990.
republic-of-chile.e: Chile returned to democracy after the 1988 plebiscite and has since become one of [[e:latin-america|Latin America's]] most prosperous economies. Proposals to replace [[e:augusto-pinochet|Pinochet]]'s 1980 constitution were rejected in referendums in 2022 and 2023.

republic-of-bologna.t: The city-republic of Europe's oldest university and its forest of towers, which held a captive king for 23 years and later flourished under the Bentivoglio.
republic-of-bologna.o: In 1116 [[e:henry-v-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Henry V]] granted privileges to the citizens of [[e:bologna|Bologna]], the starting point of the commune. Its law school, traditionally dated to 1088 and associated with the jurist [[e:irnerius|Irnerius]], drew students from all over [[e:europe|Europe]] and made the city famous.
republic-of-bologna.r: [[e:bologna|Bologna]] was ruled by consuls, then a podestà and popular councils. Noble families built hundreds of defensive towers, including the [[e:two-towers-bologna|Asinelli]] and Garisenda. [[e:guelphs-and-ghibellines|Guelph]] Bologna captured [[e:enzo-of-sardinia|King Enzo]], son of Frederick II, at [[e:battle-of-fossalta|Fossalta]] in 1249 and held him until his death in 1272; the [[e:liber-paradisus|Liber Paradisus]] of 1256 freed the serfs of its countryside. Nominally under the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]], the city was dominated by the [[e:pepoli-family|Pepoli]] and then the [[e:bentivoglio-family|Bentivoglio]] families.
republic-of-bologna.e: [[e:pope-julius-ii|Pope Julius II]] marched on [[e:bologna|Bologna]] in 1506 and drove out [[e:giovanni-ii-bentivoglio|Giovanni II Bentivoglio]]. The city then passed under direct papal rule, which lasted until 1796, when it briefly became the [[s:bolognese-republic|Bolognese Republic]].

rhodanic-republic.t: Napoleonic client republic in the Valais, kept separate from Switzerland to secure the Simplon pass.
rhodanic-republic.o: [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] wanted control of the [[e:simplon-pass|Simplon]] pass between [[e:france|France]] and [[e:italy|Italy]]. In 1802 he separated the [[e:valais|Valais]] from the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]] and made it a nominally independent Republic of the [[e:rhone|Rhône]] (République rhodanienne), under the joint protection of France, the [[s:italian-republic-1802-1805|Italian Republic]] and the [[e:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]].
rhodanic-republic.r: The republic was governed by a small administration in [[e:sion-switzerland|Sion]] under a constitution imposed by [[e:france|France]], with a diet and a council of state. Its main obligation was to maintain the new [[e:simplon-pass|Simplon]] road, completed by French engineers in 1805, and to allow free passage to French troops. The population was Catholic and largely rural.
rhodanic-republic.e: In November 1810 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] annexed the [[e:valais|Valais]] to [[e:france|France]] as the [[e:departement|department]] of [[e:simplon-pass|Simplon]]. After his fall it became a canton of the [[s:swiss-confederation|Swiss Confederation]] in 1815.

republic-of-genoa.t: A maritime republic whose fleets and bankers dominated Mediterranean and Black Sea trade and later financed the Spanish Empire, lasting nearly seven centuries.
republic-of-genoa.o: Genoese citizens formed a sworn association, the compagna communis, around 1099, as fleets returned rich from the [[e:first-crusade|First Crusade]] under leaders such as [[e:guglielmo-embriaco|Guglielmo Embriaco]]. The commune won trading privileges in the crusader states and fought [[e:pisa|Pisa]] and Muslim powers for the western [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]].
republic-of-genoa.r: [[e:genoa|Genoa]] built colonies at [[e:galata|Pera]] beside [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]], [[s:genoese-gazaria|Caffa]] in the [[e:crimea|Crimea]] and [[s:chios|Chios]], and destroyed [[e:pisa|Pisa's]] fleet at [[e:battle-of-meloria-1284|Meloria]] in 1284. Factions of great families, the [[e:doria-family|Doria]], [[e:spinola-family|Spinola]], Fieschi and Grimaldi, competed for power; from 1339 doges such as [[e:simone-boccanegra|Simone Boccanegra]] headed the state. The [[e:bank-of-saint-george|Bank of Saint George]], founded in 1407, managed public debt and colonies. [[e:christopher-columbus|Columbus]] was a Genoese.
republic-of-genoa.e: After losing the [[e:war-of-chioggia|War of Chioggia]] to [[e:venice|Venice]] in 1381, [[e:genoa|Genoa]] often fell under French or [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milanese]] rule. [[e:andrea-doria|Andrea Doria's]] constitution of 1528 created an aristocratic republic allied to [[s:habsburg-spain|Habsburg Spain]], which Genoese bankers financed. Genoa sold [[s:corsican-republic|Corsica]] to [[e:france|France]] in 1768 and became the [[s:ligurian-republic|Ligurian Republic]] in 1797.

raj-of-sarawak.t: Kingdom in northern Borneo ruled for a century by an English family, the White Rajahs of the Brooke dynasty.
raj-of-sarawak.o: The English adventurer [[e:james-brooke|James Brooke]] helped the [[s:brunei-sultanate|Brunei Sultanate]] put down a revolt of [[e:malays|Malays]] and [[e:bidayuh|Bidayuh]] near [[e:kuching|Kuching]] in 1839 to 1841. As a reward the sultan made him [[e:rajah-of-sarawak|Rajah of Sarawak]] in 1841. Brooke and his successors then took further river basins from Brunei until Sarawak far exceeded the sultanate in size.
raj-of-sarawak.r: The Brookes ruled personally, with a small European staff and Malay chiefs, and governed through longhouse headmen among [[e:iban-people|Iban]] and other [[e:dayak-people|Dayak peoples]]. They suppressed piracy and headhunting, often with Iban levies, and limited European plantation companies. Chinese settlers grew [[e:pepper|pepper]] and mined gold. [[e:charles-brooke-rajah-of-sarawak|Charles Brooke]] ruled for nearly fifty years, and Sarawak became a British [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] in 1888.
raj-of-sarawak.e: After Japanese occupation from 1941 to 1945, [[e:charles-vyner-brooke|Charles Vyner Brooke]] ceded Sarawak to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in 1946 despite strong local opposition, creating the [[s:crown-colony-of-sarawak|Crown Colony of Sarawak]]. It joined [[s:malaysia|Malaysia]] in 1963.

republic-of-ecuador.t: The Andean republic on the equator, formed when Quito, Guayaquil and Cuenca left Gran Colombia in 1830, which includes the Galápagos Islands.
republic-of-ecuador.o: In May 1830 an assembly in [[e:quito|Quito]] declared the southern district of [[s:gran-colombia|Gran Colombia]] an independent state, naming it Ecuador after the equator. The Venezuelan general [[e:juan-jose-flores|Juan José Flores]] became the first president. Ecuador annexed the [[e:galapagos-islands|Galápagos Islands]] in 1832.
republic-of-ecuador.r: Politics were shaped by rivalry between conservative [[e:quito|Quito]] and liberal [[e:guayaquil|Guayaquil]]. [[e:gabriel-garcia-moreno|Gabriel García Moreno]] built a strongly Catholic state until his assassination in 1875, while [[e:eloy-alfaro|Eloy Alfaro's]] Liberal Revolution of 1895 separated church and state and completed the [[e:guayaquil-and-quito-railway|Guayaquil-Quito railway]] in 1908. Exports of [[e:cacao|cacao]] and then bananas drove the economy. After war with [[e:peru|Peru]] in 1941, Ecuador lost much of its [[e:amazon|Amazon]] claim under the [[e:rio-protocol|Rio Protocol]] of 1942. Oil exports began in 1972.
republic-of-ecuador.e: Democracy returned in 1979. After a banking crisis, Ecuador adopted the US dollar in 2000. [[e:rafael-correa|Rafael Correa's]] government from 2007 to 2017 introduced a 2008 constitution recognising the rights of nature. Rising drug-related violence has marked recent years.

republic-of-siena.t: Florence's great Tuscan rival, a banking and wool republic whose Palazzo Pubblico frescoes picture the ideals of good government.
republic-of-siena.o: Siena's citizens took power from their [[e:bishop|bishop]] in the early 12th century, and consuls are recorded by 1125. Lying on the [[e:via-francigena|Via Francigena]] pilgrim road, the commune prospered from banking and trade and expanded its territory across southern [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Tuscany]].
republic-of-siena.r: Siena was generally Ghibelline and crushed [[s:duchy-of-florence|Florence]] at [[e:battle-of-montaperti|Montaperti]] in 1260 under leaders such as [[e:provenzan-salvani|Provenzan Salvani]]. From 1287 to 1355 the merchant government of the Nine built the [[e:palazzo-pubblico-siena|Palazzo Pubblico]], where [[e:ambrogio-lorenzetti|Ambrogio Lorenzetti]] painted his [[e:allegory-of-good-and-bad-government|Allegory of Good and Bad Government]] in 1338–1339. [[e:duccio|Duccio]] and [[e:simone-martini|Simone Martini]] made the city a centre of painting. The [[e:black-death|Black Death]] of 1348 halted its growth; the [[e:banca-monte-dei-paschi-di-siena|Monte dei Paschi]] bank dates from 1472.
republic-of-siena.e: After a period of rule by [[e:pandolfo-petrucci|Pandolfo Petrucci]], Siena rebelled against a Spanish garrison in 1552. Imperial and Florentine troops besieged it until it surrendered in April 1555. Exiles continued as the [[s:republic-of-siena-at-montalcino|Republic of Siena at Montalcino]], and Siena was granted to the [[s:duchy-of-florence|Duchy of Florence]] in 1557.

republic-of-katagalugan.t: Last revolutionary republic of the Philippine-American War, led by Macario Sakay in the mountains of southern Luzon.
republic-of-katagalugan.o: After the [[s:united-states|United States]] declared the [[e:philippine-american-war|Philippine-American War]] over in 1902, the former Katipunan member [[e:macario-sakay|Macario Sakay]] refused to accept defeat. In 1902 he revived the name of [[e:andres-bonifacio|Andres Bonifacio's]] [[s:tagalog-republic|Tagalog Republic]] and proclaimed the Republic of Katagalugan, with himself as president, in the hills of [[e:rizal-province|Rizal]] and neighbouring provinces.
republic-of-katagalugan.r: The republic had a constitution, a cabinet and a flag, and it organised [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrilla]] bands that raided towns in [[e:rizal-province|Rizal]], Cavite, [[e:laguna-province|Laguna]] and [[e:batangas|Batangas]]. American authorities labelled its fighters bandits under the [[e:brigandage-act|Brigandage Act]] of 1902 and used reconcentration of villagers to cut them off from support.
republic-of-katagalugan.e: In July 1906 [[e:macario-sakay|Sakay]] surrendered after the labour leader [[e:dominador-gomez|Dominador Gomez]] promised amnesty, but he was arrested, tried for banditry and hanged in 1907. He is now honoured as a Filipino patriot.

republic-of-sale.t: A corsair republic of Morisco exiles at the mouth of the Bou Regreg, whose ships raided from the Atlantic coasts to Iceland.
republic-of-sale.o: [[e:moriscos|Moriscos]] expelled from [[e:spain|Spain]] between 1609 and 1614, among them the [[e:hornacheros|Hornacheros]] from [[e:extremadura|Extremadura]], settled in the kasbah of [[e:rabat|Rabat]] opposite [[e:sale|Salé]]. In 1627 they declared independence from the [[s:saadi-sultanate|Saadi Sultanate]], forming a self-governing corsair state.
republic-of-sale.r: The republic was ruled by a council, the divan, and an elected governor. Its corsairs, including the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] renegade [[e:jan-janszoon|Jan Janszoon]], known as Murat Reis, raided European shipping and coasts, and in 1627 raiders reached [[s:republic-of-iceland|Iceland]]. Captives were ransomed or sold, and European powers signed treaties and bombarded the port in turn. Feuds divided the [[e:hornacheros|Hornacheros]] and later Andalusi settlers.
republic-of-sale.e: From 1641 the [[s:dilaiyya|Dila'iyya]] dominated [[e:sale|Salé]], and in 1668 the Alaouite ruler [[e:al-rashid-of-morocco|Moulay al-Rashid]] took the twin towns. Corsairing continued under the [[s:alaouite-sultanate|Alaouite Sultanate]] into the 19th century.

republic-of-haiti-1806-1849.t: The southern Haitian republic of Pétion and Boyer, which reunited Haiti, ruled all of Hispaniola for two decades and paid France a crushing indemnity.
republic-of-haiti-1806-1849.o: After the assassination of Jacques I in 1806, [[e:alexandre-petion|Alexandre Pétion]] and the southern elite drafted a republican constitution that limited presidential power, prompting [[e:henri-christophe|Henri Christophe]] to found a rival state in the north. Pétion was elected president of the republic, based at [[e:port-au-prince|Port-au-Prince]], in 1807, and the two halves fought an inconclusive civil war.
republic-of-haiti-1806-1849.r: [[e:alexandre-petion|Pétion]] broke up state plantations and distributed land to soldiers and smallholders, creating a peasant economy based on [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] and food crops. He sheltered and armed [[e:simon-bolivar|Simón Bolívar]] in 1815 to 1816. His successor [[e:jean-pierre-boyer|Jean-Pierre Boyer]] reunited the north in 1820 and occupied the east in 1822. In 1825 he accepted [[e:france|France's]] demand for an indemnity of 150 million francs in return for recognition, a debt that burdened [[s:first-empire-of-haiti|Haiti]] for generations.
republic-of-haiti-1806-1849.e: [[e:jean-pierre-boyer|Boyer]] was overthrown in 1843, and the [[s:first-dominican-republic|Dominican Republic]] broke away in 1844. A string of short presidencies followed until the senate chose [[e:faustin-soulouque|Faustin Soulouque]] in 1847; he proclaimed himself emperor in 1849, creating the [[s:second-empire-of-haiti|Second Empire of Haiti]].

rani.t: A Slavic people on the island of Rügen whose temple of Svantevit at Arkona was the last great pagan sanctuary on the Baltic until the Danes destroyed it.
rani.o: The Rani were West Slavic settlers of the island of [[s:principality-of-rugen|Rügen]] and nearby coast from around the 8th or 9th century. Their island position and the prestige of their sanctuary gave them influence over neighbouring Slavic peoples, and they are mentioned in German and Danish chronicles from the 10th century.
rani.r: The Rani were ruled by princes, but [[e:saxo-grammaticus|Saxo Grammaticus]] and [[e:helmold-of-bosau|Helmold of Bosau]] describe the high priest of [[e:arkona|Arkona]] as the real power. The temple of the four-faced god [[e:svantevit|Svantevit]] stood on a cliff at Cape Arkona, receiving tribute from other [[e:slavs|Slavs]] and keeping a sacred white horse for divination. The Rani raided Danish coasts and traded across the Baltic.
rani.e: In 1168 [[e:valdemar-i-of-denmark|King Valdemar I of Denmark]] and [[e:absalon|Bishop Absalon]] captured [[e:arkona|Arkona]] and destroyed the idol of [[e:svantevit|Svantevit]]. Prince [[e:jaromar-i-of-rugen|Jaromar I]] accepted [[e:christianity|Christianity]] and Danish overlordship, founding the [[s:principality-of-rugen|Principality of Rügen]], which lasted until its absorption into the [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Duchy of Pomerania]] in 1325.

republic-of-cospaia.t: A tiny Umbrian republic born of a surveying error in 1440 that lived for nearly four centuries largely on tax-free tobacco.
republic-of-cospaia.o: In 1440 [[e:pope-eugene-iv|Pope Eugene IV]] sold [[e:sansepolcro|Borgo Sansepolcro]] to the [[s:republic-of-florence|Republic of Florence]]. The new border was set along a stream, but two streams had the same name, and a strip of land about two kilometres long between them was left out of both states. Its few hundred inhabitants declared themselves independent.
republic-of-cospaia.r: Cospaia had no army, no prisons and no written constitution; a council of elders and heads of families settled affairs in the church. Its motto, Perpetua et firma libertas, was carved over the church door. From the 16th century the villagers grew tobacco, which escaped the monopolies and taxes of the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]] and the [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Grand Duchy of Tuscany]], and the hamlet became a centre for smuggling.
republic-of-cospaia.e: In 1826 the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]] and [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Tuscany]] agreed to divide the territory. The inhabitants accepted in return for a [[e:silver|silver]] coin each and the right to keep growing tobacco.

regional-defence-council-of-aragon.t: An anarchist-led regional government in eastern Aragon during the Spanish Civil War, known for its sweeping rural collectives.
regional-defence-council-of-aragon.o: In the summer of 1936 anarchist militia columns from [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]] advanced into eastern Aragon, where collectives sprang up in hundreds of villages. In October 1936 the [[e:confederacion-nacional-del-trabajo|CNT]] created the Regional Defence [[e:council-of-aragon|Council of Aragon]], first at [[e:fraga|Fraga]] and then at [[e:caspe|Caspe]], under [[e:joaquin-ascaso|Joaquín Ascaso]].
regional-defence-council-of-aragon.r: The council organised the collectivisation of land and trade, in some villages abolishing money, and coordinated supplies for the Aragon front. It was later broadened to include other Republican parties and was recognised by [[e:francisco-largo-caballero|Largo Caballero]]'s government in December 1936, though Communists and Republicans criticised it.
regional-defence-council-of-aragon.e: After the [[e:barcelona-may-days|May Days of 1937]] weakened the anarchists, the [[e:juan-negrin|Negrín]] government dissolved the council in August 1937. [[e:enrique-lister|Enrique Líster's]] troops arrested its leaders and broke up many collectives. Aragon was overrun by [[e:francisco-franco|Franco]] in 1938.

republic-of-iceland.t: Independent Icelandic republic proclaimed at Þingvellir in 1944, a small NATO member famous for its fisheries disputes and parliamentary tradition.
republic-of-iceland.o: After a referendum in which Icelanders voted overwhelmingly to end the union with [[e:denmark|Denmark]], the [[s:kingdom-of-iceland|Kingdom of Iceland]] became a republic on 17 June 1944, the birthday of the independence leader [[e:jon-sigurdsson|Jón Sigurðsson]], in a ceremony at [[e:thingvellir|Þingvellir]]. [[e:sveinn-bjornsson|Sveinn Björnsson]] became its first president.
republic-of-iceland.r: Iceland is a parliamentary republic governed through the [[e:althing|Althing]]. It has no army but joined [[e:nato|NATO]] as a founding member in 1949, and a US base operated at [[e:keflavik|Keflavík]] until 2006. Fishing dominated the economy, and Iceland extended its fishing limits in the Cod Wars with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] between 1958 and 1976. In 1980 [[e:vigdis-finnbogadottir|Vigdís Finnbogadóttir]] became the world's first democratically elected female president.
republic-of-iceland.e: Iceland grew prosperous, diversifying into aluminium smelting with geothermal and hydro power, and tourism. Its banking system collapsed in 2008, but the economy recovered. It remains outside the EU but belongs to the [[e:european-economic-area|European Economic Area]] and the [[e:schengen-area|Schengen Area]].

rhodesia.t: The unrecognised white-minority state declared by Ian Smith in 1965, which fought a long guerrilla war before giving way to Zimbabwe.
rhodesia.o: After the end of the [[s:federation-of-rhodesia-and-nyasaland|Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland]], [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] insisted on progress towards majority rule before independence. Rather than accept this, [[e:ian-smith|Ian Smith's]] [[e:rhodesian-front|Rhodesian Front]] government of [[s:southern-rhodesia|Southern Rhodesia]] issued a [[e:unilateral-declaration-of-independence-rhodesia|Unilateral Declaration of Independence]] on 11 November 1965, keeping [[e:harare|Salisbury]] as the capital.
rhodesia.r: No state recognised Rhodesia, and the [[e:united-nations|United Nations]] imposed [[e:sanctions|sanctions]], though trade continued through [[s:republic-of-south-africa|South Africa]] and [[s:portuguese-mozambique|Portuguese Mozambique]]. A republic was declared in 1970 with [[e:clifford-dupont|Clifford Dupont]] as president. From the late 1960s and especially after 1972, [[e:zimbabwe-african-national-union|ZANU]] and [[e:zimbabwe-african-peoples-union|ZAPU]] [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrillas]] fought the [[e:rhodesian-bush-war|Bush War]], known to nationalists as the second Chimurenga; tens of thousands died and white emigration grew.
rhodesia.e: Under military and economic pressure, [[e:ian-smith|Smith]] signed an Internal Settlement in March 1978 with moderate African leaders including [[e:abel-muzorewa|Abel Muzorewa]], and the state was renamed [[s:zimbabwe-rhodesia|Zimbabwe Rhodesia]] in June 1979.

republic-of-alba.t: A republic proclaimed for a few days in the Piedmontese town of Alba in 1796, the first Jacobin republic on Italian soil.
republic-of-alba.o: As [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] army drove back the Piedmontese troops of the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]] in April 1796, local [[e:jacobin-club|Jacobins]] led by [[e:ignazio-bonafous|Ignazio Bonafous]] and the exiled publicist [[e:giovanni-antonio-ranza|Giovanni Antonio Ranza]] entered Alba and proclaimed a republic, hoping for French support for a revolution in [[e:piedmont|Piedmont]].
republic-of-alba.r: The republic planted a liberty tree and issued proclamations calling on the Piedmontese to rise, but it had no real institutions and relied on the presence of French troops. Its leaders hoped to spread the revolution to other towns of southern [[e:piedmont|Piedmont]].
republic-of-alba.e: [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] preferred to make peace with the king. The [[e:armistice-of-cherasco|Armistice of Cherasco]], signed on 28 April 1796, returned Alba to the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]], and the republic disappeared after only a few days.

rus-khaganate.t: A shadowy 9th-century polity of Scandinavian Rus' whose ruler took the title khagan, predecessor of the state of Kievan Rus'.
rus-khaganate.o: In 839 envoys of a people called the Rhos, whose ruler was styled chacanus, reached the court of [[e:louis-the-pious|Louis the Pious]] with a Byzantine embassy and turned out to be Swedes. Historians use the term Rus' Khaganate for this polity of Scandinavian traders and warriors in north-western [[e:russia|Russia]], but its location, perhaps [[e:staraya-ladoga|Ladoga]] or the [[e:veliky-novgorod|Novgorod]] region, is debated.
rus-khaganate.r: Arab geographers such as [[e:ibn-rusta|Ibn Rusta]] describe the Rus' as living on a marshy island under a [[e:khagan|khagan]], collecting slaves and [[e:fur-trade|furs]] from the [[e:slavs|Slavs]] and selling them for [[e:silver|silver]]. The title was borrowed from the [[e:khazar-khaganate|Khazars]] and claimed equal rank with their ruler. The Rus' attack on [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] in 860 may have been launched from this state.
rus-khaganate.e: Its fate is unclear. The chronicle tradition of [[e:rurik|Rurik's]] arrival around 862 and Oleg's capture of [[e:kyiv|Kiev]] in 882 describes the creation of [[s:kievan-rus|Kievan Rus']], into which the earlier khaganate was presumably absorbed. Later Kievan rulers such as Vladimir I were still occasionally called [[e:khagan|khagan]].

republic-of-haiti.t: Haiti as a republic since 1859, shaped by an unpayable debt, US occupation, the Duvalier dictatorship and repeated disasters and crises.
republic-of-haiti.o: General [[e:fabre-geffrard|Fabre Geffrard]] overthrew Emperor [[e:faustin-soulouque|Faustin I]] in December 1858 and restored the republic in 1859. Geffrard signed a concordat with the Vatican in 1860, which brought French clergy to run churches and schools, and invited African American immigrants.
republic-of-haiti.r: Frequent revolts, often by peasant armies called cacos, toppled most 19th-century presidents. The indemnity to [[e:france|France]] and later loans drained revenue. The [[s:united-states|United States]] occupied [[s:first-empire-of-haiti|Haiti]] from 1915 to 1934, building roads but imposing forced labour and crushing resistance led by [[e:charlemagne-peralte|Charlemagne Péralte]]. [[e:francois-duvalier|François Duvalier]], elected in 1957, ruled with the [[e:tonton-macoute|Tonton Macoute]] militia; his son [[e:jean-claude-duvalier|Jean-Claude]] succeeded him in 1971. [[e:coffee-economy|Coffee]] and peasant farming sustained the economy as forests vanished.
republic-of-haiti.e: [[e:jean-claude-duvalier|Jean-Claude Duvalier]] fled in 1986. [[e:jean-bertrand-aristide|Jean-Bertrand Aristide]] was elected in 1990, overthrown in 1991 and removed again in 2004. An earthquake in 2010 killed over 200,000 people. After President [[e:jovenel-moise|Jovenel Moïse]] was assassinated in 2021, gangs took control of much of [[e:port-au-prince|Port-au-Prince]], and a transitional presidential council took office in 2024.
