republic-of-ragusa.t: Aristocratic merchant republic of Dubrovnik, which grew rich on Balkan and Mediterranean trade and kept its freedom for four and a half centuries.
republic-of-ragusa.o: Ragusa ([[e:dubrovnik|Dubrovnik]]) had been a Byzantine and then Venetian-ruled commune. In 1358, under the [[e:treaty-of-zadar|Treaty of Zadar]], [[e:venice|Venice]] gave up [[e:dalmatia|Dalmatia]] to [[e:louis-i-of-hungary|Louis I of Hungary]], and Ragusa became a self-governing republic under loose Hungarian protection.
republic-of-ragusa.r: Power lay with the noble Great Council; a rector served a one-month term to prevent anyone gaining personal power. Ragusan merchants carried [[e:silver|silver]], lead and goods from the [[s:kingdom-of-bosnia|Kingdom of Bosnia]] and Serbian mines, and their fleet traded across the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]]. The republic paid tribute to the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] from 1458 and stayed neutral, banned the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] in 1416 and set up early quarantine. Writers such as [[e:marin-drzic|Marin Držić]] and [[e:ivan-gundulic|Ivan Gundulić]] made it a centre of Croatian literature.
republic-of-ragusa.e: A great earthquake in 1667 devastated the city, but the republic recovered. French troops occupied it in 1806, and [[e:auguste-de-marmont|Marshal Marmont]] abolished it in 1808; it passed to [[e:austria|Austria]] in 1815 and is now part of [[e:croatia|Croatia]].

republic-of-cuba-in-arms.t: The insurgent republic proclaimed by Cuban rebels in their wars of independence against Spain, with its own constitutions, presidents and assembly.
republic-of-cuba-in-arms.o: On 10 October 1868 the planter [[e:carlos-manuel-de-cespedes|Carlos Manuel de Céspedes]] freed his enslaved workers and proclaimed independence at [[e:la-demajagua|La Demajagua]], starting the [[e:ten-years-war|Ten Years' War]]. In April 1869 an assembly at [[e:constitution-of-guaimaro|Guáimaro]] adopted a constitution creating the Republic of [[e:cuba|Cuba]] in Arms, with Céspedes as president.
republic-of-cuba-in-arms.r: The republic had no fixed capital; its government moved through the eastern countryside held by rebel armies. A legislative House of Representatives often clashed with the president and deposed [[e:carlos-manuel-de-cespedes|Céspedes]] in 1873. Generals [[e:maximo-gomez|Máximo Gómez]] and [[e:antonio-maceo|Antonio Maceo]] led the fighting. After the [[e:pact-of-zanjon|Pact of Zanjón]] of 1878 the republic lapsed. [[e:jose-marti|José Martí's]] [[e:cuban-revolutionary-party|Cuban Revolutionary Party]] relaunched the war in 1895, and new constitutions at Jimaguayú in 1895 and La Yaya in 1897 revived it.
republic-of-cuba-in-arms.e: The [[s:united-states|United States]] intervened in 1898 and defeated [[e:spain|Spain]], but excluded the Cuban republic from the peace talks. Its assembly dissolved itself in 1899, and [[e:cuba|Cuba]] passed under the [[s:united-states-military-government-in-cuba|United States Military Government in Cuba]].

rajauri-state.t: A hill state on the road from the Punjab to Kashmir, known as Rajapuri in Kashmiri chronicles and ruled in later centuries by Muslim Jarral Rajas.
rajauri-state.o: Rajapuri appears in [[e:rajatarangini|Kalhana's Rajatarangini]] as a hill kingdom bordering [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]]. Tradition holds that the Jarral dynasty, [[e:rajputs|Rajputs]] who became Muslim, took power around 1194.
rajauri-state.r: Rajauri controlled a stage on the Mughal road over the [[e:pir-panjal-range|Pir Panjal]] to [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]], which the emperors used on their journeys to the valley; Mughal gardens and inns survive along it. In the early 19th century Raja Agar Khan dealt with and fought against the [[s:sikh-empire|Sikh Empire]] during [[e:ranjit-singh|Ranjit Singh's]] Kashmir campaigns.
rajauri-state.e: Rajauri fell under [[e:sikhism|Sikh]] control and then to [[e:gulab-singh|Gulab Singh of Jammu]], and in 1846 it became part of [[s:jammu-and-kashmir-princely-state|Jammu and Kashmir (princely state)]]. It is now a district of [[e:jammu|Jammu]] and [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]].

realm-of-jovan-nenad.t: Brief Serbian realm in the southern Hungarian plain, created by the self-proclaimed tsar Jovan Nenad in the chaos after the battle of Mohács.
realm-of-jovan-nenad.o: After the Ottoman victory at [[e:battle-of-mohacs|Mohács]] in 1526, a Serbian adventurer known as [[e:jovan-nenad|Jovan Nenad]], the Black Man, gathered an army of Serbian refugees and peasants in [[e:backa|Bačka]] and [[e:banat|Banat]] that may have numbered 15,000. He drove off Ottoman raiders, took control of the region and proclaimed himself tsar, setting up his court at [[e:subotica|Subotica]].
realm-of-jovan-nenad.r: His realm was a military regime resting on his army, which lived from the land and from requisitions on Hungarian nobles. In the contest for the Hungarian throne [[e:jovan-nenad|Jovan Nenad]] first backed [[e:john-zapolya|John Zápolya]], then switched to [[e:ferdinand-i-holy-roman-emperor|Ferdinand of Habsburg]]. His claim to a Serbian imperial title and his origins remain obscure, and contemporary accounts are partisan.
realm-of-jovan-nenad.e: [[e:john-zapolya|Zápolya]]'s forces defeated [[e:jovan-nenad|Jovan Nenad]] in the summer of 1527, and he was killed soon afterwards near [[e:szeged|Szeged]]. His army dispersed and the region fell to the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] within a few years. Serbian tradition remembers him as a forerunner of later Serbian autonomy in [[e:vojvodina|Vojvodina]].

recherla-nayakas.t: Telugu warrior rulers of Rachakonda and Devarakonda who replaced the Musunuris in Telangana and allied with the Bahmanis.
recherla-nayakas.o: The Recherla family were [[e:velama|Velama]] [[e:nayaka|Nayaka]] commanders who had served the [[s:kakatiya-dynasty|Kakatiya dynasty]]. In the 1360s, allied with the [[s:bahmani-sultanate|Bahmani Sultanate]], [[e:anapota-nayaka|Anapota Nayaka]] defeated and killed [[e:kapaya-nayaka|Kapaya Nayaka]] of the [[s:musunuri-nayaks|Musunuri Nayaks]] around 1368 and established rule over [[e:telangana|Telangana]] from the [[e:hill-fort|hill forts]] of [[e:rachakonda|Rachakonda]] and [[e:devarakonda|Devarakonda]].
recherla-nayakas.r: The Recherlas, also called Padmanayakas, ruled through a network of [[e:hill-fort|hill forts]] and warrior families. Their courts supported [[e:telugu-language|Telugu]] and [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] writing; [[e:sarvajna-singabhupala|Sarvajna Singabhupala]] wrote the [[e:rasarnava-sudhakara|Rasarnava Sudhakara]], a treatise on poetics. They generally sided with the [[e:bahmani-sultanate|Bahmanis]] against the [[s:vijayanagara-empire|Vijayanagara Empire]] and the [[s:reddi-kingdom|Reddi Kingdom]].
recherla-nayakas.e: Over the 15th century the [[s:bahmani-sultanate|Bahmani Sultanate]] turned against its former allies and gradually annexed their forts; [[e:rachakonda|Rachakonda]] and [[e:devarakonda|Devarakonda]] were absorbed by about 1475. [[e:velama|Velama]] families later served as zamindars under the [[s:golconda-sultanate|Golconda Sultanate]] and the British.

republic-of-cuba-1902-1959.t: Independent Cuba under US tutelage, a sugar republic of dictators and reformers that ended when Fidel Castro's revolution drove out Batista.
republic-of-cuba-1902-1959.o: After the [[s:united-states-military-government-in-cuba|United States Military Government in Cuba]] ended, the [[s:republic-of-cuba|Republic of Cuba]] was inaugurated on 20 May 1902 with [[e:tomas-estrada-palma|Tomás Estrada Palma]] as president. Its constitution included the [[e:platt-amendment|Platt Amendment]], which allowed US intervention, and [[e:washington-dc|Washington]] soon used it, occupying the island again from 1906 to 1909.
republic-of-cuba-1902-1959.r: [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar]], largely owned by American firms, dominated the economy, and [[e:havana|Havana]] became a magnet for tourists and gamblers. [[e:gerardo-machado|Gerardo Machado's]] dictatorship from 1925 ended in revolution in 1933, after which the army sergeant [[e:fulgencio-batista|Fulgencio Batista]] became the power behind governments. The [[e:platt-amendment|Platt Amendment]] was repealed in 1934, and a progressive constitution was adopted in 1940. Batista served as elected president from 1940 to 1944, and corruption marked the governments of [[e:ramon-grau-san-martin|Grau]] and [[e:carlos-prio-socarras|Prío]] that followed.
republic-of-cuba-1902-1959.e: [[e:fulgencio-batista|Batista]] seized power in a coup in 1952. [[e:fidel-castro|Fidel Castro]] attacked the [[e:attack-on-the-moncada-barracks|Moncada barracks]] in 1953 and returned on the [[e:granma-yacht|Granma]] in 1956 to wage [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrilla]] war in the [[e:sierra-maestra|Sierra Maestra]]. Batista fled on 1 January 1959, and the revolutionary [[s:republic-of-cuba|Republic of Cuba]] began.

ramdurg-state.t: A small Maratha Brahmin state in the southern Maratha country, ruled by a branch of the family of Nargund.
ramdurg-state.o: Ramdurg and Nargund were held by the Bhave family, [[e:brahmins|Brahmin]] officials of the [[e:peshwa|Peshwas]]. Around 1799 the holding was divided, and Ramdurg became a separate state under a branch of the family.
ramdurg-state.r: Under British rule Ramdurg was a minor state of the [[e:southern-maratha-country|Southern Maratha Country]], later the [[e:deccan-states-agency|Deccan States Agency]]. Its population was mainly [[e:kannada|Kannada]]-speaking farmers. In 1939 peasant agitation for responsible government ended in violence and police firing.
ramdurg-state.e: After accession to [[e:india|India]] Ramdurg was merged into [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]] in 1948, and since 1956 its lands have been in [[e:belagavi|Belagavi]] district of [[e:karnataka|Karnataka]].

republic-of-liege.t: The short-lived revolutionary government of Liège, which drove out its prince-bishop in 1789 in a 'happy revolution' inspired by events in Paris.
republic-of-liege.o: Resentment against the authoritarian prince-[[e:bishop|bishop]] [[e:constantin-francois-de-hoensbroeck|Constantin-François de Hoensbroeck]] had grown among Liège's [[e:burghers|burghers]] and Enlightenment-minded elites. On 18 August 1789, weeks after the fall of the [[e:storming-of-the-bastille|Bastille]], citizens seized the town hall and installed new mayors; the prince-bishop fled, and the [[s:prince-bishopric-of-liege|Prince-Bishopric of Liège]] came under patriot control.
republic-of-liege.r: The patriots, led by [[e:jacques-joseph-fabry|Jacques-Joseph Fabry]] and [[e:jean-remy-de-chestret|Jean-Rémy de Chestret]], governed through a revived city council and the estates, proclaimed the rights of citizens and sought support from [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], whose troops briefly occupied the city. The revolution was largely bloodless and called the 'happy revolution', though divisions grew between moderates and radicals.
republic-of-liege.e: After [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] withdrew, Austrian troops of the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]] restored the prince-[[e:bishop|bishop]] in January 1791. His return was brief: French armies arrived in 1792 and again in 1794, and [[s:prince-bishopric-of-liege|Liège]] was annexed to [[e:france|France]] in 1795.

ringerike.t: Inland petty kingdom north-west of Oslo whose last king, Sigurd Syr, was stepfather of Saint Olaf and father of Harald Hardrada.
ringerike.o: Ringerike lay around [[e:tyrifjorden|Lake Tyrifjorden]] in the inland [[e:upplands-norway|Upplands]] of eastern [[e:norway|Norway]]. The sagas name a king Sigurd Hart as ruler here in the 9th century and make his daughter the mother of [[e:harald-fairhair|Harald Fairhair]]. Like its neighbours, it was a farming district ruled by local kings who might accept a more powerful overlord.
ringerike.r: The area was fertile and well settled, and its kings held large estates. Ringerike lent its name to an art style of the early 11th century, seen on carved stones quarried in the district, with tendrils and animal motifs. Local kings kept their titles under the overlordship of [[e:harald-fairhair|Harald Fairhair's]] successors.
ringerike.e: Its best-known king, [[e:sigurd-syr|Sigurd Syr]], married [[e:asta-gudbrandsdatter|Åsta]], mother of [[e:olaf-ii-of-norway|Olaf Haraldsson]], and supported Olaf's bid for the Norwegian throne in 1015. Sigurd died around 1018, and Olaf soon put an end to the [[e:upplands-norway|Uppland]] petty kings, so Ringerike became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-norway|Kingdom of Norway]]. Sigurd's son was [[e:harald-hardrada|Harald Hardrada]].

ritsuryo-japan.t: The classical Japanese imperial state of the Nara and Heian periods, governed by Chinese-style law codes and home to the courtly culture of The Tale of Genji.
ritsuryo-japan.o: The [[e:taiho-code|Taiho code]] of 701 gave [[e:japan|Japan]] a full system of penal and administrative law modelled on [[e:tang-dynasty|Tang China]], completing reforms begun under [[s:yamato|Yamato]]. In 710 the court moved to the planned capital of [[e:heijo-kyo|Heijo-kyo]] at [[e:nara|Nara]], and the first histories, the [[e:kojiki|Kojiki]] of 712 and the [[e:nihon-shoki|Nihon shoki]] of 720, presented the emperors as descendants of the sun goddess.
ritsuryo-japan.r: A [[e:daijo-kan|Council of State]], eight ministries and provincial governors administered land allotted to cultivators in return for taxes and labour. Emperor [[e:emperor-shomu|Shomu]] built [[e:todai-ji|Todai-ji]] with its Great Buddha, dedicated in 752. [[e:emperor-kanmu|Kammu]] moved the capital to [[e:heian-kyo|Heian-kyo]] in 794. From the 9th century [[e:fujiwara-clan|Fujiwara]] regents ruled in the emperor's name, and court women wrote masterpieces in the new kana script.
ritsuryo-japan.e: Private estates eroded the tax base and provincial warriors grew powerful. The [[e:genpei-war|Genpei War]] of 1180 to 1185 brought [[e:minamoto-no-yoritomo|Minamoto no Yoritomo]] to power and the [[s:kamakura-shogunate|Kamakura shogunate]], though the imperial court survived in [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]].

rai-dynasty.t: A dynasty of Sindh known from the Chach Nama, which ruled the lower Indus from Aror before the Brahman dynasty took power.
rai-dynasty.o: The Rai dynasty is known almost entirely from the [[e:chach-nama|Chach Nama]], a Persian history of the Arab conquest of [[e:sindh|Sindh]] written in the 13th century from earlier Arabic sources. It describes a line of five kings ruling Sindh from [[e:aror|Aror]], near modern [[e:sukkur|Sukkur]], from around the end of the 5th century.
rai-dynasty.r: The [[e:chach-nama|Chach Nama]] portrays a large kingdom stretching from [[e:kashmir|Kashmir's]] borders to the sea and from [[s:makran-state|Makran]] to the edge of [[e:rajasthan|Rajasthan]], divided into provinces under governors. [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] was widespread in [[e:sindh|Sindh]] in this period, as [[e:xuanzang|Xuanzang]] confirms, and the dynasty was reportedly Buddhist or tolerant of Buddhism. One king is said to have died fighting an army from Sasanian [[e:persia|Persia]].
rai-dynasty.e: According to the [[e:chach-nama|Chach Nama]], after the death of the last king, [[e:rai-sahasi-ii|Rai Sahasi II]], his [[e:brahmins|Brahmin]] chamberlain [[s:principality-of-chach|Chach]] married the widowed queen and seized the throne around 632, founding the [[s:brahman-dynasty-of-sindh|Brahman dynasty of Sindh]].

revolutionary-government-of-the-philippi.t: Government set up by Emilio Aguinaldo in 1898 that declared Philippine independence from Spain and prepared the Malolos Republic.
revolutionary-government-of-the-philippi.o: After the [[s:united-states|United States]] destroyed the Spanish fleet at [[e:manila|Manila]] Bay on 1 May 1898, [[e:emilio-aguinaldo|Emilio Aguinaldo]] returned from exile in [[e:hong-kong|Hong Kong]] and on 24 May proclaimed a dictatorial government at Cavite. He declared independence at [[e:kawit|Kawit]] on 12 June 1898, and on the advice of [[e:apolinario-mabini|Apolinario Mabini]] converted his regime into a Revolutionary Government on 23 June.
revolutionary-government-of-the-philippi.r: [[e:emilio-aguinaldo|Aguinaldo]] ruled as president with a cabinet of secretaries, while provincial and municipal governments were organised in liberated areas. Revolutionary armies took most of [[e:luzon|Luzon]] from Spanish garrisons. A congress met at [[e:barasoain-church|Barasoain church]] in [[e:malolos|Malolos]] in September 1898 and drafted the [[e:malolos-constitution|Malolos Constitution]], drawing on Spanish and [[e:latin|Latin]] American models.
revolutionary-government-of-the-philippi.e: The [[s:united-states|United States]] refused to recognise the government, and the [[e:treaty-of-paris-1898|Treaty of Paris]] of December 1898 transferred the islands from [[e:spain|Spain]] to America. The Revolutionary Government gave way to the [[s:first-philippine-republic|First Philippine Republic]] on 23 January 1899.

cr.a: See File history below for details.

roman-egypt.t: Egypt as the richest province of the Roman and Byzantine empires, the granary of Rome and a cradle of Christian monasticism.
roman-egypt.o: After the deaths of [[e:mark-antony|Antony]] and [[e:cleopatra-vii|Cleopatra VII]] in 30 BCE, Octavian annexed the [[e:ptolemaic-kingdom|Ptolemaic Empire's]] heartland. [[e:egypt|Egypt]] was governed by an equestrian prefect answerable to the emperor alone, and senators were forbidden to enter without permission, so valuable was its grain.
roman-egypt.r: [[e:egypt|Egypt's]] harvest fed [[e:rome|Rome]] and later [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]]. [[e:alexandria|Alexandria]] remained a great centre of Greek learning, home to Ptolemy, [[e:plotinus|Plotinus]] and the [[e:catechetical-school-of-alexandria|Catechetical School]]. Papyri from [[e:oxyrhynchus|Oxyrhynchus]] document daily life in detail. [[e:christianity|Christianity]] spread quickly: Anthony and [[e:pachomius-the-great|Pachomius]] founded desert monasticism and [[e:athanasius-of-alexandria|Athanasius]] shaped orthodoxy. After the [[e:council-of-chalcedon|Council of Chalcedon]] in 451, most [[e:egyptians|Egyptians]] followed the [[e:coptic-orthodox-church|Coptic Church]] against the imperial church, and Coptic writing developed from Egyptian.
roman-egypt.e: The [[e:persians|Persians]] occupied [[e:egypt|Egypt]] as [[s:sasanian-egypt|Sasanian Egypt]] from 619 to 629, and [[e:heraclius|Heraclius]] recovered it. In 639 to 641 [[e:amr-ibn-al-as|Amr ibn al-As]] invaded for the [[s:rashidun-caliphate|Rashidun Caliphate]], and [[e:alexandria|Alexandria]] surrendered by treaty, ending nearly seven centuries of Roman rule.

roman-cyrenaica.t: The Roman and Byzantine province of eastern Libya, a Greek-speaking land of five cities on the Jebel Akhdar.
roman-cyrenaica.o: [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]] was bequeathed to [[e:rome|Rome]] by [[e:ptolemy-apion|Ptolemy Apion]] of the [[s:ptolemaic-kingdom-of-cyrene|Ptolemaic Kingdom of Cyrene]] in 96 BCE and organised as a province in 74 BCE. After [[e:quintus-caecilius-metellus-creticus|Quintus Metellus]] conquered [[e:crete|Crete]] in 67 BCE, the two were joined, by the time of Augustus, as the province of Crete and Cyrenaica, administered by a proconsul.
roman-cyrenaica.r: The Greek cities of the [[e:pentapolis-cyrenaica|Pentapolis]], [[s:republic-of-cyrene|Cyrene]], [[e:apollonia-cyrenaica|Apollonia]], [[s:barca|Ptolemais]], [[e:taucheira|Taucheira]] and [[s:euesperides|Berenice]], kept [[e:greek-language|Greek language]] and institutions. The region exported grain and wine, though silphium died out under Roman rule. A large Jewish community rose in the revolt of 115 to 117 CE, devastating Cyrene. [[e:diocletian|Diocletian]] split the region into [[e:libya|Libya]] Superior and [[e:libya-inferior|Libya Inferior]]. [[e:synesius|Bishop Synesius of Ptolemais]] described raids by the [[s:austuriani|Austuriani]] around 400.
roman-cyrenaica.e: From 395 the province belonged to the [[s:byzantine-empire|Byzantine Empire]], but its cities declined. In 642 to 643 Arab forces under [[e:amr-ibn-al-as|Amr ibn al-As]] took [[s:barca|Barca]] and the [[e:pentapolis-cyrenaica|Pentapolis]] for the [[s:rashidun-caliphate|Rashidun Caliphate]], and the region became an Islamic province known as [[e:cyrenaica|Barqa]].

republic-of-lower-california.t: Paper republic proclaimed by the American filibuster William Walker after his raid on Baja California in 1853, which collapsed within months.
republic-of-lower-california.o: [[e:william-walker|William Walker]], a Tennessee-born adventurer, sailed from [[e:san-francisco|San Francisco]] with about 45 men and landed at [[e:la-paz-baja-california-sur|La Paz]] in November 1853. He arrested the governor and declared [[e:baja-california|Baja California]] an independent republic with himself as president, then moved north to [[e:ensenada|Ensenada]].
republic-of-lower-california.r: The republic existed mainly on paper. In January 1854 [[e:william-walker|Walker]] also proclaimed the Republic of [[e:sonora|Sonora]], claiming the mainland state, and introduced the laws of [[e:louisiana|Louisiana]], including [[e:slavery|slavery]]. His men had little food or money, many deserted, and Mexican forces and local ranchers harassed them. He controlled only a few settlements on the Pacific coast.
republic-of-lower-california.e: [[e:william-walker|Walker]]'s attempt to march into [[e:sonora|Sonora]] failed, and in May 1854 he and his remaining men surrendered to US forces at the border. He was tried in [[e:san-francisco|San Francisco]] for violating neutrality laws and acquitted. He later seized power in [[s:republic-of-nicaragua|Nicaragua]] and was executed in [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]] in 1860.

rairakhol-state.t: A small, forested princely state in western Odisha, one of the Garhjat states ruled by local Rajas until 1948.
rairakhol-state.o: The ruling family was connected with the [[e:chauhan|Chauhan]] rulers of [[s:sambalpur-state|Sambalpur State]], and tradition dates the state to around 1500. Its early history is poorly recorded.
rairakhol-state.r: Rairakhol was a hilly, thinly populated state of forest and small farms. It was part of the [[s:sambalpur-state|Sambalpur]] group of chiefships under the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] and came under British supervision in the 19th century, joining the [[e:orissa-tributary-states|Orissa Tributary States]] in 1905.
rairakhol-state.e: Rairakhol merged into [[e:odisha|Orissa]] on 1 January 1948 and is now in [[s:sambalpur-state|Sambalpur]] district.

republic-of-brescia.t: A republic proclaimed in Brescia in March 1797 when the city overthrew Venetian rule, one of the blows that hastened the end of Venice.
republic-of-brescia.o: [[s:commune-of-brescia|Brescia]] had been a Venetian mainland city since 1426. On 18 March 1797, a few days after [[s:commune-of-bergamo|Bergamo]], local patriots backed by French troops and Bergamasque volunteers seized power, expelled the Venetian governor and proclaimed the Brescian Republic.
republic-of-brescia.r: The provisional government abolished Venetian institutions, planted liberty trees and raised a national guard. It sent forces to spread the revolt to the Brescian valleys and [[e:lake-garda|Lake Garda]] towns, where peasants loyal to [[e:venice|Venice]] and the Church resisted. It depended on French protection, and its leaders sought union with the [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] republics.
republic-of-brescia.e: After the fall of the [[s:republic-of-venice|Republic of Venice]] in May 1797, [[s:commune-of-brescia|Brescia]] was incorporated into the [[s:cisalpine-republic|Cisalpine Republic]] in late 1797.

republic-of-lithuania-1918-1940.t: Interwar independent Lithuania, ruled from Kaunas because of the loss of Vilnius, and later under the authoritarian presidency of Antanas Smetona.
republic-of-lithuania-1918-1940.o: On 16 February 1918 the [[e:council-of-lithuania|Council of Lithuania]] in [[e:vilnius|Vilnius]], chaired by [[e:antanas-smetona|Antanas Smetona]], declared independence at a session presided over by [[e:jonas-basanavicius|Jonas Basanavicius]]. After a brief attempt at the [[s:kingdom-of-lithuania-1918|Kingdom of Lithuania]] (1918), it fought Soviet, Bermontian and Polish forces. When [[e:poland|Poland]] seized Vilnius in 1920, [[e:kaunas|Kaunas]] became the temporary capital.
republic-of-lithuania-1918-1940.r: The constitution of 1922 created a parliamentary republic under presidents [[e:aleksandras-stulginskis|Aleksandras Stulginskis]] and [[e:kazys-grinius|Kazys Grinius]]. Land reform broke up great estates, and dairy and [[e:flax|flax]] exports grew. [[s:republic-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] took [[e:klaipeda|Klaipeda]] in 1923. In December 1926 a military coup restored [[e:antanas-smetona|Smetona]] as president, and he ruled in an authoritarian, nationalist style until 1940.
republic-of-lithuania-1918-1940.e: In 1939 [[s:republic-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] lost [[e:klaipeda|Klaipeda]] to [[s:nazi-germany|Nazi Germany]] and regained [[e:vilnius|Vilnius]] from the USSR. In June 1940 the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] occupied the country, and a staged parliament proclaimed the [[s:lithuanian-soviet-socialist-republic|Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic]]. [[e:antanas-smetona|Smetona]] fled abroad.

republic-of-paraguay.t: A landlocked South American republic shaped by long dictatorships and one of history's most devastating wars, and among the most bilingual nations in the world.
republic-of-paraguay.o: In 1811 [[e:paraguay|Paraguay]] defeated an army from [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]] under [[e:manuel-belgrano|Manuel Belgrano]] and in May overthrew the Spanish governor of the [[s:governorate-of-paraguay|Governorate of Paraguay]], becoming independent. [[e:jose-gaspar-rodriguez-de-francia|José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia]] ruled as dictator from 1814, and as perpetual dictator from 1816 until his death in 1840, closing the country to outside contact and confiscating church lands.
republic-of-paraguay.r: [[e:carlos-antonio-lopez|Carlos Antonio López]] opened [[e:paraguay|Paraguay]] and built railways and an ironworks. His son [[e:francisco-solano-lopez|Francisco Solano López]] led it into the War of the Triple Alliance against [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]], [[s:argentine-republic|Argentina]] and [[s:oriental-republic-of-uruguay|Uruguay]] from 1864 to 1870, in which Paraguay lost much of its population and territory. In the [[e:chaco-war|Chaco War]] of 1932 to 1935 it defeated the [[s:republic-of-bolivia|Republic of Bolivia]]. [[e:alfredo-stroessner|Alfredo Stroessner]] ruled from 1954 to 1989.
republic-of-paraguay.e: After [[e:alfredo-stroessner|Stroessner]]'s overthrow in 1989, [[e:paraguay|Paraguay]] adopted a democratic constitution in 1992. The [[e:itaipu-dam|Itaipú]] dam, shared with [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]], made it a major exporter of electricity, alongside soya and beef. [[e:guarani-language|Guaraní]] and Spanish are both official languages.

republic-of-india.t: The world's most populous country and largest democracy, a federal republic since its constitution came into force in 1950.
republic-of-india.o: The [[s:dominion-of-india|Dominion of India]] became a republic on 26 January 1950, when the constitution drafted by the Constituent Assembly under [[e:b-r-ambedkar|B. R. Ambedkar]] came into force. [[e:rajendra-prasad|Rajendra Prasad]] became the first president, while [[e:jawaharlal-nehru|Jawaharlal Nehru]] continued as prime minister, governing a federation of states and union territories from [[e:new-delhi|New Delhi]].
republic-of-india.r: [[e:india|India]] is a parliamentary democracy with universal suffrage, an independent judiciary and a federal structure; states were reorganised on linguistic lines from 1956. [[e:jawaharlal-nehru|Nehru]] pursued planned development and non-alignment. [[e:indira-gandhi|Indira Gandhi's]] Emergency of 1975 to 1977 suspended civil liberties. Wars were fought with [[e:china|China]] in 1962 and [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Pakistan]] in 1965 and 1971, nuclear tests followed in 1974 and 1998, and economic liberalisation began in 1991.
republic-of-india.e: The republic continues today with regular elections and coalition and single-party governments. It annexed [[e:goa|Goa]] from [[s:portuguese-india|Portuguese India]] in 1961 and [[s:kingdom-of-sikkim|Sikkim]] joined in 1975. [[e:india|India's]] population overtook [[e:china|China's]] around 2023.

republic-of-west-florida.t: A 74-day republic declared by American settlers in Spanish West Florida in 1810, swiftly annexed by the United States.
republic-of-west-florida.o: The strip of [[e:gulf-coast-of-the-united-states|Gulf Coast]] between the [[e:mississippi-river|Mississippi]] and [[e:perdido-river|Perdido]] rivers remained Spanish after the [[e:louisiana-purchase|Louisiana Purchase]], though the [[s:united-states|United States]] claimed it. Many settlers in the [[e:baton-rouge|Baton Rouge]] district were Americans. On 23 September 1810 rebels stormed the Spanish fort at Baton Rouge, and three days later a convention declared independence.
republic-of-west-florida.r: The republic adopted a constitution modelled on American practice, elected [[e:fulwar-skipwith|Fulwar Skipwith]] as governor and set its capital at [[e:st-francisville-louisiana|St. Francisville]]. It flew a blue flag with a single white star, later known as the [[e:bonnie-blue-flag|Bonnie Blue Flag]]. Its leaders hoped for admission to the [[s:united-states|United States]] on favourable terms, and it raised a small militia that tried to march on Mobile.
republic-of-west-florida.e: President [[e:james-madison|James Madison]] proclaimed the territory part of the [[s:united-states|United States]] in October 1810, and American troops took over in December. Most of it became the [[e:florida-parishes|Florida Parishes]] of [[e:louisiana|Louisiana]]; the area east of the [[e:pearl-river-mississippi-louisiana|Pearl River]] later went to [[e:mississippi-river|Mississippi]] and [[e:alabama|Alabama]].

republic-of-somaliland.t: A self-declared republic in northern Somalia, stable and democratic by regional standards, which has sought international recognition since 1991.
republic-of-somaliland.o: After the fall of [[e:siad-barre|Siad Barre]], the [[e:somali-national-movement|Somali National Movement]], which had fought his regime in the north, declared the restoration of [[e:italian-somaliland|Somaliland's]] independence at [[e:burao|Burao]] on 18 May 1991, within the borders of former [[s:british-somaliland|British Somaliland]]. A conference of clan elders at [[e:borama|Borama]] in 1993 chose [[e:muhammad-haji-ibrahim-egal|Muhammad Haji Ibrahim Egal]] as president.
republic-of-somaliland.r: [[s:state-of-somaliland|Somaliland]] built a hybrid system combining an elected president and parliament with a House of Elders, the [[e:house-of-elders-somaliland|Guurti]], rooted in clan institutions. After clan conflicts in the mid-1990s it has stayed largely peaceful, holding contested but competitive elections. Its economy depends on livestock exports, remittances and the port of [[e:berbera|Berbera]], developed with [[e:dp-world|DP World]] investment.
republic-of-somaliland.e: [[s:somalia|Somalia]] regards it as part of its territory, and recognition remains very limited: in December 2025 [[s:kingdom-of-israel|Israel]] became the first UN member state to recognise it. It maintains its own currency, army and passports, and power has changed hands through elections, as in 2024. Its capital is [[e:hargeisa|Hargeisa]].

republic-of-franceville.t: A short-lived self-governing commune at Port Vila in the New Hebrides, often said to be the first polity with universal suffrage regardless of sex or race.
republic-of-franceville.o: In 1887 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and [[e:france|France]] agreed that neither would annex the [[s:new-hebrides-condominium|New Hebrides]], leaving the islands without any government over the settlers. In 1889 residents of the [[e:port-vila|Port Vila]] area, mostly French settlers linked to the Société Française des Nouvelles-Hébrides, declared an independent municipality called Franceville.
republic-of-franceville.r: Its charter gave the vote to all adult residents, men and women, without regard to race, though only white men could hold office. It had a small elected council and an elected president, and it relied on the goodwill of planters and traders in a population of a few hundred Europeans and many more ni-[[e:vanuatu|Vanuatu]]. Little is recorded of its day-to-day administration.
republic-of-franceville.e: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and [[e:france|France]], unwilling to accept an independent settler state, refused to recognise it, and the commune collapsed in 1890. The islands later came under joint rule as the [[s:new-hebrides-condominium|New Hebrides Condominium]], and the site is now [[e:port-vila|Port Vila]], capital of [[e:vanuatu|Vanuatu]].

republic-of-crema.t: A brief Jacobin republic proclaimed in Crema in March 1797, when the town broke from Venice in the last weeks of the Serenissima.
republic-of-crema.o: [[e:crema|Crema]], a [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] town between [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]] and [[s:commune-of-cremona|Cremona]], had belonged to the [[s:republic-of-venice|Republic of Venice]] since 1449. On 28 March 1797, following the revolts of [[s:commune-of-bergamo|Bergamo]] and [[s:commune-of-brescia|Brescia]] and with French troops present, local patriots deposed the Venetian governor and proclaimed the Cremasque Republic.
republic-of-crema.r: The republic was a provisional government of local notables and [[e:jacobin-club|Jacobins]] under French protection. It abolished Venetian institutions and noble privileges, set up committees on the French model and looked to union with the new [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] republics. Little is known of its brief administration.
republic-of-crema.e: After the fall of [[e:venice|Venice]] in May 1797, [[e:crema|Crema]] was absorbed into the [[s:cisalpine-republic|Cisalpine Republic]] later that year, ending its separate existence.

republic-of-german-austria.t: The short-lived first Austrian republic of 1918-19, created from the German-speaking lands of the Habsburg monarchy and seeking union with Germany.
republic-of-german-austria.o: As [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]] dissolved, the German-speaking members of the Imperial Council formed a provisional national assembly on 21 October 1918. On 12 November 1918, the day after [[e:karl-i|Emperor Charles I]] withdrew from government, it proclaimed the Republic of German-[[e:austria|Austria]], declaring it part of the [[e:weimar-republic|German Republic]].
republic-of-german-austria.r: [[e:karl-renner|Karl Renner]] of the Social Democrats led the government as state chancellor. The republic claimed the [[e:sudetenland|Sudetenland]], [[e:south-tyrol|South Tyrol]] and other German-speaking areas, but could not enforce these claims. It faced hunger, [[e:inflation|inflation]], returning soldiers and a communist putsch attempt, and abolished the nobility and banished the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] in April 1919.
republic-of-german-austria.e: The [[e:treaty-of-saint-germain-en-laye-1919|Treaty of Saint-Germain]] in September 1919 forbade union with [[e:germany|Germany]] and set [[e:austria|Austria's]] borders. On 21 October 1919 the state was renamed the [[s:first-austrian-republic|Republic of Austria]], the First Austrian Republic.

republic-of-sassari.t: A self-governing Sardinian city-republic that rose from the ruins of the Judicate of Logudoro and wrote its laws partly in Sardinian.
republic-of-sassari.o: After the death of [[e:adelasia-of-torres|Adelasia]] ended the [[s:judicate-of-logudoro|Judicate of Logudoro]] in 1259, the growing town of Sassari took control of its own affairs and part of the surrounding territory. From 1272 it governed itself as a commune under Pisan influence, before allying with the [[s:republic-of-genoa|Republic of Genoa]] in 1294.
republic-of-sassari.r: The free commune was led by a podestà sent from [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] and local councils. Its statutes of 1316, the [[e:statutes-of-sassari|Statuti Sassaresi]], survive in [[e:latin|Latin]] and Sardinian versions and regulated trade, farming and justice. Sassari lived from grain, livestock and trade through [[e:porto-torres|Porto Torres]].
republic-of-sassari.e: In 1323 Sassari submitted to the [[e:alfonso-iv-of-aragon|Infante Alfonso]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-aragon|Kingdom of Aragon]] at the start of the Aragonese conquest, becoming part of the new [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]]. It revolted several times in the following years.

roman-kingdom.t: Rome under its seven kings, traditionally 753–509 BCE, when a Latin settlement on the Tiber became a city with temples, a forum and institutions that outlived the monarchy.
roman-kingdom.o: [[e:rome|Rome]] grew from [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] villages on the Palatine and nearby hills by the [[e:tiber-river|Tiber]] crossing. Tradition dated its founding by [[e:romulus|Romulus]] to 753 BCE; archaeology shows settlement from the 10th century BCE and the drainage and paving of the [[e:roman-forum|Forum]] around 650–600 BCE, when the villages became a single city.
roman-kingdom.r: The king (rex) ruled with the advice of a Senate of clan elders, and the people were organised in thirty curiae. Tradition credits [[e:numa-pompilius|Numa Pompilius]] with [[e:rome|Rome's]] religious institutions and [[e:servius-tullius|Servius Tullius]] with the [[e:census|census]] and a new army based on wealth classes. The last three kings had Etruscan links; under them Rome built the [[e:cloaca-maxima|Cloaca Maxima]] and the temple of [[e:jupiter-god|Jupiter]] on the [[e:capitoline-hill|Capitol]], and became the leading city of [[e:latium|Latium]].
roman-kingdom.e: Tradition says that after Sextus Tarquinius raped [[e:lucretia|Lucretia]], [[e:lucius-junius-brutus|Lucius Junius Brutus]] led the nobles in expelling [[e:tarquinius-superbus|Tarquinius Superbus]] in 509 BCE. The kingship was replaced by two annually elected consuls, founding the [[s:roman-republic|Roman Republic]]. The title rex survived only in a priesthood, and [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] long hated the very word.

rattanakosin-kingdom.t: Siam under the Chakri dynasty from the founding of Bangkok in 1782 to the 1932 revolution, the only Southeast Asian state to escape colonisation.
rattanakosin-kingdom.o: In 1782 [[e:rama-i|Chao Phraya Chakri]], [[e:taksin|Taksin's]] leading general, deposed the [[s:thonburi-kingdom|Thonburi Kingdom]]'s king and became [[e:rama|Rama]] I. He moved the capital across the [[e:chao-phraya-river|Chao Phraya]] to [[e:bangkok|Bangkok]], on Rattanakosin island, where he built the [[e:grand-palace|Grand Palace]] and installed the [[e:emerald-buddha|Emerald Buddha]] at [[e:wat-phra-kaew|Wat Phra Kaew]].
rattanakosin-kingdom.r: Early Chakri kings rebuilt Siamese power, reasserting control over [[s:lan-na|Lan Na]], the Lao kingdoms and [[s:kingdom-of-cambodia-1953-1970|Cambodia]]. [[e:rama-iii|Rama III]] expanded Chinese trade. [[e:mongkut|Mongkut]] signed the [[e:bowring-treaty|Bowring Treaty]] with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in 1855, opening the economy. [[e:chulalongkorn|Chulalongkorn]] abolished [[e:slavery|slavery]], created ministries and provincial administration, and built railways, while ceding [[e:laos|Laos]] and Cambodian provinces to [[e:france|France]] and Malay states to [[e:britain|Britain]] to keep independence.
rattanakosin-kingdom.e: Growing discontent among the educated elite led to the bloodless revolution of 24 June 1932 by the [[e:khana-ratsadon|Khana Ratsadon]], which ended absolute monarchy under [[e:prajadhipok|Prajadhipok]]. Siam continued as a [[e:constitutional-monarchy|constitutional monarchy]], renamed [[s:thailand|Thailand]] in 1939.

ryukyu-domain.t: The transitional status imposed on the Ryukyu Kingdom by Meiji Japan from 1872 until its annexation as Okinawa Prefecture in 1879.
ryukyu-domain.o: After the abolition of domains in mainland [[e:japan|Japan]] in 1871, the Meiji government moved to assert sole control over [[s:ryukyu-kingdom|Ryukyu]], which had long been a tributary of both [[e:qing-empire|Qing China]] and the [[s:satsuma-domain|Satsuma Domain]]. In 1872 [[e:sho-tai|King Sho Tai]] was named lord of the new Ryukyu Domain.
ryukyu-domain.r: The royal government at Shuri continued to run local affairs, but foreign relations passed to [[e:edo-tokyo|Tokyo]]. [[e:japan|Japan]] used the killing of shipwrecked Ryukyuan sailors in [[s:republic-of-china|Taiwan]] in 1871 to launch its [[e:taiwan|Taiwan]] expedition of 1874, presenting [[e:ryukyuans|Ryukyuans]] as Japanese subjects. In 1875 Tokyo ordered [[s:ryukyu-kingdom|Ryukyu]] to stop sending tribute to [[e:china|China]], which the court resisted.
ryukyu-domain.e: In 1879 the official [[e:matsuda-michiyuki|Matsuda Michiyuki]] arrived with police and troops, abolished the domain and created [[e:okinawa-prefecture|Okinawa Prefecture]]; [[e:sho-tai|Sho Tai]] was moved to [[e:edo-tokyo|Tokyo]]. The Qing protested, but the annexation stood.

republic-of-ararat.t: A Kurdish self-proclaimed republic around Mount Ararat, crushed by Turkey in 1930.
republic-of-ararat.o: After the failure of the Sheikh Said rebellion of 1925, Kurdish nationalists founded the [[e:xoybun|Xoybun]] league in 1927. That year, in October, it proclaimed a Kurdish republic in the region of [[e:mount-ararat|Mount Ararat]], near the borders with [[e:iran|Iran]] and the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]], with [[e:ihsan-nuri-pasha|Ihsan Nuri Pasha]] as military commander and the tribal leader [[e:ibrahim-heski|Ibrahim Heski]] as civil governor.
republic-of-ararat.r: The republic was a rebel administration based in the mountain villages, with its centre at Kurd Ava, relying on tribal fighters and support from Kurdish exiles. Its control was limited to the [[e:mount-ararat|Ararat]] massif and surrounding valleys.
republic-of-ararat.e: [[e:turkey|Turkey]] launched major campaigns in 1930, accompanied by mass killings in the Zilan valley. Turkish forces, operating close to and across the Iranian border, encircled the rebels, who were defeated by autumn 1930. Turkey and [[e:iran|Iran]] adjusted their border in 1932, giving Turkey the slopes of Little [[e:mount-ararat|Ararat]].

rinpungpa.t: A family of ministers from Tsang who overshadowed the Phagmodrupa kings and dominated western and central Tibet for over a century.
rinpungpa.o: The Rinpung family served the [[s:phagmodrupa-dynasty|Phagmodrupa dynasty]] as governors in the [[e:tsang|Tsang]] region of west-central [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]]. In 1435, after a succession crisis at the Phagmodru court, Norbu Zangpo of Rinpung seized the fortress of [[e:shigatse-dzong|Samdrubtse]] ([[e:shigatse|Shigatse]]), and the family became the real power in Tsang while still nominally serving the Phagmodru kings.
rinpungpa.r: The Rinpungpa governed through fortress-districts and alliances with local nobles. They were patrons of the [[e:karma-kagyu|Karma Kagyu]] school and its [[e:karmapa|Karmapa]] lamas, and under [[e:donyo-dorje|Donyö Dorje]], at the height of their power around 1500, they took control of the [[e:lhasa|Lhasa]] region and banned [[e:gelug|Gelug]] monks from Lhasa's great prayer festival between 1498 and 1517.
rinpungpa.e: Their power declined after 1512 through internal quarrels. [[e:zhingshak-tseten-dorje|Zhingshak Tseten Dorje]], a former Rinpungpa official at [[e:shigatse-dzong|Samdrubtse]], rebelled in the 1550s and in 1565 founded the [[s:tsangpa-dynasty|Tsangpa dynasty]], which took over Rinpung's position.

republic-of-estonia.t: The Estonian nation-state, declared in 1918, occupied by the Soviet Union from 1940 and restored in 1991 as a digital-minded EU and NATO member.
republic-of-estonia.o: The [[e:estonian-salvation-committee|Salvation Committee]] declared the Republic of [[e:estonia|Estonia]] on 24 February 1918, building on the [[s:autonomous-governorate-of-estonia|Autonomous Governorate of Estonia]]. After German occupation, Estonia fought the [[e:estonian-war-of-independence|War of Independence]] against [[s:russian-sfsr|Soviet Russia]] and the [[e:baltic-germans|Baltic German]] [[e:baltic-landeswehr|Landeswehr]], and the [[e:treaty-of-tartu-russian-estonian|Treaty of Tartu]] in February 1920 secured its independence.
republic-of-estonia.r: The interwar republic carried out a radical land reform breaking the [[e:baltic-germans|Baltic German]] estates, and granted cultural autonomy to minorities. [[e:konstantin-pats|Konstantin Päts]] ruled by decree from 1934. The [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] occupied [[e:estonia|Estonia]] in 1940, creating the [[s:estonian-soviet-socialist-republic|Estonian Soviet Socialist Republic]], followed by German occupation and renewed Soviet rule, with [[e:deportation|mass deportations]].
republic-of-estonia.e: The Singing Revolution of the late 1980s led to the restoration of independence on 20 August 1991, based on legal continuity with the pre-war republic. [[e:estonia|Estonia]] joined the EU and [[e:nato|NATO]] in 2004 and the eurozone in 2011, and became known for its e-government and technology sector.

roman-republic.t: The Roman state from the expulsion of the kings to Augustus, which grew from a city in Latium to master of the Mediterranean before collapsing in civil war.
roman-republic.o: Tradition dates the Republic to 509 BCE, when Roman aristocrats expelled [[e:tarquinius-superbus|Tarquinius Superbus]] and replaced the king with two consuls elected each year. The early Republic was a small city-state in [[e:latium|Latium]], at war with its neighbours and divided internally between patricians and plebeians.
roman-republic.r: Power was shared between annual magistrates, the Senate of former officials and the citizen assemblies, with tribunes protecting plebeians. The [[e:twelve-tables|Twelve Tables]] of 451–450 BCE codified law. [[e:rome|Rome]] conquered [[e:italy|Italy]] by 270 BCE through alliances and colonies, defeated [[e:carthage|Carthage]] in the [[e:punic-wars|Punic Wars]], and took [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]], [[e:greece|Greece]], [[e:spain|Spain]] and [[e:africa|Africa]]. Conquest brought slaves, wealth and an army of professional soldiers loyal to their generals, while Greek culture transformed Roman literature and art.
roman-republic.e: From the [[e:gracchi|Gracchi]] in 133 BCE, political violence grew: [[e:gaius-marius|Marius]], [[e:sulla|Sulla]], [[e:pompey|Pompey]] and [[e:julius-caesar|Julius Caesar]] fought civil wars, and Caesar became dictator for life before his murder in 44 BCE. After Octavian defeated [[e:mark-antony|Antony]] at [[e:battle-of-actium|Actium]] in 31 BCE he received the name Augustus in 27 BCE, beginning the [[s:roman-empire|Roman Empire]].

republic-of-saint-titus.t: Rebel republic proclaimed by Venetian colonists in Crete in 1363, which briefly united Latin and Greek Cretans against Venice.
republic-of-saint-titus.o: In 1363 [[e:venice|Venice]] demanded a new tax from the feudal settlers of [[s:venetian-crete|Venetian Crete]] to pay for repairs to the harbour of [[e:heraklion|Candia]]. The colonists, already resentful at being excluded from power in Venice, rebelled under leaders including [[e:marco-gradenigo|Marco Gradenigo]] and [[e:tito-venier|Tito Venier]], imprisoned the Venetian duke and proclaimed independence under [[e:titus-saint|Saint Titus]], patron of [[e:crete|Crete]].
republic-of-saint-titus.r: The rebels formed a government in [[e:heraklion|Candia]] led by a governor and councillors. To win Greek support they made concessions to the [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] church and drew in Greek nobles such as the [[e:kallergis-family|Kallergis family]]. Their republic lacked outside allies: the pope and other powers backed [[e:venice|Venice]].
republic-of-saint-titus.e: [[e:venice|Venice]] sent a [[e:mercenary|mercenary]] army under [[e:luchino-dal-verme|Luchino dal Verme]], which retook [[e:heraklion|Candia]] in May 1364. Leaders were executed and [[e:mark-the-evangelist|Saint Mark's]] banner restored, though Greek rebels led by the [[e:kallergis-family|Kallergis]] brothers fought on until 1367.

roman-britain.t: The Roman province of Britannia, ruled from 43 until about 410, which brought towns, roads, villas, Latin and Christianity to most of what is now England and Wales.
roman-britain.o: [[e:julius-caesar|Julius Caesar]] raided [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in 55 and 54 BCE, but conquest began only in 43, when [[e:claudius|Claudius]] sent [[e:aulus-plautius|Aulus Plautius]] with four legions. [[e:camulodunum|Camulodunum]] fell, and over the next forty years the army pushed west and north, overcoming the revolt of [[e:boudica|Boudica]] in 60 or 61 and reaching the far north under [[e:gnaeus-julius-agricola|Agricola]], who defeated the [[s:caledonii|Caledonians]] at [[e:battle-of-mons-graupius|Mons Graupius]] in 83 or 84.
roman-britain.r: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] was governed by a senatorial legate commanding four legions at first and three from the late 1st century, based at [[e:caerleon|Caerleon]], [[e:chester|Chester]] and [[e:york|York]]. [[e:hadrians-wall|Hadrian's Wall]], begun in 122, and briefly the [[e:antonine-wall|Antonine Wall]] marked the northern frontier. Under [[e:septimius-severus|Severus]] or [[e:caracalla|Caracalla]] the province was divided in two, and later four provinces formed a diocese. Towns such as [[e:londinium|Londinium]], the main city, grew with fora and baths; villas, wool, grain, lead and [[e:tin|tin]] sustained the economy. [[e:christianity|Christianity]] spread from the 3rd century.
roman-britain.e: From the late 3rd century [[e:saxons|Saxon]], Pictish and Irish raids increased, and usurpers such as [[e:carausius|Carausius]] and [[e:constantine-iii-western-roman-emperor|Constantine III]] drew troops away. By about 410, when [[e:honorius|Honorius]] reportedly told the cities to look to their own defence, Roman rule had ended. Successor kingdoms such as the [[s:kingdom-of-powys|Kingdom of Powys]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-dumnonia|Kingdom of Dumnonia]] arose from its remains.

raigarh-state.t: A Gond-ruled state of eastern Chhattisgarh whose music-loving ruler made it a centre of Kathak dance.
raigarh-state.o: Raigarh was ruled by a [[e:raj-gond|Raj Gond]] dynasty whose traditions say they came from [[e:chandrapur|Chanda]] (Chandrapur). The register dates the state to around 1625. It was later a dependency of the [[s:nagpur-kingdom|Bhonsles of Nagpur]] before passing under British paramountcy.
raigarh-state.r: The Rajas ruled a territory of [[e:rice|rice]] fields and forests along the Mand river. Raja [[e:chakradhar-singh|Chakradhar Singh]], who reigned from 1924, gathered leading musicians and dancers at his court and wrote treatises on dance, giving rise to the Raigarh gharana of Kathak.
raigarh-state.e: Raigarh merged into the [[e:central-provinces|Central Provinces and Berar]] in 1948, later [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]]. Since 2000 it has been in [[e:chhattisgarh|Chhattisgarh]], where the annual Chakradhar Samaroh festival of music recalls its court.

rajkot-state.t: A Jadeja Rajput state of Kathiawar whose capital hosted the British agency for the peninsula and where Gandhi spent his boyhood.
rajkot-state.o: Rajkot was founded in 1620 by [[e:vibhaji-ajoji|Vibhaji Ajoji]], a grandson of [[e:jam-sataji|Jam Sataji of Nawanagar]], who received the area as his share. The town was later briefly held by Mughal officers, but the [[e:jadeja|Jadeja]] line recovered it.
rajkot-state.r: The Thakore Sahibs ruled a small territory, but Rajkot became important as the seat of the British agency for [[e:kathiawar|Kathiawar]] and of [[e:rajkumar-college-rajkot|Rajkumar College]] for princes. [[e:karamchand-gandhi|Karamchand Gandhi]], father of [[e:mahatma-gandhi|Mohandas Gandhi]], served as its [[e:diwan|diwan]]. [[e:lakhajirajsinhji-ii|Lakhajirajsinhji II]] introduced a representative assembly, while the 1939 Rajkot satyagraha challenged his successor.
rajkot-state.e: Rajkot merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and served as that state's capital until 1956. It became part of [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]] and then [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960, and is now one of Gujarat's largest cities.
